context.topic: current harness-ledger priorities and audio acceptance criteria
context.text:
SHIPPED AND HARDWARE-VERIFIED. 24 kHz superwideband runs end to end today; treat it as a constraint you build on, not an open question.

Downlink: the model's own 24 kHz PCM goes straight to Opus with NO resampling anywhere. 12 kHz of delivered bandwidth. 9 kHz sibilance arrives at -22.6 dB where it was previously folded onto 7 kHz.

Framing, not sample rate, was the thing that failed before. The earlier 24 kHz attempt used 20 ms frames = 50 packets/s against a chip that can start about 48.8 decodes/s. At 60 ms frames it is 16.7/s and fits. A second cause was that libopus had been compiling -Os the whole time: target_compile_options put -O3 before Zephyr's flags so the command line read "-O3 -Os" and the last -O won. Applied as a source property it wins; text 255K -> 316K, encode 20.4 -> 16.4 ms.

Costs are MEASURED on-device with a 32.768 kHz counter around each call, not estimated: decode 8.8 ms/packet at 16 kHz, 25.2 ms at 24 kHz, encode 15.0 ms/call. That is about 87% of one 64 MHz core, which is why the uplink encoder runs at complexity 0 — uplink audio only has to be understood by speech-to-text, while the decoded downlink is what the owner actually hears. mic_drops went 29 -> 7 of 931.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA, all of them numbers you can re-measure rather than judgements:
- Alias rejection on any resampling stage >= 60 dB. The 16 kHz path's 2-tap average gave 3.2 dB; the polyphase windowed-sinc FIR that replaced it gives 67.5 dB. Measure with scripts/audio-quality-probe.mjs.
- Codec cost under 100% of one 64 MHz core, with the measurement taken on-device.
- mic_drops under about 1% of blocks.
- tx_starved at or near zero. Last hardware run: "agent 24 kHz down", 284 packets decoded, tx_starved 3.
- No audible content before the agent speaks. The sync preamble used to be played as audio — 4 bursts of 16 samples at 0x6C6C (~85% of full scale) 20 ms apart, i.e. loud clicks at the start of every conversation. Post-fix the same press-moment capture is peak 0, 0 nonzero samples of 22050.

Do not propose work premised on 24 kHz being unavailable, on the SoC being too slow for it, or on needing a resampler in the downlink path. If you want to change the audio path, the bar is a measurement from scripts/audio-quality-probe.mjs or an on-device counter, not an argument.

context.topic: authoritative routine timezone and quiet-hours policy
context.text:
America/New_York. That is this Mac's system zone, read from /etc/localtime, currently EDT (UTC-4).

Scope this correctly, because it is the part that has been getting confused: it is authoritative for anything RESOLVED ON THIS MAC — routine firing times, quiet hours, "this morning", file timestamps, calendar reads. It is not a claim about where the owner is standing. The pendant has never been given a zone: NITZ was never captured, no GNSS receiver is started (CONFIG_LOCATION and CONFIG_GNSS are unset and nrf_modem_gnss appears zero times in the firmware), and the device clock arrives as zoneless digits. Code that parses those digits must return a null instant rather than borrowing this zone — catchupSources.js and voiceNotes.js both already refuse it, and that refusal is correct.

If you need the owner's own timezone as distinct from the machine's, that is still an open question for the owner and you should say so rather than substituting this value for it.

context.topic: current cross-surface job and event persistence primitives
context.text:
Answer from reading the source. Short version: ONE of the primitives you asked about really exists and works; the rest are either schema-with-no-implementation or in-memory-only. Do not build a new Intent Thread from scratch, and do not assume the existing "cross-surface" modules do what their header comments say.

=== 1. Shared request/correlation IDs: NO. There are five unrelated ID namespaces.

  relay job id     job_<uuid>       cloud-relay/jobs.js:3 createJobId()
  Mac job id       local_<uuid>     local-agent/jobTracker.js:45 recordJobStart()
  browser job id   browser_<uuid>   local-agent/browserBridge.js:316
  Mac action id    act_<sha1[0:12]> local-agent/actionReceipts.js:150 actionIdFor()
  browser cmd id   idem:<x>|cmd:<x> browser-extension/src/bridge-core.js:300 commandIdentity()

No relay job id is ever derived from or stored alongside a Mac job id. The ONLY place they meet is a telemetry field, localJobId, written into a pipeline event meta blob at local-agent/bridge.js:333 and :509. It is not a foreign key, not indexed, not queryable. If you need cross-surface joins today they do not exist.

The one genuine content-addressed idempotency key is actionIdFor() above: sha1 over {type, params}. executionJournal.js:227 surfaces it as idempotencyKey and repeatedActions() (executionJournal.js:307) makes "has this exact step already run" answerable. It is Mac-local and never crosses to the relay.

=== 2. The one primitive that DOES cross both ways: shared/contextHandoff.js

This is the module to build on. It is the only shared/ module imported by BOTH cloud-relay and local-agent and actually exercised in production paths.

  relay packs:   cloud-relay/server.js:233 and :647 -> store.saveContext(record)
  handle rides on the job as contextHandle (cloud-relay/jobs.js:55,65), deliberately
    stripped from publicJob (jobs.js:145-151), handed only to the bridge (server.js:2708)
  Mac resumes:   local-agent/bridge.js:307 -> local-agent/server.js:382 ->
    local-agent/orchestrator.js:197 -> resumeContext() local-agent/contextResume.js:33
    -> POST /v1/context/resume (cloud-relay/server.js:677)

  handle format: pcx_<base64url 12B>.<base64url 32B>, HANDLE_PATTERN contextHandoff.js:78
  only the SHA-256 of the secret is stored (secretHash); verifyContextHandle uses
    crypto.timingSafeEqual
  record fields: version, handleId, secretHash, origin, model, sessionId, jobId,
    createdAt, expiresAt, items[], shed[], redaction, bytes
  storage: D1 relay_contexts (cloudflare-worker/context-handoff-migration.sql:17, also
    schema.sql:227), PK handle_id, index relay_contexts_expiry
  CONTEXT_TTL_MS contextHandoff.js:54 = CONTEXT_HANDOFF_TTL_MS env || 2h
  MAX_CONTEXT_BYTES contextHandoff.js:67 = 256KB; KEEP_TEXT_CHARS :73 = 400
  RESUME_TIMEOUT_MS contextResume.js:19 = CONTEXT_RESUME_TIMEOUT_MS || 2500ms
  every failure returns {resumed:false} with a reason string (no_handle,
    relay_status_N, relay_unreachable, missing_or_expired, empty_context) and plans
    cold. Nothing in contextResume.js can fail a job.

Closest thing to a cross-body correlation id that exists: buildResumeMessages() returns
cacheKey = ctx_<handleId> (contextHandoff.js:517). But that is a provider prompt-cache
key, not a store key.

=== 3. shared/fleetMemory.js — 893 lines, two store implementations, two mounted HTTP routes, and ZERO WRITERS.

Its own header says "every body appends typed events." grep disagrees. It is imported ONLY by cloud-relay/fleetContext.js:24, cloud-relay/store/memoryStore.js:6, cloud-relay/store/d1Store.js:7. Zero imports in local-agent/, browser-extension/, src/ (iOS).

The routes are real and mounted: registerFleetMemoryRoutes (fleetContext.js:834) is called at cloud-relay/server.js:2326, serving POST /v1/memory/events (scope memory:write) and GET /v1/memory/projection (scope memory:read), FLEET_MEMORY_SCOPES at fleetContext.js:816. Nothing anywhere calls either route.

So the read path (loadFleetFromStore -> projectFleetMemoryFromStore, fleetContext.js:726 and :774) reads a table nobody writes, and the memory the voice agent actually gets is carried ENTIRELY by inheritedText — the pre-rendered blob the Mac PUTs to /v1/state/fleet as memory.text (local-agent/bridge.js:693,698; buildFleetPayloadFromLocal at fleetContext.js:603; clipped to MAX_MEMORY_TEXT_CHARS = 2000 at fleetContext.js:39). That one-way pre-rendered pipe from a single node is precisely what fleetMemory.js:5-15 says it exists to replace. The comment at fleetMemory.js:453 predicting that branch will go dead is currently exactly backwards.

Also: relay_memory_events exists only in cloudflare-worker/fleet-memory-migration.sql, NOT in cloudflare-worker/schema.sql. A DB provisioned from schema.sql has no such table, and fleetContext.js:854-862 has a bespoke handler turning that into a 503.

Its schema is good and I would reuse it rather than invent one: normalizeMemoryEvent (fleetMemory.js:133) -> version, eventId (fme_<uuid>), type (MEMORY_EVENT_TYPES = preference|task|entity|event), key, value, retracted, node, surfaces[] (MEMORY_SURFACES = voice|mac|browser|ios), confidence, sensitivity, at, expiresAt, bytes, optional clipped. MEMORY_TTL_MS :83 = {preference:null, task:14d, entity:30d, event:6h}. MAX_EVENT_BYTES :105 = 1024. MAX_LOG_BYTES :108 = 128KB. DEFAULT_PROJECTION_BYTES :120 = 800, MAX_PROJECTION_BYTES :121 = 2000.

=== 4. shared/approvalHandoff.js — APPROVAL_STORE_CONTRACT is documentation, not code.

APPROVAL_STORE_CONTRACT (approvalHandoff.js:965) declares reads/writes against getState(approvalStateKey(id)) / saveState(approvalIndexKey(deviceId), index). Nothing in cloud-relay/ or cloudflare-worker/ reads or writes those keys. indexApproval() and MAX_INDEXED_APPROVALS (:988 = 20) have no caller at all.

The only wiring is Mac-local: registerPrepareApproveRoutes (local-agent/prepareApprove.js:469) mounts POST /prepare, GET /prepare/:ledgerId/world, POST /approve on the Mac agent. prepareAction (prepareApprove.js:102) returns relay:{stateKey,indexKey,contract} with the comment "This module does not talk to the relay; the bridge does" (:137). The bridge does not.

Consequence for your proposals: the manifest is durable (.pendant-action-ledger.json), the approval DECISION is durable nowhere, and the stated invariant "relay holds the decision, Mac holds the plan" (approvalHandoff.js:962-963) is not enforced by any code.

TTLs that exist but govern nothing yet: APPROVAL_DEFAULT_TTL_MS :67 = 30min, APPROVAL_MIN_TTL_MS :68 = 60s, APPROVAL_MAX_TTL_MS :69 = 2h, READBACK_MAX_CHARS :292 = 700.

=== 5. shared/capabilityRegistry.js persists NOTHING and is Mac-only.

createCapabilityRegistry() (capabilityRegistry.js:435) returns four in-RAM Maps. No file I/O, no store. Imported only by local-agent/goalRouter.js:78 and local-agent/goalRouterSurfaces.js:50; zero relay imports. buildGoalRoutingContext (goalRouterSurfaces.js:159) rebuilds the whole registry per call, including a registerSurface(...{surface:'relay'}) where the Mac describes the relay to itself rather than the relay publishing. toCapabilityRegistrySnapshot / mergeCapabilityRegistrySnapshot (:1307, :1330) define a cross-body wire format exercised only in capabilityRegistry.test.js. shared/capabilityRegistryExpress.js (196 lines) has ZERO production importers.

=== 6. Durable storage: real on the Mac, conditional on the relay.

Mac root = workspacePath = PENDANT_WORKSPACE_PATH || ~/AI-Pendant-Workspace (local-agent/config.js:30).
local-agent/atomicJsonStore.js is the real primitive: writeRawAtomic (:160) does openSync(wx,0o600) -> writeFileSync -> fsyncSync -> renameSync -> chmodSync -> syncDirectory, keeps a .bak sibling, and recovers from .bak or orphaned .tmp.<pid>.<uuid>.
Files: pendant-jobs.json (jobTracker.js:9), pendant-pipeline.json (pipelineTrace.js:9), pendant-thinking.json, mac-agent-activity-log.json (config.js:48), pendant-sessions.json (sessionStore.js:21), .pendant-browser-spool.json (browserSpool.js:28), .pendant-action-ledger.json (actionLedger.js:100, override PENDANT_ACTION_LEDGER_PATH).
Known gap: local-agent/sessionStore.js does NOT use atomicJsonStore.js — it reimplements the atomic write inline (writeSessionDocumentAtomic :247) and writes NO .bak, so a torn pendant-sessions.json falls to emptyDocument() (:38) with no recovery. durableState.test.js covers only four stores (:33-38); sessionStore, browserSpool and actionLedger are not among them.

Relay: getStore() (cloud-relay/store/index.js:7) returns createD1Store(bindings.DB) only when getCloudflareBindings()?.DB exists, else createMemoryStore(). And cloud-relay/store/memoryStore.js declares its Maps at MODULE scope (:19-29), not inside the factory — two createMemoryStore() calls share one state and all of it dies with the process, while the file describes itself as "same contract as d1Store" (:371-375). Anything you design that assumes relay durability must check which store is live.

=== 7. Reconnect semantics: THERE IS NO JOB LEASE. This is the biggest hole.

claimNextJob (d1Store.js:753, memoryStore.js:224) does a compare-and-set UPDATE ... SET status='processing' WHERE job_id=?1 AND status='queued', stamping claimedBy/claimedAt. There is no lease_until column, no expiry, no requeue sweep; cloudflare-worker/schema.sql:31 (relay_jobs) has no lease columns. If the Mac dies mid-job the row sits at 'processing' invisibly until JOB_TTL_MS (cloud-relay/config.js:18 = 24h) prunes it.

Leases exist for exactly one thing: routines. lease_owner/lease_until on relay_routines, claimDueRoutines({leaseMs = 300_000}) at d1Store.js:887 / memoryStore.js:297. Jobs never got the same treatment.
Other real leases: COMMAND_LEASE_MS = 45s (browserBridge.js:11) with genuine orphan detection at :575-597; AGENT_PROXY_MAX_AGE_MS = 10s (memoryStore.js:30) which fails rather than requeues.
cloud-relay/polling.js is 17 lines and is not resume logic: bridgeClaimDelay() explicitly ignores its own emptyClaimCount (void emptyClaimCount, :15). It is a CPU yield.
Bridge-side reconnect is only backoff: createRetryBackoff (retryPolicy.js:1) baseMs 250, maximumMs 30_000, jitterRatio 0.2, wired at bridge.js:127.

=== What this means for your proposal

Narrow it. Do not specify a new checkpoint schema — three already exist (contextHandoff record, fleetMemory event, approvalHandoff manifest) and the problem is not schema, it is that two of the three have no writer and no lease.

The highest-value foundational changes the code actually points at, in order:
1. Add lease_until + a requeue sweep to relay_jobs. Nothing recovers an orphaned in-flight job today. The routine lease at d1Store.js:887 is the working template.
2. Give fleetMemory a writer. The store, the schema, the eviction ladder, the byte budgets and both HTTP routes are already built and tested; what is missing is one call from the Mac bridge (and later the extension) to POST /v1/memory/events. That is a much smaller change than an Intent Thread and it deletes the pre-rendered memory.text pipe.
3. Implement APPROVAL_STORE_CONTRACT on the relay, or delete it. Right now an approval is a Mac-local flag with three unused TTL constants next to it.
4. Persist a relay-job-id <-> Mac-job-id mapping. It exists today only as telemetry meta.

Anything you propose about "policy/UI on top of existing infrastructure" should assume: context handoff works, memory does not cross, approvals do not cross, capabilities do not cross, and orphaned jobs are never recovered.

Signal inventory, read from local-agent/ directly. Read the three "does not exist" items first, because they invalidate the most likely shape of your interruption gate.

=== THINGS THAT DO NOT EXIST AT ALL

1. THERE IS NO macOS FOCUS / DO NOT DISTURB SIGNAL ANYWHERE.
   Repo-wide grep for do-not-disturb / donotdisturb / \bdnd\b / Assertions.json /
   focusmodes / ModeConfigurations / doNotDisturb across *.js, *.swift, *.md returns
   ZERO matches. Nothing reads ~/Library/DoNotDisturb/DB/Assertions.json, no
   com.apple.donotdisturb defaults read, no NSUserNotificationCenter check.
   "Focus" in this codebase means two unrelated things and neither is a macOS Focus mode:
     - window FOREGROUND focus: focusPolicy.js, focusCoordinator.js
     - a Pomodoro timer: focusSession.js
   If your gate needs to know the owner is in a Focus mode, that adapter does not exist
   and must be listed as new work, not assumed.

2. NO NOTIFICATION CENTER DATABASE IS EVER READ. There is no OS notification feed.
   notificationTriage.js:6-10 documents the decision not to: the Notification Center db
   sits behind Full Disk Access and holds banners that have already been dismissed.
   What this codebase calls "notifications" is a SYNTHETIC triage over mail + calendar +
   reminders. It is not the OS notification stream.

3. FULL DISK ACCESS IS NEVER PROBED. The string fullDisk appears once, as a Settings-pane
   URL at macos/permissions.js:22, reachable only via openPrivacySettings() which opens
   all six panes blindly. Nothing checks whether FDA is granted.

=== WHAT ACTUALLY EXISTS, BY SOURCE

--- CALENDAR + REMINDERS (the only real calendar signal) — appleData.js
Exports runJxa, listEvents, listOpenReminders, createRecurringAlarm, deleteEventByUid,
listRecentMail, firstOccurrence, RRULE_DAY_CODES.
Mechanism: real, not a stub. JXA over `osascript -l JavaScript` spawned with spawn()
(appleData.js:30-68). EK_PREAMBLE (:76-95) does ObjC.import('EventKit'),
$.EKEventStore.alloc.init, then requestFullAccessToEventsWithCompletion /
requestFullAccessToRemindersWithCompletion. listEvents uses
predicateForEventsWithStartDateEndDateCalendars + eventsMatchingPredicate (:106-140).
listOpenReminders uses predicateForIncompleteRemindersWithDueDateStartingEndingCalendars
+ fetchRemindersMatchingPredicateCompletion with a manual runloop pump (:147-174).
Writes deliberately go through Calendar.app AppleScript instead (:206-223, :236-252).

*** THE PERMISSION DEFECT THAT MOST AFFECTS YOUR GATE ***
appleData.js:70-75 states: EventKit's authorization callback never completes under
osascript — there is no app run loop to deliver it on. Consequence, documented at
briefingTriage.js:914-934: AN UNAUTHORISED READ DOES NOT THROW, IT RETURNS []. Measured
in-repo: listEvents over a 7-day window returned 0 and listOpenReminders returned 0 from
a process with no grant, on a day with four real events.
Two callers corroborate that, two do not:
  briefingTriage.gatherTriageFindings  CORROBORATES (briefingTriage.js:936-941 treats
                                       both-empty as unreadable)
  meetingPrep.readUpcomingEvents       CORROBORATES (meetingPrep.js:174-207, returns
                                       calendarReadable:false)
  notificationTriage.triageNotifications  DOES NOT. Empty -> speak() returns
                                       'Nothing waiting for you.' (notificationTriage.js:226)
  dayPlan.buildDayPlan                 DOES NOT. Empty -> formatBriefing returns
                                       'Your calendar is clear and nothing is overdue.'
                                       (dayPlan.js:81)
So GET /notifications and GET /day-plan will CONFIDENTLY REPORT ALL-CLEAR on a Mac with no
Calendars grant. If your gate consumes either route, it will suppress correctly-urgent
items and believe it saw a quiet calendar. Use the briefingTriage/meetingPrep
corroboration pattern, or fix those two, before trusting emptiness.

TCC probe mismatch: AUTOMATION_TARGETS (macos/permissions.js:30-126) probes Calendar and
Reminders with AppleScript AUTOMATION probes (tell application "Calendar" to get name of
first calendar). That is a DIFFERENT TCC grant from the EventKit Calendars/Reminders grant
appleData.js depends on. A green automation.Calendar.granted proves nothing about
listEvents. Do not use the permission report as evidence the calendar is readable.

Numbers: JXA_TIMEOUT_MS=20_000 (appleData.js:27); EventKit auth poll deadline now+1500
(:84); reminders fetch deadline now+8000 (:152); attendee cap 30 (:131);
createRecurringAlarm/deleteEventByUid osascript timeout 30_000 (:222,:250);
listRecentMail timeout 60_000 (:289), default limit 40 (:260).
DEAD: deleteEventByUid (:235) — one occurrence in the repo, its own definition.

--- MAIL — two independent AppleScript readers
appleData.listRecentMail (:260-302): plain AppleScript tell application "Mail", per-message
subject/sender/date received/read status. Needs Automation -> Mail. Denial THROWS
(osascript non-zero) and is caught by settle() (notificationTriage.js:240-246). Only
consumer: notificationTriage.js.
mailTriage.readUnreadEnvelopes (mailTriage.js:354-419): the real reader. Batched
AppleScript — `set subs to subject of messages 1 thru total`, one Apple event per column,
ASCII 31/30 separators. Bodies via readMessageBodies (:461) with subject re-verification.
Structural refusal: assertScriptNeverSends (:313-325) throws on any script matching
/\bsend\b/i, called inside runOsascript (:325-333).
Wired: POST /mail/triage (server.js:1918), GET /mail/triage (:1939),
GET /mail/triage/:runId (:1947); action type triage_inbox (computerControl.js:285 ->
mailTriageAction :512); also consumed by briefingTriage.
Numbers: DEFAULT_SCAN_LIMIT=200 (:59), DEFAULT_SINCE_HOURS=72 (:60), MAX_SCAN_LIMIT=600
(:61), OSASCRIPT_TIMEOUT_MS=120_000 (:63), MAX_BODY_CHARS=4000 (:66),
DEFAULT_MAX_DRAFTS=8 (:67), MAX_STORED_RUNS=30 (:68).

--- NOTIFICATION TRIAGE — notificationTriage.js
Exports scoreMail, scoreEvent, scoreReminder, triageNotifications, TRIAGE_THRESHOLD.
Composes the three readers above (injectable, defaults real). Scoring is pure regex plus
arithmetic. Wired: GET /notifications (server.js:1971-1993), action type
triage_notifications (computerControl.js:287 -> triageAction :534). scoreMail reused by
mailTriage.js:15.
Numbers: IMPORTANCE_THRESHOLD=4 (:37), IMMINENT_MEETING_MINUTES=60 (:39), mailLimit
default 60 (:149). Weights: bulk sender -4 (:52), marketing subject -3 (:56), deadline
subject +4 (:60), question +2 (:64), known person +3 (:71), Re: +1 (:80), <=4h old +1
(:88), >72h old -2 (:92); event imminent/in-progress +5 (:106,:109), attendees>1 +1
(:114); reminder past-due +4 (:128), due<6h +4 (:132), priority 1-4 +2 (:137). Spoken cap
slice(0,4) (:229).
DEAD: TRIAGE_THRESHOLD (:248) has one occurrence in the repo — its own definition. It is
not the threshold in use; IMPORTANCE_THRESHOLD is.

--- focusPolicy.js — the ONLY presence signal, and it is not Focus modes
Exports idleSeconds, ownerIsPresent, shouldTakeFocus, openArgs, focusPolicy.
Mechanism: execFile('/bin/sh', ['-c', "ioreg -c IOHIDSystem | awk '/HIDIdleTime/ {print
$NF; exit}'"]) (focusPolicy.js:27-30), nanoseconds -> seconds. NO PERMISSION REQUIRED
(documented at :22-24). Failure -> null -> ownerIsPresent() returns true, fail-safe toward
not stealing focus (:43).
This is the single best real signal for "is the owner at the machine" and it is cheap and
ungated. It has NO HTTP ROUTE — idleSeconds/ownerIsPresent/shouldTakeFocus are exported
but used only internally in the openArgs chain. Exposing it is a small, concrete adapter.
Numbers: POLICY=PENDANT_FOCUS_POLICY||'auto' (:15),
PRESENT_IDLE_SECONDS=PENDANT_PRESENT_IDLE_SECONDS||60 (:18).

--- focusCoordinator.js — foreground drift detection, not interruption policy
Exports FOCUS_BATCH_SIZE, classifyFocus, inferTargetApp, planFocus, routeByTargetApp,
fingerprintHost, detectDrift, runFocusSafePlan.
Mechanism: execFile('lsappinfo', ['info','-only','name,bundleID,pid', app],
{timeout:4000}) (:211-215) plus readForegroundApp from executionJournal.js. Optional AX
window fingerprint via injected uiSnapshot, which DEFAULTS TO null — fingerprintWindows
then returns {probed:false, detail:'Not probed...'} (:228-236). It honestly reports
not-probed rather than faking. Restore uses open -b <bundleId> (:415).
lsappinfo needs no permission; the AX path needs Accessibility.
Wired: runFocusSafePlan -> orchestrator.js, actionLedger.js, visionLoop.js;
classifyFocus/fingerprintHost -> visionLoopPolicy.js; planFocus/routeByTargetApp ->
visionLoop.js. NO DIRECT HTTP ROUTE — reachable only through POST /execute.
Numbers: FOCUS_BATCH_SIZE=PENDANT_FOCUS_BATCH_SIZE||4 (:35-38), lsappinfo timeout 4000
(:213), uiSnapshot max 40 (:238), digest slice(0,12) (:245), open -b timeout 8000 (:415).
Unused exports: FOCUS_BATCH_SIZE, inferTargetApp, detectDrift.

--- focusSession.js — a Pomodoro timer. NOT macOS Focus. Do not build on it as one.
Exports focusStoreLocation, activeFocusSession, startFocusSession, endFocusSession,
resumeFocusSessions, focusStatus, describeBlocked, FOCUS_DEFAULT_DISTRACTIONS.
"Block distractions" is implemented as: osascript System Events to enumerate non-background
processes (:282-286), then one batched script setting `visible of process appName to false`
(:332-353) — i.e. CMD-H HIDING — plus setOutputMuted(true) (:245). The end alarm is
`say -r 180` plus `display notification ... sound name "Glass"` (:366-374). State at
PENDANT_FOCUS_STORE_PATH || <workspace>/.pendant-focus.json (:37-38). Failures are caught
into blocked.failures (:236,:250) rather than thrown.
Wired: POST /focus (server.js:1862), GET /focus (:1870), DELETE /focus (:1874); actions
start_focus_session/end_focus_session (computerControl.js:279-281 -> :466,:476);
resumeFocusSessions() called on boot at server.js:2233.
Numbers: DEFAULT_DISTRACTIONS is 12 hardcoded app names (:42-55), MAX_MINUTES=8*60 (:57),

Signals you may claim exist and are reachable: mail (two readers, one batched and good),

=== 1. THE SENSITIVITY TAXONOMY: exactly three strings, one classifier, and it is NOT an access gate

local-agent/redaction.js:68-74, classifySensitivity(value) returns exactly:
   'secret'     — matched SECRET_PATTERNS
   'sensitive'  — matched PERSONAL_PATTERNS
   'normal'     — neither
There is no fourth class. No numeric level. No per-surface variant. Fifteen modules import
it, and several say in comments that a second pattern list is forbidden
(evidenceCapsules.js:262; browserProvenance.js:399-401 "there is one classifier and one
masker in this codebase and this is not a third").

Callers: memoryService.js:141 -> fact.sensitivity; quickCapture.js:95,107;
evidenceCapsules.js:284; voiceNotes.js:614; formPreview.js:167;
browserProvenance.js:433; visionLoopRelay.js:82; actionLedger.js:215;
shared/fleetMemory.js:192; shared/approvalHandoff.js:441;
shared/contextHandoff.js:290,297.

CRITICAL for your design: sensitivity is EXPLICITLY NOT an access gate. Stated three times
(redaction.js:62-66, memoryService.js:31-32, evidenceCapsules.js:268-270). It only selects
what may be pasted into a THIRD-PARTY PROMPT. The owner reads everything at full fidelity
through the API. If your epistemic-claim layer treats 'sensitive' as an authorization
level, you will be the first thing in this codebase to do so and you must say so
explicitly rather than inheriting a meaning that is not there.

Adjacent, smaller taxonomies, so you do not invent a fourth:
  evidenceCapsules.js:315 classification — same three strings rolled up per capture;
    per-span class is 'secret'|'sensitive' with action 'withheld'|'flagged' (:288-303)
  browserProvenance.isSecretLocator (:382) -> browserBridge.redactAction, whose only
    pattern is SECRET_SELECTOR = /pass|pwd|otp|totp|mfa|cvv|cvc|csc|card|secret|token|pin\b/i
  evidenceCapsules.capsuleState() (:526-533) — 'revoked'|'retired'|'expired'|'live'|
    'unknown'. Lifecycle, not sensitivity.

WHAT THE TAXONOMY DOES NOT HAVE: no medical, financial, legal, health, or third-party-person
class. No per-recipient policy — a fact classed 'normal' goes to every model provider
identically. No notion of WHO ELSE appears in a fact; a 'normal' fact naming another person
is treated exactly like a battery level.

=== 7. THE HONEST ANSWER TO WHAT YOU ASKED

Your request asks for "an explicit owner-safe retention boundary." THERE IS NO SUCH
BOUNDARY AND NO DECISION HAS BEEN MADE. What exists is:
  - a mechanism: three sensitivity classes, one classifier, one masker (with a known bug),
    per-store TTL constants, and content-addressed capsules with revocation tombstones;
  - one enforcement point that works (briefingTriage.redactForDelivery);
  - one cascade that works (voice note -> its audio);
  - and no policy tying any of it together.
The three specific questions you asked have these answers TODAY:
  "may normalized claims persist?"  — nothing stops them; facts have TTLs by kind,
     capsules have a 24h body TTL plus a 7d retire grace, browserProvenance has NO TTL,
     and the context graph has no TTL and is 92% telemetry.
  "which sensitivity classes may be spoken?" — undecided. The only rule in code is that a
     'secret' capture and a 'secret' voice note get a non-revealing confirmation line. The
     audio modules themselves have no gate.
  "how does deletion propagate to Mac/browser sources?" — it does not, with one exception
     (voice note -> audio). Revoking a capsule does not touch derived facts; deleting a
     capture does not touch the graph copy; there is no cross-store forget.

Your stated fallback — short-TTL derived metadata only, never persist raw quotes or
secrets, explicit confirmation before a claim influences an external action — is a sound
DEFAULT and I am not overriding it. Keep it as a default and surface it as an owner
decision. But two of its three parts are already contradicted by the code you would be
building on: raw quotes ARE persisted (capsule content up to 20,000 chars, and the
context graph holds full capture text with no TTL), and a short TTL on your claims will
not remove the copies that already exist in facts.json and context_graph.json unless you
also build the cascade that does not exist.
Concrete recommendation: add a capsuleId (or equivalent provenance link) to the fact record
in memoryService.js:131-149 before doing anything else. Without it, no revocation you
design can ever reach a derived claim.

tools.name: reconcile_personal_state
tools.why: The owner’s system currently has conflicting timezone/permission reports and duplicate scheduled audio. Judgement needs a read-only, provenance-backed reconciliation before promising calendar/mail access or issuing briefings; existing status endpoints expose raw surfaces but no unified conflict detector.

tools.name: pendant_diagnostics_and_bug_draft
tools.why: The owner explicitly has the idea of a pendant that files its own bug reports from the UART log. Existing production tools cover Mac/browser/research/status but do not expose a safe, structured UART-log parser or issue-draft workflow. This is useful even before automatic filing: detect anomalies, correlate link/audio metrics, and produce a reviewable draft without sending externally.

since.description: ISO timestamp, duration (for example 'last 30m'), or log cursor from which to inspect UART/diagnostic records

include_audio_metrics.description: Include packet loss, queue depth, underruns, sample-rate transitions, and latency evidence

draft_target.description: Where to prepare a reviewable draft; never send or submit

tools.name: cross_surface_preflight
tools.why: To fulfill the proposed truthful routing behavior, I need one cheap authoritative call that reports which surfaces can currently read, draft, or execute for a given job, rather than repeatedly invoking unavailable tools or claiming success.

tools.name: audio_brief_item_action
tools.why: The two proposed capabilities need a durable, source-linked way to pause the pendant brief, bind the owner's utterance to the current item, and enqueue a reminder/note/draft without losing playback position. Existing tools expose generic Mac/browser actions but not the semantic audio cursor or idempotent item action.

tools.name: explain_action_provenance
tools.why: The owner needs an immediate, trustworthy answer to ‘why did you suggest/do this?’ and the ability to revoke a source. Existing receipts are completion records, not a verified chain from evidence through judgement to effect.

action_or_item_id.description: Receipt, job, briefing item, reminder, or proposal identifier.

mode.description: Explain the evidence chain or apply a scoped revocation.

confirmation_token.description: Required for revocation writes; generated by a prior explanation response.

include_sensitive.description: Only local dashboard may request true; spoken relay must reject it.

tools.name: revalidate_pending_plan
tools.why: The proposed stale-plan sentinel cannot safely compare a prepared browser/Mac action against current state without a typed, least-privilege recheck that returns only changed fields and provenance. Existing generic execution tools are too broad and may commit actions.

sources.description: Optional source IDs; defaults to sources captured in the plan

includeSensitiveSnippets.description: Must default false; only true after explicit owner request

tools.name: autonomy_policy_evaluate
tools.why: A shared deterministic evaluator is needed so relay, Mac, browser, and pendant make the same ACT/PREPARE/QUEUE/ASK decision without asking the expensive model on every job. It must be fail-closed and expose matched rules for owner-facing explanations.

tools.name: attention_arbitrate
tools.why: A single durable arbiter is needed to decide whether cross-surface events should interrupt, defer, coalesce, or suppress. Without a typed decision endpoint, each scheduled job and surface will continue notifying independently and the proposed capability cannot be implemented safely.

input_schema.expected_output: A signed, explainable decision per event: decision (speak_now|vibrate|defer|queue|coalesce|suppress), deliver_after, expires_at, rationale_codes, grouped_event_ids, policy_version, and an audit record with idempotency key. It must fail closed for normal sensitive content but fail open for explicit deadlines above the urgent threshold.

tools.name: record_pendant_delivery_event
tools.why: The existing job and pipeline receipts stop at server-side generation/acceptance; no current tool can ingest or reconcile a pendant's authenticated downloaded/played ACK, including offline replay and duplicate suppression.

deviceSkills.name: universal_stop_latch
deviceSkills.what_it_does: A deliberate long button press (and, when locally recognized, a spoken 'stop everything') immediately silences queued playback, marks the current interaction cancelled, and emits a tiny signed stop token. The relay, Mac planner, browser runner, and any pending pipeline consume that token to cancel only owner-owned in-flight work, while irreversible actions remain stopped before submission. When the link is down, the pendant keeps the latch active and reports cancellation as soon as it reconnects.

deviceSkills.name: audio_delivery_ack_queue
deviceSkills.what_it_does: For each downloaded audio artifact, persist an opaque artifact ID, byte-range/checksum, download completion, and playback start/finish (or interruption) event. Retry unsent ACKs over the link, deduplicate by event ID, and expose a local LED/button-safe status when the queue cannot be uploaded.

deviceSkills.name: offline_privacy_panic_wipe
deviceSkills.what_it_does: A deliberate five-second button hold enters a local panic state: stop microphone capture, discard queued PCM and generated audio, revoke/rotate locally cached auth material, emit a red LED pattern, and persist only a tiny revocation epoch so the relay/Mac can invalidate remote sessions on reconnect. A short press after recovery acknowledges the state but cannot restore erased data.

proposals.user_asks: “I’m going offline for a while—prepare what I need, and catch me up on only what changed when I’m back.”
proposals.why_useful: A dropped link, flight, dead phone, or closed laptop currently fragments the agent’s work. This creates a deliberate continuity handoff: the owner gets a small offline packet before disconnecting, and a conflict-aware delta when the pendant reconnects instead of repeating stale briefings.
surfaces: pendant detects a spoken offline request or link-loss transition and confirms the handoff locally
relay freezes active jobs, records a signed checkpoint, and queues safe background work
Mac planner gathers explicitly permitted local files, calendar items, and browser page snapshots into an encrypted offline capsule
browser bridge captures only approved authenticated pages and marks each item with its capture time and freshness
on reconnect, relay compares the capsule against current Mac/browser evidence, asks the owner about conflicts, and speaks a short changed-since-handoff digest
proposals.model_tier: Cheap background model extracts and diffs documents/pages; gpt-5.6-luna handles conflict resolution and prioritization; realtime is only for the two short spoken interactions.
proposals.latency_budget: Handoff acknowledgement under 2 seconds; capsule preparation within 60 seconds for a normal work set. Reconnect digest under 10 seconds after the link is usable, with deeper reconciliation continuing in the background.
proposals.cost_estimate: Roughly $0.02–$0.15 per handoff, dominated by document/page extraction and diffing; negligible cost when no handoff occurs.
proposals.security_concerns: Offline capsules are high-value copies of private data. Use end-to-end encryption with device-bound keys, short expiry, explicit source allowlists, and a visible capsule manifest. Never cache passwords, browser cookies, raw microphone audio, or secrets. Require confirmation before syncing any changed content back or taking external actions.
missing: A durable cross-surface checkpoint and job freeze/resume protocol
Encrypted pendant-readable handoff metadata and a Mac-local encrypted capsule store
Browser snapshot/export support that preserves freshness and provenance without exporting session credentials
A reconnect diff engine with conflict and stale-data handling
A local pendant state indicator and offline/reconnected event surfaced to relay

proposals.user_asks: “Before I walk into this conversation, give me the context I need—and afterward, turn what I explicitly marked into a follow-up plan without sending anything.”
proposals.why_useful: The owner’s important conversations span calendar invitations, email threads, private project pages, and spoken notes, but today those surfaces do not form a safe before/after loop. This capability gives a concise pre-conversation context packet, then converts only deliberately marked observations into sourced follow-up items, preserving continuity without secretly recording everyone.
surfaces: pendant receives an explicit “brief me for this conversation” request and offers a local mark gesture during or immediately after it
relay identifies the meeting/person and coordinates a bounded job
Mac planner gathers permitted calendar, Mail, local notes, and files relevant to that person or meeting
browser bridge reads approved authenticated project/customer pages and returns only cited excerpts
afterward, the pendant asks whether to finalize the marked items; relay reconciles them with the gathered context
Mac creates a reviewable follow-up workspace with owners, dates, evidence, and drafts, while the pendant speaks only the top two actions
proposals.model_tier: Use a cheap background model for retrieval, clustering, and citation extraction; use gpt-5.6-luna for identity/entity resolution, conflict handling, and concise plan synthesis; use realtime only for the short pre-brief and post-conversation confirmation.
proposals.latency_budget: Pre-brief in under 15 seconds, with a first three-bullet answer in under 5 seconds. Post-conversation extraction can finish within 60 seconds. No outbound action occurs without explicit approval.
proposals.cost_estimate: Approximately $0.03–$0.20 per conversation, dominated by authenticated browser and mailbox retrieval; recurring cost is avoided by caching cited source fingerprints until they expire.
proposals.security_concerns: This must not become covert meeting surveillance. Require an explicit pre-brief invocation and an unmistakable mark gesture/phrase; do not retain unmarked audio or third-party speech. Enforce source allowlists, redact sensitive excerpts, show provenance and retention, and require confirmation before sending mail, submitting forms, or sharing any generated content.
missing: An identity-and-meeting resolver spanning calendar attendees, Mail, local files, and browser sessions
A pendant-local mark/unmark interaction that works offline and survives a dropped link
A bounded retrieval policy with source allowlists, freshness, and sensitive-field redaction
A durable conversation checkpoint tying pre-brief evidence to post-conversation marks
A Mac review workspace that shows each proposed follow-up, its source, confidence, and approval state

proposals.user_asks: “I can’t deal with this now—bring it back to me later.” Then, at the right time, remind me with the exact page, message, or file I was looking at and a one-sentence explanation of what I meant to do; let me snooze or finish it by voice.
proposals.why_useful: People lose commitments at the handoff between attention states. This turns an offhand spoken intention into a reliable return to the precise context, rather than a generic reminder that requires reconstructing the task.
surfaces: pendant captures the spoken intent and gives immediate audible confirmation
relay stores a durable deferred-action packet and schedules the return
Mac planner resolves the relevant local file/window and browser extension resolves the authenticated tab, each with read-only evidence
relay recontacts the pendant at the chosen time; Mac/browser re-open or stage the context without sending/submitting anything
dashboard shows the packet, source evidence, snooze history, and a clear delete control
proposals.model_tier: gpt-realtime-2.1 only for the short capture/confirmation and spoken return; gpt-5.6-luna on the relay/Mac for deferred interpretation and context resolution; gpt-4.1-mini only for screenshot/UI grounding when selectors fail. No expensive realtime turn while asleep.
proposals.latency_budget: Capture confirmation under 1.5s. Background context resolution under 30s. At reminder, spoken summary within 3s, with staged context allowed to follow asynchronously.
proposals.cost_estimate: About $0.01–$0.08 per deferred item depending on browser/UI recovery; realtime audio dominates capture, while most scheduled work uses cheaper model and can be batched.
proposals.security_concerns: The packet may contain private page text, file paths, and sensitive intent. Encrypt at rest, retain only a bounded source excerpt plus hashes, honor existing browser-read permission, and require confirmation for any send, delete, purchase, or other irreversible action. Never expose secrets in spoken notifications or dashboard previews by default.
missing: durable deferred-action packet and scheduler with idempotent lifecycle
cross-surface context handoff that can bind a browser tab, Mac window/file, and source evidence
voice snooze/complete controls and a notification quiet-hours policy
owner-visible retention and deletion controls

proposals.user_asks: “Protect my attention. While I’m working or in a meeting, decide which incoming things truly deserve an interruption; quietly queue the rest, and tell me afterward what you held back and why.”
proposals.why_useful: Today notifications compete blindly with the owner’s attention. The hive should understand the owner’s current activity, urgency, relationship, and deadline, then make a transparent interruption decision rather than merely forwarding alerts or producing another periodic briefing.
surfaces: pendant detects the owner’s interruptibility mode locally from button state, spoken preference, and connection status, and provides a discreet haptic or short spoken interrupt when authorized
relay remains awake, receives candidate events, applies quiet-hours and escalation policy, and keeps an auditable held/allowed queue
Mac planner reads foreground app/window, calendar meeting state, local task deadlines, and notification metadata without exporting unnecessary content
browser extension inspects only opted-in authenticated tabs for urgent changes and supplies source evidence; it never sends or mutates anything
dashboard lets the owner set policies such as ‘never interrupt calls except family’ and review, release, or permanently dismiss held items
proposals.model_tier: Use a cheap background model for event classification and policy explanation; use gpt-5.6-luna only for ambiguous cross-source conflicts; reserve gpt-realtime-2.1 for the rare spoken escalation and the owner’s reply. Deterministic deadline/contact rules should run without a model.
proposals.latency_budget: Candidate events should be classified in under 2 seconds. A permitted urgent interruption should reach the pendant within 3 seconds; held events can be summarized in a later batch.
proposals.cost_estimate: Roughly $0.01–$0.05 per classified burst, dominated by private-content summarization; metadata-only rules should be effectively free. Realtime cost occurs only when an interruption is actually delivered or discussed.
proposals.security_concerns: This system sees highly sensitive notification, calendar, browser, and activity metadata. Process metadata locally where possible, minimize snippets sent to the relay, encrypt the queue, define short retention, expose the reason/source for every decision, and require explicit confirmation before any reply, dismissal, or external action. A fail-safe mode must hold rather than suppress when classification is uncertain.
missing: an interruptibility policy language with precedence, contacts, deadlines, and escalation windows
a local Mac activity/calendar/notification broker that emits privacy-minimized candidate events
a relay-side durable held-event queue with reason codes, replay protection, and delivery acknowledgements
pendant haptic/privacy interaction hardware and firmware for discreet acknowledgement
a review UI showing what was interrupted, held, expired, or escalated and allowing policy correction

proposals.user_asks: “Only interrupt me when something truly matters; otherwise keep a quiet queue and tell me at the right time.”
proposals.why_useful: The owner currently has several daily routines, browser watches, long-running Mac jobs, and a pendant that can reach them anywhere, but no shared decision about when an alert deserves an interruption. This would merge duplicate findings, weigh deadline and consequence, respect quiet hours, and escalate only when waiting is likely to cost them something. The owner gets fewer noisy briefings and does not miss the one item that actually matters.
surfaces: browser-extension reads the owner's authenticated pages and produces sourced change events without exporting page contents
mac-planner/mac-terminal correlate calendar deadlines, running jobs, files, and failed or blocked work
relay stores a compact urgency queue and applies quiet hours, deduplication, sensitivity, and escalation policy
pendant/relay-realtime speaks a single short interruption when the threshold is crossed; otherwise it announces the next digest at a natural interaction
dashboard or Mac workbench shows why an item was escalated, what evidence supports it, and snooze/resolve controls
proposals.model_tier: Use a cheap background model for extraction, clustering, deadline and consequence scoring; reserve gpt-realtime for the actual short spoken interruption. Use the expensive judgement model only when evidence conflicts or an escalation would cause a meaningful interruption.
proposals.latency_budget: Background events can settle within 1–5 minutes. A high-confidence urgent event should reach the pendant within 10 seconds; routine items can wait for the next scheduled digest. The spoken alert must be one short sentence with an optional follow-up.
proposals.cost_estimate: Roughly $0.01–$0.08 per day for normal event classification and digesting, dominated by authenticated-page extraction and repeated context. Urgent voice delivery adds only a small realtime turn. Avoid sending full page contents repeatedly by retaining hashes, snippets, source URLs, and expiry times.
proposals.security_concerns: Private mail, calendar, and page contents should remain on the Mac/browser bridge; the relay should receive only the minimum normalized event, sensitivity label, deadline, and evidence pointer. Never speak secrets aloud by default. Escalation must not send mail, submit forms, delete files, or buy anything; those remain confirmation-gated. The owner must be able to inspect, mute, snooze, correct, and delete every queued event.
missing: A durable cross-surface event schema with provenance, expiry, sensitivity, and idempotency
A shared urgency policy/queue service with quiet hours, deduplication, escalation and snooze state
A pendant notification/queue protocol that survives a dropped voice session
A small dashboard/workbench for explaining and correcting escalation decisions

proposals.user_asks: “While I’m away, carry this through within the limits I set—and stop, ask, or hand it back whenever the situation exceeds those limits.”
proposals.why_useful: Today the owner must either remain in the conversation or grant a dangerously broad instruction. This would let them delegate a real goal across private browser sessions, Mac applications, and the always-awake relay with explicit bounds: allowed sites, budget, deadline, reversible actions, people it may contact, and conditions requiring approval. The pendant is the portable consent and hand-back channel, not merely a microphone. The owner returns to a trustworthy result, a stopped-at-boundary task, or a concise request for the one missing decision.
surfaces: pendant captures the owner's spoken delegation and provides local button/voice approval, cancellation, and emergency stop
relay mints short-lived, scoped delegation capabilities, tracks heartbeats and expiry, and routes questions or completion notices
mac-planner/mac-terminal execute bounded file, research, and application work under the issued capability and preserve a step-by-step receipt
browser-extension operates only in explicitly allowed authenticated tabs/sites, with field-level and action-level policy checks
faculty-perception verifies current page/task state and detects when the requested bounds no longer match reality
faculty-action performs only permitted reversible work and pauses before any boundary-crossing action
proposals.model_tier: Use a cheaper background model for routine planning, policy matching, and progress summaries. Use the expensive judgement model only for ambiguity or a proposed boundary change. Use realtime solely for the brief live question, approval, or hand-back message.
proposals.latency_budget: Delegated work can run asynchronously. A boundary violation or approval question should reach the pendant within 10 seconds; normal progress can wait for completion or a scheduled digest.
proposals.cost_estimate: Approximately $0.02–$0.20 per delegation, dominated by browser/Mac execution and occasional ambiguity resolution; most steps should use deterministic policy checks and a cheaper model. No full private page or file corpus needs to be resent to the relay.
proposals.security_concerns: This is high-impact delegation and must default to deny. Capabilities need audience/device binding, short expiry, one-time nonces for irreversible steps, a spend limit, domain/app allowlists, data egress rules, and revocation from the pendant. Mail sending, purchases, deletion, account/security changes, and external uploads always pause for explicit confirmation. Every action needs before/after evidence and a tamper-evident receipt; private content should remain on the Mac/browser bridge except for the minimum needed to ask or report.
missing: A capability-token and policy-enforcement layer shared by relay, Mac, and browser
A durable delegation state machine with heartbeat, pause, revoke, expiry, and hand-back semantics
A pendant-local emergency stop and approval protocol that works through intermittent connectivity
A provenance-rich execution receipt that can be replayed and audited across surfaces

proposals.user_asks: “I’m back—catch me up on anything you did or anything that changed while I was away, and tell me the one thing I should do next.”
proposals.why_useful: Today async work, browser watches, scheduled briefs, and pendant conversations can each produce updates, but the owner has to reconstruct them. This gives them a single interruption-safe return point: a short spoken delta, evidence links on the Mac, explicit uncertainty, and one prioritized next action. It is more useful than another dashboard because it answers the human question at the moment they regain attention.
proposals.model_tier: Use the relay realtime model only to recognize the short return command and speak the final sentence. A background/cheap model on the relay should gather and rank completed/changed items; mac-planner should reconcile Mac jobs, browser watches, schedules, and pending confirmations; browser supplies private-page evidence; dashboard/Mac writes the detailed evidence packet.
proposals.latency_budget: A spoken acknowledgement under 300 ms, then a 1–3 second concise answer from cached event summaries. If reconciliation is still running, speak the top known item and continue in the background, delivering a second update only if it changes the recommendation.
proposals.cost_estimate: Roughly $0.01–$0.05 per return check if event summaries are precomputed; dominant cost is model ranking and any browser re-read. Avoid sending raw page contents or full transcripts by using typed event deltas and cached evidence snippets.
proposals.security_concerns: Private browser titles/snippets and Mac activity must remain local or encrypted to the relay; do not read unrelated tabs. Clearly label inferred versus verified changes. Never send, delete, purchase, or submit as part of catch-up; any suggested action remains a separate confirmation-gated job. The owner should be able to say 'only tell me urgent' and 'show evidence.'
missing: A cross-surface event journal with durable completion/change records and deduplication IDs
A resume/return packet compiler that ranks items by urgency, owner commitments, and freshness
A single spoken catch-up intent routed from pendant to relay, with detailed evidence exposed on the Mac/dashboard
A privacy filter that redacts sensitive event payloads from voice while preserving local evidence links

proposals.user_asks: “Before I commit to this, show me what it will make harder, what it displaces, and the safest alternative.”
proposals.why_useful: The owner can currently ask for calendar facts or have a form prepared, but not see the downstream consequences of a decision across their real life. This capability turns a proposed meeting, purchase, deadline, or browser action into a compact consequence map: conflicts, displaced commitments, travel or time costs, unfinished Mac work, and reversible alternatives. It helps the owner decide before creating a problem rather than receive another reminder afterward.
proposals.model_tier: Use a cheaper background reasoning model to construct the consequence graph from typed calendar, task, job, and browser facts. Use the realtime model only for the owner's spoken question and a concise explanation. mac-planner gathers local jobs and files; browser reads only explicitly relevant authenticated pages; the dashboard presents the evidence and alternatives.
proposals.latency_budget: A spoken acknowledgement under 300 ms, with a useful first answer in 2–5 seconds from cached facts. Deep comparisons can continue in the background, but the owner must never be blocked from making the original decision.
proposals.cost_estimate: Approximately $0.02–$0.10 per analysis, dominated by graph construction and any authenticated-page reads. Cache stable commitments and use deterministic conflict checks before invoking a model.
proposals.security_concerns: This crosses highly sensitive calendar, mail, task, and browser data, so raw content should stay on the Mac whenever possible and only redacted facts should reach the relay. Never make the commitment automatically. Clearly separate observed conflicts from inferred risks, show source/time for each claim, and require confirmation before opening, sending, buying, or rescheduling anything.
missing: A typed personal commitment/dependency graph spanning calendar, reminders, Mac jobs, and browser tasks
A consequence-analysis service that models displacement, deadlines, travel, and reversibility rather than merely listing conflicts
A Mac-local privacy boundary that performs sensitive joins before sending a minimal projection to the relay
A dashboard view for alternative scenarios and an explicit 'do not change anything' mode

proposals.user_asks: “I’m back—what happened while I was away?”
proposals.why_useful: Today a dropped LTE link, dead battery, or headphones disconnected can make completed work indistinguishable from lost work. This gives the owner one trustworthy catch-up across the pendant, always-awake relay, Mac jobs, and authenticated browser work, without replaying every notification.
surfaces: pendant detects reconnect/charging and sends its last acknowledged event sequence
relay retains a compact ordered stream of job, approval, failure, and urgency events while the pendant is unreachable
mac-planner and browser-extension attach evidence links and completion receipts for work done during the gap
faculty-perception deduplicates events and separates heard, completed, blocked, and awaiting approval
relay-realtime speaks a one-sentence digest; pendant haptics indicate whether more items are waiting; Mac workbench holds full details
proposals.model_tier: Use a cheap background summarizer (gpt-5.6-luna or equivalent) to cluster and prioritize the retained event stream; use realtime only for the short spoken digest and follow-up questions. Browser/Mac evidence extraction happens at job completion, not at reconnect.
proposals.latency_budget: Under 2 seconds for a short digest after reconnect, assuming cached event metadata; under 10 seconds only when evidence must be fetched. Never block the digest on a slow browser page.
proposals.cost_estimate: About $0.01–$0.05 per reconnect digest, dominated by summarization and any fresh evidence extraction; cached metadata should keep most reconnects near the low end.
proposals.security_concerns: The relay must retain event metadata without retaining private page contents longer than policy allows. Browser links/snippets should be fetched only for items the owner requests. Spoken output can expose sensitive subjects in public; default to neutral titles and require a button press or voice request for details. Never imply an irreversible action occurred unless the Mac/browser receipt is cryptographically tied to its idempotency key.
missing: A durable cross-surface event stream with per-pendant acknowledgment cursor and replay protection
A compact completion/blocked/approval receipt schema shared by Mac and browser jobs
Reconnect-triggered pendant push and optional haptic status patterns
Retention and redaction policy for offline event metadata

proposals.user_asks: “Put us in silent mode—I need to use you without speaking or taking out my phone.”
proposals.why_useful: The owner cannot reliably use the assistant in a meeting, on transit, or anywhere speech would be inappropriate. A true silent mode would turn the wearable into a discreet two-way interface instead of merely muting spoken output.
surfaces: a revised pendant with a small capacitive touch strip or two tactile controls and a haptic motor accepts a constrained tap language and renders short replies as distinct haptic patterns
relay-realtime switches the conversation into a low-bandwidth silent session and sends only compact intents/results
mac-planner and browser-extension perform the same authenticated work as voice sessions, but expose a terse status/result vocabulary
the Mac workbench retains the full text transcript and evidence for later review, while the pendant receives only the minimum needed to choose the next step
proposals.model_tier: Use the cheaper background model for intent classification, result compression, and action planning; reserve realtime for a brief transition command or if the owner exits silent mode. No expensive model should be spent generating prose the pendant cannot convey.
proposals.latency_budget: Local tap acknowledgment under 100 ms; common status/result patterns under 1 second; complex work can run asynchronously with haptic progress and a full Mac receipt.
proposals.cost_estimate: Approximately $0.01–$0.05 per silent interaction, dominated by model calls; hardware revision adds roughly $5–$15 in controls, haptic actuator, driver, and enclosure changes, plus engineering.
proposals.security_concerns: Haptics are observable by touch and can be misunderstood. Limit silent mode to reversible actions by default; require an explicit multi-tap confirmation for sending, deleting, purchasing, or sharing. Do not encode sensitive content in publicly guessable patterns. Show the full proposed action and evidence on the Mac before any irreversible operation.
missing: A silent-mode protocol with a small, tested intent/result vocabulary
Pendant input hardware beyond the current single button and output beyond the current LED
Relay session state that can switch modalities without losing the conversation or action idempotency
Mac/browser UI for reviewing silent-session transcripts and pending confirmations

proposals.user_asks: “Don’t interrupt me unless it’s important; if I’m busy, queue it and tell me at the right moment.”
proposals.why_useful: The pendant becomes considerate rather than merely loud: urgent changes reach the owner, while routine mail, job completions, and watch events wait for a safe conversational opening. It uses the wearable’s presence, the Mac’s current work state, browser task state, and the always-awake relay together—something no single surface can judge reliably.
surfaces: pendant: captures a local quiet/urgent override and delivers a one-sentence alert or haptic cue
relay: maintains the durable notification queue, deadlines, deduplication, and escalation while the Mac sleeps
mac-planner: reports coarse foreground-app/focus/meeting state and classifies whether an item truly needs interruption
browser: contributes authenticated page-watch urgency and evidence links without exposing page contents to the pendant
dashboard: lets the owner inspect, reprioritize, snooze, or replay queued items
proposals.model_tier: A cheap background model/rules engine classifies urgency and likely interruptibility; gpt-5.6-luna is used only for ambiguous prioritization or a requested digest; realtime is reserved for the final low-latency spoken delivery.
proposals.latency_budget: Urgent alerts should arrive within 2 seconds of a relay event; routine items may wait for the next inferred break (up to 30 minutes) and must expire rather than nag. A spoken “quiet until 3” override should take effect immediately.
proposals.cost_estimate: Roughly $0.001–$0.01 per queued event, dominated by occasional classification; most events use deterministic rules and no model call. Delivery uses the existing realtime session, so there is no extra generation cost when already connected.
proposals.security_concerns: Send only coarse state (focus/busy/meeting, not keystrokes or screenshots) and event metadata; keep authenticated page evidence on the Mac/browser unless the owner asks to hear it. No destructive action is taken. Creating or changing an external reminder still follows the owner’s existing confirmation policy; snooze/queue changes are reversible.
missing: A shared event envelope with urgency, expiry, provenance, and sensitivity
A relay-side durable notification queue with dedupe and escalation rules
A Mac/browser interruptibility signal API that reports coarse state only
Pendant delivery semantics for haptic versus spoken alerts and an offline queue
A small owner policy surface for quiet windows, VIP sources, and escalation thresholds

proposals.user_asks: “If I walk away, pause anything that could change the world, and only resume it when I’m back and the context is still valid.”
proposals.why_useful: The owner can safely delegate multi-step work without worrying that a stale browser page, expired login, changed price, or unattended Mac will complete the wrong action. The pendant supplies real-world presence, the Mac and browser provide task state, and the relay preserves and revalidates the work while the owner is away.
surfaces: pendant: emits a privacy-preserving presence/return signal and gives a local pause/resume control
relay: freezes the job, records its exact checkpoint and expiry, and wakes it for revalidation when the owner returns
mac-planner: checkpoints the plan and verifies that files, app state, and assumptions are still current
browser: freezes authenticated tabs and rechecks URL, account, page fingerprint, and all irreversible fields before any continuation
dashboard: shows paused jobs, the reason they were held, what changed while away, and the exact next action requiring approval
proposals.model_tier: Deterministic state checks handle presence, lease expiry, page fingerprints, and checkpoint validation. gpt-5.6-luna is used only to explain changed assumptions or revise an ambiguous plan; realtime is used for the short return-time spoken summary.
proposals.latency_budget: Pause within 1 second of a reliable departure signal. On return, provide a brief status within 3 seconds, but never resume an irreversible step automatically; revalidation can take up to 10 seconds before presenting the owner with a confirmation.
proposals.cost_estimate: Usually below $0.005 per pause/resume cycle, dominated by occasional model-based explanation. State checks and checkpoint storage are effectively negligible; browser revalidation is the main operational cost.
proposals.security_concerns: Presence should be represented as a coarse local signal, not a location history. While away, no external side effects occur. On return, changed or destructive actions require explicit confirmation and show before/after evidence. Checkpoints may contain sensitive task data and must be encrypted with bounded retention.
missing: Pendant presence and return events with reliability/uncertainty metadata
A resumable job lease and checkpoint protocol shared by relay, Mac, and browser
Browser page/account fingerprinting and stale-form invalidation
A return-time revalidation and approval UI
An explicit policy distinguishing safe reversible work from world-changing work

proposals.user_asks: “Only interrupt me when it is genuinely worth breaking my concentration; otherwise queue it and catch me at the next natural pause.”
proposals.why_useful: The owner currently has separate voice, Mac, browser, and scheduled workflows, but no shared decision about when an event deserves an interruption. This would make the pendant feel considerate rather than noisy: it combines calendar state, active Mac/browser work, urgency and deadlines, then either speaks now, queues a compact card/audio item, or suppresses it with an explainable reason. At the next pause it can summarize what accumulated, without losing the original source or actionability.
proposals.model_tier: Use a cheap background classifier/rules engine for event scoring and queue maintenance; use gpt-5.6-luna only to summarize a grouped queue or resolve ambiguous priority; reserve gpt-realtime-2.1 for the owner's live request to interrupt, defer, or review. The pendant should enforce a local emergency/voice override when disconnected.
proposals.latency_budget: Urgent events should score in under 2 seconds; ordinary events can wait 30–60 seconds for batching. A spoken review should begin within 500 ms after the owner asks. Context should be compact (event, source, deadline, current activity, confidence), not a full transcript.
proposals.cost_estimate: Usually <$0.01 per day if scoring is rules plus a small model only for ambiguous items; a review costs roughly $0.01–$0.05 depending on queue size. The dominant cost is summarization, not event ingestion.
proposals.security_concerns: Calendar titles, browser page metadata, notifications and active-window state leave the Mac only as normalized event records; raw page text and notification bodies should stay local unless explicitly needed. Never auto-dismiss, send, submit, or alter a reminder. Require confirmation before suppressing an item permanently; show source, score factors, expiry, and an undo path. Treat secrets and message content as sensitive.
missing: A cross-surface interruption policy and durable event queue with urgency/deadline/expiry fields
Mac hooks for notification and active-window/context signals, plus browser tab activity summaries
Pendant-side queue/override protocol that works offline and survives a dropped relay link
A dashboard showing queued, deferred, suppressed, and expired items with one-tap restore
Owner interruption preferences (already requested upstream) must be applied once available

proposals.user_asks: “When I double-press the pendant, make the whole system private until I say otherwise.”
proposals.why_useful: The owner cannot currently establish a trustworthy, immediate privacy boundary across a live voice session, Mac automation, authenticated browser tabs, and queued background work. A physical gesture would give them a simple social-space control: stop listening, stop screen/page observation, pause outgoing jobs and notifications, and prevent sensitive queued material from being spoken or shown until explicitly resumed. The owner should receive one discreet confirmation (LED/haptic), not an explanation that could itself disclose private content.
proposals.model_tier: No expensive model is needed for entering or leaving private mode. Firmware and deterministic relay/Mac/browser policy enforcement do the work; gpt-realtime is used only if the owner later asks what was paused, and a cheaper background model can summarize the paused queue after explicit resume.
proposals.latency_budget: The pendant must enter local mute/privacy state in under 100 ms, with relay audio cut and Mac/browser observation paused within 1 second. Resume should reconcile state in the background without replaying anything automatically.
proposals.cost_estimate: Negligible API cost during privacy transitions; a later explicit queue summary is roughly $0.01–$0.05. Engineering cost dominates: synchronized state, interruption of in-flight jobs, and safe recovery after power or network loss.
proposals.security_concerns: Privacy mode must be fail-closed: mute microphone locally, revoke/disable capture streams, stop new browser DOM/screenshot reads, pause Mac actions and relay pushes, and mark queued envelopes as withheld. Do not rely on a model to honor it. Persist only a signed mode transition and timestamp; encrypt withheld metadata, expire it, and give the owner a visible dashboard count without revealing titles. Require an explicit physical gesture or spoken confirmation to resume; never resume merely because the network reconnects.
missing: A pendant firmware privacy latch with physical confirmation and persistent fail-closed state
A signed, monotonic privacy-mode signal understood by relay, Mac agent, vision loop, and browser bridge
Cancellation/pause semantics for in-flight jobs, with safe checkpoints and idempotent resume rather than replay
Capture-stream revocation hooks and an audit trail showing which surfaces actually acknowledged privacy mode
A dashboard control to inspect and discard withheld work after resume

proposals.user_asks: When I make a consequential decision out loud, capture what I decided, the evidence and assumptions behind it, and—if I name a date—check back later and tell me whether reality matched the bet.
proposals.why_useful: People remember the conclusion but lose the reasoning, making repeated decisions and hindsight painful. This creates a private, searchable decision trail and a low-noise learning loop without requiring the owner to maintain another app. It is meaningfully more than a note: the pendant catches the moment, the Mac/browser assemble evidence, and the relay brings back the outcome at the right time.
surfaces: pendant: detect an explicit decision phrase or a button-marked moment, ask one brief confirmation before recording sensitive content, and provide a spoken/haptic receipt
relay: transcribe/classify the decision, store an encrypted decision packet and schedule a future check-in; remain available while the Mac is asleep
mac-planner: turn the packet into a structured Markdown record in ~/AI-Pendant-Workspace with decision, alternatives, assumptions, confidence, owner, and review date
browser-extension: gather cited facts from the currently relevant authenticated tabs, but only from tabs the owner has associated with the decision
mac-terminal: at review time, compare the recorded success criteria against current local files or explicitly permitted browser evidence and prepare a concise delta
unified: reconcile the evidence and ask whether to revise the decision record; never silently infer that an outcome is success or failure
proposals.model_tier: Use gpt-realtime-2.1 only for the pendant's live capture and confirmation; use gpt-5.6-luna for extraction, evidence reconciliation, and review; use a cheaper scheduled/background model for polling and drafting the review packet.
proposals.latency_budget: Receipt under 2 seconds after confirmation. Evidence assembly can finish in the background within 2 minutes. Review notifications should be quiet and arrive only at the named date or a meaningful evidence change.
proposals.cost_estimate: Roughly $0.01–$0.06 per decision capture/review, dominated by realtime audio and authenticated-page extraction; scheduled unchanged checks should be pennies or less using hashes and a cheap model.
proposals.security_concerns: Decision records may expose health, finances, or work strategy. Store locally by default, encrypt relay payloads, attach sensitivity and retention, and require confirmation before capturing an ambiguous or sensitive decision. Browser evidence must be allowlisted and cited; never send mail, submit forms, or change source data. The owner can delete a record and cancel its review.
missing: A decision-record schema distinct from reminders/commitments, with assumptions, alternatives, evidence citations, success criteria, and review state
An event-to-file persistence and encrypted relay queue shared by pendant, Mac, and scheduled jobs
A user-controlled browser evidence binding (which tabs/sites may be consulted) and provenance-preserving extraction
A quiet review scheduler that can compare criteria without turning every watch into a notification
A compact pendant confirmation interaction and a private audio/haptic receipt

proposals.user_asks: Keep this private: do the work, but don't say the answer out loud—show it on my Mac and give me only a discreet pendant signal when it's ready.
proposals.why_useful: A wearable assistant is otherwise unusable in meetings, transit, or around family. The owner can delegate sensitive or lengthy work without broadcasting either the request's result or its contents. The Mac/browser can present detail while the pendant remains a safe, minimal control surface.
surfaces: pendant: a long-press or spoken phrase enables private-output mode, acknowledges with a distinct haptic pattern, and speaks only a generic completion cue
relay: carries the privacy/output policy with every job, redacts result text from realtime playback, and queues a minimal notification if the Mac is temporarily unavailable
mac-planner: renders the result in a lock-screen-safe or unlocked workspace pane according to the owner's setting, with an explicit expiry
browser-extension: performs authenticated research or prepares drafts while keeping page text out of spoken responses
faculty-judgement: selects whether the result can be summarized publicly, privately displayed, or withheld until the owner unlocks the Mac
faculty-action: enforces the output policy at the final delivery boundary, not merely in the model prompt
proposals.model_tier: gpt-realtime-2.1 for the short live mode toggle only; gpt-5.6-luna for planning and synthesis; background work on a cheaper model. No realtime call is needed just to signal completion.
proposals.latency_budget: Mode acknowledgement under 300 ms; discreet completion signal under 1 second after the result is committed. Detailed Mac rendering can take normal task latency.
proposals.cost_estimate: Negligible incremental API cost—mostly one short realtime turn per mode change. Hardware/software work dominates; polling should use push events rather than repeated model calls.
proposals.security_concerns: A generic signal can still reveal that a private task exists, so offer neutral vibration and configurable quiet hours. Never put sensitive text in desktop notifications, logs, URLs, or TTS buffers. Clear private mode after a timeout or explicit toggle, and require confirmation before switching back to spoken output for a sensitive result.
missing: A policy-carrying job envelope whose output channel and sensitivity survive relay, Mac, and browser handoffs
A pendant-local private-mode toggle and distinct haptic acknowledgement
A Mac presentation surface with lock-screen-safe redaction and automatic expiry
A final output firewall that blocks accidental TTS/log/notification leakage
Push completion events and a recovery path when the Mac is offline

proposals.user_asks: Before I commit to this, show me the likely consequences of each option using my actual calendar, messages, files, and logged-in services—and tell me what assumption would change your recommendation.
proposals.why_useful: The owner can get generic advice today, but not a grounded, private decision rehearsal spanning the surfaces that contain their real constraints. This would turn scattered facts into an explicit comparison without taking the action or pretending uncertain predictions are facts.
surfaces: pendant: capture the decision question and constraints hands-free, then read only the recommendation and the key uncertainty aloud
relay: maintain a short-lived encrypted scenario packet and coordinate the work while the Mac or browser is busy
mac-planner: decompose options, identify required evidence, and generate a comparison with confidence and missing-data labels
browser-extension: inspect only owner-approved authenticated tabs for prices, policies, availability, or account-specific constraints, preserving citations
mac-terminal: inspect local calendars, files, and project state when permitted, calculate dates/costs, and run deterministic what-if checks
faculty-perception: distinguish observed facts from forecasts and detect contradictions across sources
faculty-judgement: rank options against the owner's stated priorities, expose tradeoffs, and ask for clarification when the result is sensitive
faculty-action: make no external change; save a reviewable scenario packet and optionally set a user-approved expiry
proposals.model_tier: Use gpt-realtime-2.1 only for the live question and concise handoff. Use gpt-5.6-luna for decomposition and reconciliation, and a cheaper background model for deterministic comparisons and evidence collection.
proposals.latency_budget: A first useful comparison in 10–20 seconds for local evidence; authenticated browsing may take up to 2 minutes in the background. The pendant should immediately acknowledge scope and sources without reading sensitive details.
proposals.cost_estimate: Approximately $0.03–$0.20 per rehearsal, dominated by authenticated browser extraction and synthesis; cache source snapshots and use deterministic code for arithmetic to keep repeated comparisons inexpensive.
proposals.security_concerns: This could expose private mail, finances, health, or work information.
