The owner needs dependable closure, especially when they leave the room or lose connectivity. This turns the pendant into a trustworthy second check: it can say confirmed, not confirmed, or unknown with a reason and a link/evidence trail.
proposals.model_tier: Use the cheaper background model for post-action verification and evidence summarization; reserve realtime only for the owner's spoken follow-up and the final one-sentence answer.
proposals.latency_budget: Dispatch remains immediate; verify after a 2–10 second settle (configurable), then answer within 15 seconds. If a surface is offline, keep a durable pending check and notify when it reconnects.
proposals.cost_estimate: Roughly $0.002–$0.02 per completed verification, dominated by screenshots/DOM extraction and any model interpretation; typed checks should avoid model calls in the common case.
proposals.security_concerns: Verification must use least-privilege reads and preserve private-tab boundaries. Never infer success from a toast alone. Sensitive evidence should be hashed or redacted in receipts, and sending/deleting/purchasing still requires confirmation. Unknown must be an honest outcome, not a retry loop.
missing: A shared postcondition schema (expected entity/value plus observation recipe) across Mac, browser, relay, and pendant
Independent settle-and-reread verifier with idempotency correlation and PASS/FAIL/UNKNOWN states
A user-facing timeline linking the dispatch, observation, evidence, and any recovery/undo path
Reconnect handling for checks that were deferred while the Mac, bridge, or pendant was offline

proposals.user_asks: “If this isn’t done by Friday at 3, remind me and prepare the next step.”
proposals.why_useful: A normal reminder fires at a time whether or not the task is already complete. A conditional promise watches the actual postcondition, suppresses needless nagging when it is done, and escalates with a prepared reversible next step only when the condition remains unmet. This is a life-level safety net for applications, appointments, forms, and follow-ups.
proposals.model_tier: Cheap background/scheduled model evaluates the condition and drafts the next step; realtime is used only if the owner answers an escalation on the pendant.
proposals.latency_budget: Condition checks at a user-selected cadence or event, with a deadline-time check under 30 seconds; pendant alert should arrive within 5 seconds of a confirmed unmet condition.
proposals.cost_estimate: About $0.001–$0.01 per check when typed reads are available; model cost is dominated by drafting a next-step brief, not monitoring. Default to sparse checks and event-driven updates.
proposals.security_concerns: The promise definition must not expose private account data in notifications. Drafts remain unsent and destructive/financial actions require confirmation. The system must distinguish “not observed” from “not done” and avoid escalating on stale/offline evidence.
missing: A durable conditional-obligation record with deadline, owner-visible wording, condition, cadence, quiet hours, and escalation policy
Postcondition verification adapters and freshness-aware UNKNOWN state
A deadline scheduler that survives relay restarts and reconnects the pendant/Mac/browser
A safe next-step planner that can prepare but not execute irreversible actions

proposals.user_asks: “Notice when I keep getting stuck on the same kind of thing, and suggest one small change that would make it easier next time.”
proposals.why_useful: The system should improve the owner's life, not merely execute isolated commands. Across repeated pendant conversations, failed browser attempts, abandoned Mac jobs, and postponed reminders, it can identify recurring friction—without diagnosing or judging the owner—and offer a concrete, optional intervention at a calm moment. For example: “This is the third time the reimbursement form stalled at the same field; want me to save a private checklist?”
proposals.model_tier: Use a cheap background model over deliberately minimized, local summaries rather than raw audio or full browsing history; realtime only handles the owner's response when an intervention is offered.
proposals.latency_budget: No work on the critical interaction path. Analyze weekly or after three clearly related friction events; offer at most one suggestion in a short spoken sentence and otherwise remain silent.
proposals.cost_estimate: Approximately $0.01–$0.05 per weekly analysis, dominated by summarizing candidate events; local clustering and typed receipts should make routine detection inexpensive.
proposals.security_concerns: This is behavioral inference and therefore sensitive. Keep raw audio and page contents out of the analysis; use opt-in categories, local-first aggregation, retention limits, visible evidence for every suggestion, and a one-tap “never infer this again.” Never infer medical, psychological, or character traits, and never change routines automatically.
missing: A privacy-preserving friction-event vocabulary and local aggregation layer spanning pendant, Mac, browser, and relay
Cross-surface links that can establish repeated task friction without retaining raw content
An owner-controlled review and suppression UI for inferred patterns
A conservative intervention policy that requires repeated evidence and caps suggestion frequency

proposals.user_asks: “Do this, and tell me only when you can prove it worked.”
proposals.why_useful: Today the system can execute typed actions and return receipts, but a receipt is not proof—especially while Mac Accessibility and Screen Recording are unavailable. This gives the owner a dependable distinction between completed, observed-complete, and unable-to-verify, instead of confident false success.
proposals.model_tier: Use the realtime model only for the owner's short confirmation and spoken status; use gpt-5.6-luna for planning/contracts and a cheap background verifier for polling/re-observation. Use mac-vision only when permissions make visual observation trustworthy; otherwise prefer typed shell/browser evidence.
proposals.latency_budget: Immediate acknowledgement under 1 s; reversible actions within 5–10 s; background jobs can finish later. If verification is delayed, the pendant says it is still checking rather than claiming success.
proposals.cost_estimate: Roughly 1 planning call plus a cheap verification call per action; about $0.01–$0.05 for normal tasks, dominated by model context and any screenshot/vision upload. Realtime cost is limited to the spoken interaction.
proposals.security_concerns: Evidence may include private page text or file paths, so keep it local to the Mac/relay and redact secrets from receipts. Never infer success from a UI toast; require a typed postcondition or fresh observation. Sending mail, deleting files, or buying still requires confirmation even if the postcondition is satisfiable.
missing: A typed expected-postcondition field in every action/job contract
A re-observe verifier that can refuse success on mismatch or stale evidence
Permission-aware routing that marks visual evidence unavailable when Accessibility/Screen Recording are false
A compact pendant receipt format for verified/failed/unverified states
Dashboard history linking intent, action, evidence, and final state

proposals.user_asks: “Keep the conversation natural, even when the connection is busy or I talk over you.”
proposals.why_useful: The owner should be able to wear the pendant as a dependable conversation instrument rather than losing several seconds of their speech during talk-over. It should preserve the beginning of an interruption, keep playback intelligible, and recover without making them repeat themselves; the current prototype cannot do that.
proposals.model_tier: Use gpt-realtime only for the live turn-taking loop. Put congestion estimation, jitter buffering, packet-loss concealment, codec negotiation, and replay of a recovered interruption in firmware/relay code; do not spend model tokens on transport repair.
proposals.latency_budget: Local button/voice barge-in response under 100 ms; conversational audio one-way target under 120 ms; congestion mode switch under 300 ms; never queue more than one frame of stale speech.
proposals.cost_estimate: Near-zero incremental model API cost; engineering and bandwidth dominate. A production audio board/DSP and validation fixture are the main expense, with modest additional device power. 24 kHz full-duplex traffic may increase radio usage, so adaptive mode must protect battery and data budget.
proposals.security_concerns: Keep audio and transport telemetry TLS-protected. The relay may retain at most a tiny encrypted, expiring interruption buffer solely for loss recovery; never turn it into a transcript or durable recording without explicit consent. Authenticated codec negotiation prevents downgrade or injection.
missing: A product microphone/MCU/DSP capable of sustained 24 kHz capture and decode without consuming nearly the entire application core
A bounded full-duplex scheduler with admission control, jitter buffering, packet-loss concealment, and interruption sequence numbers
Relay support for codec/profile negotiation and selective retransmission or forward-error protection within the LTE-M record limit
A firmware/relay acceptance harness that measures speech loss, barge-in latency, intelligibility, and battery under simultaneous talk-over
A clear fallback policy that preserves continuity rather than allowing seconds of queued audio

proposals.user_asks: Tell me what I can safely ignore today, and keep anything risky from slipping through.
proposals.why_useful: The owner currently gets briefs and alerts, but still has to decide what not to read. This gives them a finite attention budget: it separates harmless noise from items whose delay could cost money, time, or a missed commitment, then quietly defers the harmless items while preserving an auditable way back. It is a judgement service, not another inbox summary.
surfaces: browser-extension: inspect already-authenticated mail, calendar, task, order, and work tabs without exposing credentials
mac-planner/mac-terminal: read local reminders/notes and current focus state, and write a reversible daily triage artifact
relay-realtime: deliver a single short spoken verdict and accept 'show me deferred' or 'why not ignore this?'
pendant: provide a one-button/voice 'defer for today' and an offline latch for the chosen quiet policy
relay: run the scheduled/background scan, retain evidence and wake the owner only when the risk score crosses a threshold
proposals.model_tier: Background scan and clustering use a cheaper slower model; realtime is used only for the owner's follow-up question or a newly urgent event. A deterministic policy layer computes deadlines, sender/account importance, and confidence before any model judgement.
proposals.latency_budget: Initial daily scan may take 1–3 minutes in the background; the spoken answer should be under 2 seconds from cached results. Any new page read can take up to 10 seconds and must return source links and freshness.
proposals.cost_estimate: Roughly $0.02–$0.10 per daily scan depending on number of private pages and model context; most cost is authenticated-page extraction and the final ranked synthesis, not the short spoken response.
proposals.security_concerns: Private mail/calendar/task contents leave the browser bridge only to the relay's authenticated job path. Never archive, delete, send, or change deadlines automatically. Deferral is reversible and records item URL, source timestamp, reason, expiry, and risk confidence. Require confirmation before muting an entire sender, changing a reminder, or suppressing an item beyond one day.
missing: A durable attention-arbitration/risk policy with per-item expiry and a user-visible deferred queue
Cross-surface authenticated reads normalized into one evidence record (not just independent summaries)
A pendant-local offline attention latch and a relay wake rule
A review/undo endpoint for deferrals and a feedback loop that learns 'ignore this' without silently broadening permissions

proposals.user_asks: Before I say yes to something, tell me what it will really cost me and give me a reply I can send.
proposals.why_useful: Today the owner can ask for calendar or browser summaries, but cannot turn a spoken opportunity or request into a consequence-aware decision. This would notice hidden costs—travel, preparation, recovery time, overlapping obligations, and deadline risk—then offer a concise accept, decline, or negotiate response before the commitment becomes real.
surfaces: pendant: capture the spoken offer or request in the moment, including an offline provisional marker when disconnected
relay: maintain the provisional decision window, calculate expiry, and deliver the short spoken recommendation
mac-planner/mac-terminal: inspect calendar, reminders, notes, travel context, and current work state; create a provisional hold and response draft
browser-extension: read the relevant authenticated message/event/page and place a reply draft in the correct private session without sending
unified/faculty-judgement: compare opportunity value against existing obligations and explain the recommendation with evidence
faculty-action: after explicit approval, send the reply or commit the calendar change and return a receipt
proposals.model_tier: Use deterministic checks for time conflicts, travel buffers, preparation estimates, deadlines, and existing commitments. Use a cheaper background model to infer preparation/recovery cost and draft language; use the expensive realtime tier only for the owner's live follow-up or an ambiguous tradeoff.
proposals.latency_budget: A cached spoken recommendation should arrive within 2 seconds. Fresh private-page/calendar inspection may take 5–15 seconds and should be announced as a pending decision window rather than blocking the conversation. Provisional captures must survive a dropped link and reconcile later.
proposals.cost_estimate: Approximately $0.02–$0.12 per decision, dominated by authenticated-page extraction and ambiguous-cost reasoning; routine conflict checks are local and nearly free. Sending or booking is not performed without explicit confirmation.
proposals.security_concerns: The system handles private messages, calendar, location/travel, and possibly sensitive commitments. Keep evidence scoped to the job with short retention and provenance hashes. Never infer or disclose private constraints in a drafted reply unless the owner approves the wording. External sends, purchases, and irreversible bookings require confirmation; stale drafts must be revalidated against the source page and calendar before commit.
missing: A durable provisional-commitment and decision-window store shared by pendant, relay, Mac, and browser
A typed obligation/cost graph that represents preparation, travel, recovery, deadlines, and uncertainty rather than only calendar events
A cross-surface preflight and stale-source revalidation step immediately before sending or booking
Pendant offline capture/replay with conflict resolution when the same decision is edited on the Mac
A review UI showing assumptions, alternatives, and the exact reply or calendar mutation before approval

proposals.user_asks: “When my scheduled brief runs, tell me exactly which sources were checked, which were unavailable or stale, and keep retrying the missing parts—never say it completed when it only produced a partial answer.”
proposals.why_useful: The current routine ledger reports multiple jobs as completed even though the owner’s requested Gmail, GitHub, and Calendar reads have repeatedly failed. This gives the owner a trustworthy brief rather than confident silence, and lets them decide whether to fix permissions or accept a partial result.
proposals.model_tier: Use a cheap background model to normalize source receipts and classify stale/blocked/complete; reserve realtime only to explain the result or ask for one permission decision. No model should infer success from a lack of error.
proposals.latency_budget: At schedule time, publish a partial coverage receipt within 2–5 seconds, then retry eligible missing sources in the background for up to 15 minutes. Spoken summary should be under 30 seconds and interruptible.
proposals.cost_estimate: Low: one background normalization call per routine run (roughly $0.001–$0.01 depending on source count); retries are mostly I/O. Realtime cost occurs only if the owner asks follow-up.
proposals.security_concerns: Receipts must contain source names, timestamps, permission state, and error class, not page contents or secrets. Browser data remains in the authenticated bridge; require confirmation before any mutation. Never expose secret-bearing URLs or snippets in the pendant audio.
missing: A routine execution contract with per-source required/optional inputs and freshness windows
A durable per-step receipt schema shared by Mac, browser bridge, relay, and pendant
A retry/lease policy that distinguishes transient offline failures from permanent permission failures
A scheduler rule preventing lastStatus=completed when required evidence is absent
A compact spoken and dashboard rendering for coverage receipts

proposals.user_asks: “If I double-press and hold the pendant, make the whole AI hive go private immediately: stop talking, cancel queued actions, freeze browser and Mac control, revoke active sessions, and do not send or retain anything else until I explicitly unlock it.”
proposals.why_useful: A person wearing an always-listening, multi-surface agent needs a dependable physical privacy brake that works even when speech recognition, the Mac, or the network is confused. Today there is no owner-verifiable way to stop every surface at once or know that private mode actually took effect.
proposals.model_tier: No model is needed to enter or enforce private mode. The pendant firmware and relay enforce it deterministically; a cheap background process may reconcile acknowledgements afterward. Realtime may only speak the short confirmation after local enforcement succeeds.
proposals.latency_budget: Pendant must mute capture/playback and emit the local privacy indication immediately, under 100 ms. Relay and connected surfaces should acknowledge within 1 second; disconnected surfaces receive the revocation on reconnect before accepting work.
proposals.cost_estimate: Very low per invocation: state propagation and cancellation only, with no inference. Small persistent event records cost negligible storage. Hardware cost is near zero if an existing button supports a distinct gesture; otherwise a dedicated privacy switch is roughly $1–$3 in components.
proposals.security_concerns: The gesture must be local, debounced, and impossible to trigger accidentally during ordinary presses. Private mode should fail closed: no queued command may execute without a fresh capability token issued after unlock. Existing in-flight irreversible actions need a defined boundary—cancel before commit where possible, otherwise report their receipt without taking new action. Store only mode transitions, not audio. Unlock must require a deliberate local gesture plus spoken/visual confirmation; never unlock from a remote request.
missing: A pendant-firmware privacy latch with local mute and nonvolatile mode state
A signed, short-lived cross-surface capability token required by Mac and browser action endpoints
Relay fan-out for immediate revoke, cancellation, and reconnect-time enforcement
Browser extension and Mac agent middleware that rejects commands while the token is revoked
A visible pendant indicator and a concise acknowledgement protocol
An audit/receipt record showing which surfaces acknowledged the freeze without recording private content

proposals.user_asks: “What do I actually know about this?” — reconcile the claims in my mail, calendar, notes, and logged-in pages, show what is confirmed versus assumed or contradicted, and keep the answer current until I tell you it is settled.
proposals.why_useful: People lose trust when assistants flatten an email, an old note, and a live account page into one fact. This gives the owner a compact answer with freshness and provenance, and surfaces contradictions before they become missed appointments, wrong payments, or embarrassing replies. It is genuinely cross-surface: the pendant is the query and alert surface, the relay coordinates durable claims, browser reads private web evidence, and Mac reads local notes/mail/calendar.
proposals.model_tier: Background/cheap model extracts and normalizes claims; faculty-perception reconciles evidence and assigns confidence; realtime is used only for the owner's spoken question or a high-impact contradiction alert.
proposals.latency_budget: Spoken answer in 3–6 seconds for an existing topic; 30–90 seconds for a fresh multi-source reconciliation. Contradiction alerts are queued and interruption-arbitrated rather than speaking immediately.
proposals.cost_estimate: Roughly $0.01–$0.06 per fresh reconciliation, dominated by model context and private-page extraction; cached claim updates should be cents or less. Storage is small structured records plus source hashes, not copied page contents.
proposals.security_concerns: Private mail, calendar, notes, and authenticated pages are processed. Keep raw content on the Mac/browser session where possible; relay stores only normalized claims, source identifiers, hashes, sensitivity, TTL, and user-selected topic scope. Never expose secrets in spoken alerts; require confirmation before turning an inferred claim into an external action.
missing: A durable claim/evidence schema with source, observedAt, freshness/TTL, confidence, sensitivity, and contradiction links
A topic-scoped reconciliation route that can fan out to Mac and authenticated browser reads and return citations
A review UI/audio format for confirmed, uncertain, and conflicting claims, with dismiss/settle/forget controls
A change-trigger bridge from page watches, calendar/mail/file events, and voice notes into claim re-evaluation
Retention and deletion policy for derived claims and source hashes

proposals.user_asks: “Help me practice this difficult conversation.” Use the context I authorize from my notes, calendar, mail, and relevant browser pages to role-play the other person, challenge my assumptions, and leave me with a concise set of points and boundaries I can recall from the pendant.
proposals.why_useful: The owner can prepare while walking, without manually assembling context or exposing private material to a separate coaching service. The pendant provides private voice rehearsal, the Mac and browser gather the authorized facts, and the relay keeps the exercise coherent across interruptions. This is not merely meeting preparation: it helps the owner discover what they actually want to say, rehearse likely objections, and preserve their chosen boundaries without sending anything.
proposals.model_tier: Use a cheaper background model to build a sourced context packet and objection candidates. Use realtime only for the live role-play and short spoken coaching turns. A final low-cost pass can compress the owner's chosen points into a durable rehearsal card.
proposals.latency_budget: Context assembly in 20–60 seconds; each spoken role-play turn under 2 seconds; final rehearsal card under 10 seconds.
proposals.cost_estimate: Approximately $0.03–$0.15 per rehearsal, dominated by context extraction and the realtime turns. Reusing a prepared context packet reduces repeat cost.
proposals.security_concerns: Mail, notes, calendar, and authenticated pages may contain sensitive relationship and employment information. Keep raw sources local to Mac/browser, send only selected excerpts and citations to the relay, and make the owner explicitly choose the role and source scope. Never contact the other person or infer sensitive traits; require confirmation before saving the rehearsal card or creating any follow-up.
missing: A first-class rehearsal session with role, objective, authorized source scope, and expiry
A local source-packet compiler that cites excerpts without copying whole private pages
A realtime role-play mode with explicit distinction between sourced facts, simulated objections, and model speculation
Pendant controls for pause, “stay in character,” “coach me,” and “save that point”
A private rehearsal-card store with automatic expiry and deletion

proposals.user_asks: “Before you submit or send this, tell me if anything private is about to reach the wrong person or a public site, and fix it if I want.”
proposals.why_useful: The most damaging assistant mistake is not a failed click but a successful disclosure: pasting a private note, API key, medical detail, or someone else’s contact information into the wrong form. The browser can see the destination and fields, the Mac can inspect the local source material, the relay can apply a consistent policy, and the pendant can give a brief warning while the owner is away from the keyboard. It should show the exact field, source, reason, and proposed redaction—not merely say “this may be sensitive.”
proposals.model_tier: Use a cheap local/relay classifier for secret and PII detection plus deterministic destination rules; reserve realtime faculty-judgement for ambiguous social context (recipient, audience, or whether disclosure is intentional). No model call is needed for known secret patterns or same-origin moves.
proposals.latency_budget: Under 300 ms for deterministic scans and under 1.5 s for a model-assisted ambiguity check before a submit/send click. Never delay ordinary browsing; inspect only at a transfer or irreversible action boundary.
proposals.cost_estimate: Usually near-zero per action with local pattern/NER checks; roughly $0.001–$0.01 only for ambiguous snippets, dominated by model classification. Do not upload whole pages or files—send field labels, destination, and minimal redacted evidence.
proposals.security_concerns: The guard itself handles sensitive data, so classification must run locally when possible and redact values in logs. A warning must fail closed for high-confidence secrets, but allow an explicit owner override with a short-lived, destination-bound approval. Never silently rewrite a message: present before/after text, affected source, and recipient/audience. Keep an audit receipt without retaining the secret value.
missing: A destination-and-data-flow policy engine that understands public/private audience, origin, sensitivity, and allowed transformations
Browser submit/send interception with a pre-submit snapshot and field-level provenance
Mac local secret/PII scanner that can return redacted spans from clipboard, editor, files, and selected text
A unified approval token bound to exact tab, URL, recipient, field values, and expiry
Pendant haptic/spoken warning and a dashboard showing disclosure receipts and overrides

proposals.user_asks: “Forget everything about this topic everywhere, and prove what was deleted and what could not be reached.”
proposals.why_useful: Today a personal AI can spread a sensitive fact across voice transcripts, relay jobs, browser receipts, Mac notes, queued audio, and pendant storage, but the owner has no single way to revoke it. A cross-surface erasure command would make the system safe to use for vulnerable conversations and accidental captures. It should search by an owner-confirmed topic/entity, show the deletion scope first, revoke queued work, remove local and relay artifacts, request browser-session cleanup, and return a signed receipt listing deleted, retained-by-law/system, and unreachable items.
proposals.model_tier: Use a cheap deterministic index and cryptographic labels to locate artifacts; use the expensive judgement tier only to resolve ambiguous references in the owner’s erasure request. Deletion execution and verification should be deterministic, not model-authored.
proposals.latency_budget: Show an initial scope in under 2 seconds. Complete reachable deletion in under 30 seconds, with asynchronous retries for offline Mac, browser, or pendant and a spoken completion/failure summary.
proposals.cost_estimate: Usually below $0.01 per request; dominated by no model calls and small durable deletion receipts. The expensive part is engineering the indexes and reliable retry protocol, not inference.
proposals.security_concerns: The erasure request itself must not reveal the secret in logs. Require confirmation of the scope when it includes broad or irreversible deletion, authenticate the owner, use tombstones and idempotent deletion, and retain only a minimal non-content receipt. A device that is offline must be marked unreachable rather than falsely reported deleted. Prevent later memory re-ingestion from surviving replicas.
missing: A cross-surface content lineage index linking transcript spans, derived facts, jobs, audio objects, browser receipts, Mac files, and pendant records without storing plaintext in the index
An authenticated erasure protocol with tombstones, leases, retries, and per-surface deletion attestations
Deletion adapters for relay storage, Mac workspace/caches, browser extension session artifacts, and pendant flash
A post-deletion ingest filter that rejects tombstoned entities and topics
Dashboard and spoken receipt UX for scope preview, confirmation, partial failure, and recheck

proposals.user_asks: “Did that actually happen?” After you act through my Mac or a logged-in site, prove the external result—not just that you clicked—and tell me if it is confirmed, probably done, still pending, or unknown.
proposals.why_useful: Today a successful local command or browser dispatch can leave the real-world effect uncertain, especially with offline tabs, stale pages, redirects, or a dropped link. This gives the owner closure and prevents duplicate payments, messages, bookings, or edits. It is specifically cross-surface: one surface acts, another independently re-observes the target, and the relay/pendant reports the result even after the owner leaves.
surfaces: unified: classify the intended external effect and its idempotency/retry policy
mac-planner: perform Mac action and capture before/after state
browser-extension: dispatch authenticated browser action and retain tab/session identity
faculty-perception: independently re-read the target and compare an effect predicate against fresh evidence
faculty-action: reconcile receipts, retry only safe idempotent steps, and escalate conflicts
relay-realtime: deliver a one-sentence closure or ask the owner when evidence remains ambiguous
pendant: provide a tactile/audio 'confirmed vs unknown' status and queue the result across a dropped link
proposals.model_tier: Use the cheaper background model for effect-predicate extraction, receipt correlation, and re-check scheduling; reserve realtime for the owner's “did it happen?” question and for ambiguous or high-consequence conflicts.
proposals.latency_budget: For reversible edits, initial confirmation within 10 seconds and one re-check after 30–90 seconds. For external systems with eventual consistency, continue in the durable job runner and report within the service's observed SLA; never claim success solely on dispatch.
proposals.cost_estimate: Usually 1–2 cheap verification passes plus existing tool calls; roughly 2–5x a normal action's tool/API overhead, with model cost dominated by extracting a predicate from the page/receipt. Realtime cost occurs only for the final short spoken result or an ambiguity.
proposals.security_concerns: Re-checking may expose private authenticated pages to the relay/model, so send only the target fields and hashes, not whole pages. Never infer a financial or destructive effect from a local success receipt. Require confirmation for retries that could duplicate an irreversible action; preserve evidence URLs, timestamps, and tab identity for audit.
missing: A first-class effect predicate (expected external state) and idempotency classification attached to every plan step
An independent re-observation/reconciliation job primitive with expiry and explicit CONFIRMED/LIKELY/PENDING/UNKNOWN/CONFLICT states
Per-surface adapters for post-action refresh/readback and external receipt correlation
A pendant/relay result packet that survives a dropped link without replaying the action

proposals.user_asks: “Before you change anything, make sure it is the right account and the right person.” Bind every browser or Mac action to the owner’s intended identity and workspace, detect account/profile changes before and during the task, and refuse to proceed when identity evidence conflicts.
proposals.why_useful: A logged-in browser can contain several accounts, workspaces, or profiles, and a successful action in the wrong one is worse than a failure. The owner should not have to remember which tab, profile, or tenant is active before asking the pendant to help. This provides a hard safety boundary that ordinary tab affinity and action receipts do not provide.
surfaces: pendant: capture the owner’s local approval gesture and a compact intended-account hint when needed
relay-realtime: bind the spoken request to a short-lived identity-and-workspace claim without storing credentials
mac-planner: identify the active macOS user, app workspace, and browser profile before planning
browser-extension: attest the active profile, origin, account label, tenant/workspace, and tab identity before dispatch and after navigation
faculty-perception: independently compare identity evidence from page chrome, URL/origin, session metadata, and Mac state
faculty-action: enforce the identity match as a non-bypassable precondition and abort on drift
unified: explain the mismatch in one short sentence and offer a read-only recovery path
proposals.model_tier: Use deterministic adapters and a cheap background model to normalize account/workspace labels. Use realtime only when the owner must resolve an ambiguity or explicitly choose among identities.
proposals.latency_budget: Preflight should complete in under 2 seconds for a known profile. Re-check identity immediately before any mutation and after redirects; ambiguity should pause rather than add latency through guessing.
proposals.cost_estimate: Small additional browser/Mac metadata reads per action; typically negligible model cost when labels are structured. The dominant cost is engineering and test coverage for multi-account sites, SSO redirects, and profile changes.
proposals.security_concerns: Never use passwords, cookies, or page contents as identity evidence. Store only origin, profile/session identifiers, normalized account/workspace labels, timestamps, and hashes. Treat a missing or stale label as a block, not as permission to infer. Owner confirmation is required when multiple identities legitimately match.
missing: A signed identity-attestation schema shared by pendant, Mac, relay, and browser bridge
A browser adapter that exposes profile and authenticated account/workspace metadata without exposing secrets
A hard identity-drift gate evaluated immediately before mutation
Fixtures and tests for multiple browser profiles, delegated tenants, SSO redirects, and account switching

proposals.user_asks: “Before you act, tell me what you can actually reach right now, what is stale or offline, and whether the result will be verified. If a surface drops out, keep the request safe and tell me what remains.”
proposals.why_useful: The owner currently gets plausible success even when UI input cannot reach the screen, while the browser bridge can be offline with queued commands. This turns raw diagnostics into a dependable decision: use a granted AppleScript route, queue work, ask for confirmation, or refuse to claim completion. It is especially valuable from the pendant, where the owner cannot inspect dashboards.
proposals.model_tier: Cheap background/state model compiles the reachability snapshot and freshness/confidence; realtime is used only for the short spoken verdict and any owner clarification. No expensive reasoning is needed unless the requested action is ambiguous.
proposals.latency_budget: Under 1 second for cached status; under 3 seconds for a fresh probe. The owner hears one sentence plus an optional actionable fallback.
proposals.cost_estimate: Near-zero model cost for typed status evaluation; occasional realtime token cost for the spoken explanation. Dominant cost is a fresh Mac/bridge probe, not inference.
proposals.security_concerns: Expose capability classes and freshness, not bearer tokens, private URLs, or secret memory. Never imply an action succeeded from a local receipt when uiActionsWillReachTheScreen=false. Any fallback that sends, deletes, purchases, or changes external state still requires the owner's existing confirmation policy.
missing: A unified typed reachability witness joining /observe, /ops/status, /browser/status, relay status, and recent /pipeline or /jobs receipts with one timestamp/confidence/expiry per claim
A pre-action gate that consumes that witness and routes around an unavailable surface
A concise pendant protocol for saying queued, blocked, attempted-but-unverified, and externally-verified as distinct outcomes

proposals.user_asks: “If I made this an automatic rule, show me what you would have done over the last week, which cases would have needed my approval, and where the rule would have gone wrong—without actually changing anything.”
proposals.why_useful: The owner is accumulating routines and delegated jobs, but cannot safely tell whether a new automation policy matches their real life. A replay against prior Mac jobs, browser observations, pendant interruptions, and receipts makes autonomy testable before it becomes surprising. It turns repeated one-off confirmations into evidence rather than silently learning permission.
proposals.model_tier: Background model performs deterministic event filtering and a cheaper batch simulation; use realtime only to answer a follow-up question or read the short result aloud. High-cost reasoning is reserved for ambiguous counterfactuals.
proposals.latency_budget: A seven-day replay in 5–15 seconds on the Mac/relay; a spoken summary in under 2 seconds after results are ready. No action is taken during simulation.
proposals.cost_estimate: Low batch-model cost; most work is local replay over logs and receipts. Dominant cost is browser page re-reads only when historical evidence is absent, and those reads should be labeled as estimates.
proposals.security_concerns: Default to local redacted event features and never upload email/page contents unless the owner explicitly includes them. Simulations must be read-only, clearly marked hypothetical, and separate from executable jobs. Secret values and destructive actions are represented as categories, not payloads.
missing: A deterministic counterfactual runner that replays historical events through a candidate policy and records hypothetical actions
A normalized event stream joining pendant bookmarks/alerts, Mac jobs, browser commands, receipts, and routine runs with retention and redaction
A dashboard and pendant report that distinguish observed historical evidence from inferred outcomes and let the owner approve a policy only after review

proposals.user_asks: “Protect my energy this week: look across my calendar, reminders, unfinished work, travel, and recent interruptions; show me where the load is likely to exceed what I can realistically do, then suggest specific swaps or deferrals for my approval.”
proposals.why_useful: The owner does not need another chronological briefing—they need judgment about capacity. Today the system can read pieces of their schedule and act on individual items, but cannot form a privacy-preserving load estimate, explain which commitments collide, or propose a humane plan that accounts for recovery time and interruption cost. This would help prevent overcommitment before it becomes an emergency.
proposals.model_tier: Use a cheap background model for extraction, clustering, and load estimation; use the expensive realtime tier only if the owner asks for a conversational tradeoff discussion. The default result is a short generated plan, not live reasoning.
proposals.latency_budget: Generate overnight or on demand in 10–30 seconds; deliver a 30-second spoken summary. Proposed calendar/reminder edits remain pending until approval.
proposals.cost_estimate: Low batch inference cost; the dominant cost is authenticated reads of calendars, task systems, and private browser pages. Cache normalized facts with short TTLs and re-read only changed sources.
proposals.security_concerns: Keep raw mail and page text on the Mac whenever possible; send the relay only redacted commitment entities, times, durations, and sensitivity labels. Never infer health or emotional diagnoses. Do not cancel, decline, reschedule, or message anyone without explicit approval. Let the owner exclude sources or categories.
missing: A personal capacity model that learns estimated effort, transition time, recovery time, and interruption cost without diagnosing the owner
A cross-source commitment graph that identifies collisions and distinguishes hard obligations from negotiable intentions
A proposal engine that produces reversible swaps/deferrals with explicit tradeoffs and approval-ready calendar/reminder changes
A feedback loop recording whether the predicted load was useful, without silently converting feedback into permissions

proposals.user_asks: “I got interrupted—pick up exactly where I left off.” The pendant should give me a 20-second resume briefing, reopen the relevant Mac document and browser tabs, and offer the single next step without repeating work or sending anything.
proposals.why_useful: Real interruptions currently erase the thread between a spoken intention, a private browser page, and Mac work. This would make the wearable a continuity anchor: I can leave a meeting, lose connectivity, or switch devices and return to the exact unfinished decision with evidence and a safe next action.
proposals.model_tier: Use the realtime tier only to capture the interruption marker and speak the short resume brief. Use a cheaper background model to compile the packet and reconcile job/session/browser evidence; use deterministic code for ordering, deduplication, and safety checks.
proposals.latency_budget: On the next pendant interaction, acknowledge in under 300 ms from a locally cached marker. Compile or refresh the packet in 2–5 s; if a surface is offline, say so and resume from the last verified checkpoint rather than blocking.
proposals.cost_estimate: About $0.005–$0.03 per resume, dominated by background summarization of changed evidence; near-zero when the cached packet is still fresh. Audio generation is a smaller additional cost.
proposals.security_concerns: The packet can expose sensitive page titles, mail, or documents, so store pointers and short redacted excerpts rather than full page content, apply per-source TTLs, and keep it device/owner scoped. Never replay secrets aloud by default. Reopening is reversible; any send, delete, purchase, or mutation still requires the existing confirmation gate. If evidence is stale or agents disagree, present uncertainty and ask one clarification instead of inventing continuity.
missing: A durable intent-continuity record with explicit interruption and checkpoint events across pendant, relay, Mac jobs, and browser sessions.
A resume-packet compiler that links the spoken intent to tab IDs, Mac paths, job IDs, receipts, and the last confirmed step, with freshness and redaction.
A local/offline pendant marker and reconnect reconciliation so an interruption survives a dropped link.
A one-tap/spoken “resume / discard / snooze” interaction and a dashboard showing packet provenance.

proposals.user_asks: “What promises have I made recently that I’m quietly failing to keep?” Give me a private, evidence-linked list of commitments inferred from my conversations, calendar, notes, and logged-in pages; rank the ones whose silence is most likely to hurt someone, and prepare a repair plan without contacting anyone.
proposals.why_useful: Today the owner can remember explicit reminders, but no system can notice the human commitments that were casually spoken or implied (“I’ll send that tonight,” “let’s meet next week”) and then compare them with what actually happened. This protects relationships and reputation without turning the assistant into an autonomous sender.
proposals.model_tier: Use a cheaper background model for nightly extraction and reconciliation; use realtime only when the owner asks for the private spoken summary. Deterministic code handles dates, evidence links, deduplication, and ranking inputs.
proposals.latency_budget: Nightly scan completes within 2 minutes in the background; an on-demand spoken answer starts in under 1 second from the cached ledger and refreshes in under 10 seconds if sources are online.
proposals.cost_estimate: Roughly $0.02–$0.10 per nightly scan depending on message/page volume; most cost is extracting candidate commitments. Incremental refreshes should be far cheaper through hashes and source cursors.
proposals.security_concerns: This is unusually sensitive social inference. Keep raw messages and page contents on the Mac/browser session, store only a redacted claim, source pointer, confidence, and expiry in the relay, and let the owner exclude people/accounts. Never present an inference as fact: say “possible promise,” quote the minimal evidence privately, and allow dismiss/correct. No message, reminder, or calendar mutation occurs without explicit approval.
missing: A commitment-specific evidence schema distinguishing explicit promises, tentative ideas, and ordinary plans.
Cross-surface extraction connectors for spoken pendant events, AppleScript-readable Mail/Messages/Calendar/Notes, and authenticated browser pages, with source cursors and deletion propagation.
A reconciliation job that marks commitments kept, deferred, expired, or unresolved without treating absence of evidence as failure.
A private review UI and voice flow for confirm, dismiss, snooze, redact, and repair-plan generation.

proposals.user_asks: “If the pendant’s audio path breaks or changes quality, keep the conversation going without making me repeat myself, and tell me clearly what happened.”
proposals.why_useful: The current device captures at 15,625 Hz, uplinks Opus at 16 kHz, and plays back at 24 kHz; the observed pipeline has already shown a 15,625-Hz input beside a 24-kHz output. Today that mismatch can look like a successful turn while the owner hears degraded audio or loses an utterance. This capability makes audio failure recoverable instead of silently conversationally expensive.
proposals.model_tier: Realtime model only for the short session-health decision and the owner's one-sentence alert; a cheaper background model summarizes diagnostics and drafts a bug report after the session. Firmware/relay contract checks are deterministic and do not call a model.
proposals.latency_budget: A preflight probe must complete in under 300 ms before speaking. On a mid-session fault, locally preserve the current utterance, announce fallback within 1 s, and resume via text or a re-established audio contract without replaying already acknowledged turns.
proposals.cost_estimate: Negligible model cost for healthy sessions; roughly one short realtime turn only on a fault, plus a cheap background diagnostic summary. Storage and relay overhead are small fixed-size telemetry records, not raw audio by default.
proposals.security_concerns: Do not upload raw probe audio or buffered speech unless the owner explicitly asks for a bug report. Send sample-rate/codec/sequence metadata and hashes by default; encrypt any owner-approved diagnostic clip, expire it quickly, and require confirmation before sharing it off-device or attaching it to an issue.
missing: A negotiated, typed audio-session contract shared by firmware, relay, and playback bridge
A small pendant utterance ring buffer that survives a dropped link and marks exactly which frames were acknowledged
A deterministic fallback transport/UI on the pendant (LED/button plus relay text response)
A Mac diagnostic collector that can turn a failed contract into a repairable bug report

proposals.user_asks: “Put me in a private bubble when I ask: keep sensitive answers and account details off nearby screens and speakers, let me review or act through the pendant, and automatically restore my normal workspace when I leave private mode.”
proposals.why_useful: A wearable assistant sits in rooms where other people can hear, while the Mac and authenticated browser expose far more than the owner intended. Today privacy is a conversational promise, not an enforced cross-surface state. A real private bubble lets the owner use the hive mind in public, at work, or beside family without leaking a password, medical detail, message, or account page through the wrong surface.
proposals.model_tier: Use deterministic policy and surface controls for entry, redaction, routing, and exit; use the realtime model only to classify the requested answer's sensitivity when no explicit label exists. A cheap background model may audit the session afterward, but must not receive raw private content merely to enforce the bubble.
proposals.latency_budget: Enter within 500 ms of a button press or explicit phrase, acknowledge privately through the pendant, and enforce screen/audio suppression before any sensitive result is rendered. Exit on explicit command or a configurable timeout, with a 1-second restoration budget.
proposals.cost_estimate: Near-zero model cost for explicit mode changes; occasional short realtime classification for unlabeled content. Main cost is engineering and OS/browser integration, not tokens.
proposals.security_concerns: The mode must fail closed: if the Mac or browser cannot attest that masking/muting succeeded, do not display or speak sensitive content there. Keep the mode state and sensitivity labels encrypted, do not log raw answers or screenshots, and require confirmation before opening the bubble to a new surface. A physical long-press should override accidental voice exit.
missing: A signed, shared privacy-mode lease with owner-selected sensitivity classes and expiry
Mac and browser adapters that can attest to screen masking, notification suppression, tab redaction, and speaker routing rather than merely claiming success
A pendant-local indicator and button gesture that work when the network is down
A policy engine that separates private answer delivery from private action execution and records only a minimal proof receipt

proposals.user_asks: When I say “pause this and come back later,” save exactly where we are across my pendant, Mac, and browser, then later give me a 20-second spoken recap and let me resume without reconstructing the task.
proposals.why_useful: Real interruptions currently destroy context: the owner has to remember which tabs, draft, approval, and audio item were in progress. This would turn an interruption into a safe handoff, preserving the pending action without sending or submitting anything accidentally.
proposals.model_tier: Use the cheap background model to compile the handoff and recap; use realtime only when the owner asks to resume or correct it. No model call is needed for the raw snapshot.
proposals.latency_budget: Capture in under 2 seconds; later recap begins within 1 second of the owner's request. Compilation can finish asynchronously in 5–15 seconds.
proposals.cost_estimate: About $0.001–$0.01 per handoff depending on recap length; dominant cost is the one short background summarization, not state capture.
proposals.security_concerns: The packet may contain private page text, draft contents, and task identifiers. Encrypt at rest, apply short retention (for example 7 days), omit secrets and full page bodies by default, and require confirmation before resuming any irreversible step. If a tab, job, or approval changed, say so and stop rather than replaying stale intent.
missing: A durable cross-surface handoff record linking pendant audio position, relay job id, Mac job id, browser session/tab ids, pending approval, and explicit next action
A resume validator that compares the saved evidence/version with current browser and Mac state
A pendant resume control that can announce the recap and select resume, inspect, or discard offline

proposals.user_asks: Make sure my scheduled brief actually reaches me. If the pendant cannot play it, keep a durable copy, retry when the link returns, and tell me exactly what was missed instead of claiming it was delivered.
proposals.why_useful: A completed background job is not the same as a useful result in the owner's ears. This closes the real-world gap between research, TTS, transport, and playback, especially when the pendant is offline or a stream underruns.
proposals.model_tier: No expensive reasoning for the normal path: deterministic delivery receipts and a cheap background repair policy. Use realtime only to explain a failure or offer the queued item.
proposals.latency_budget: Acknowledge enqueue immediately; detect a failed or unconfirmed delivery within 10 seconds; retry on reconnect without waking the owner unless the item is marked urgent.
proposals.cost_estimate: Usually below $0.001 per item for metadata and retry; TTS/audio transfer dominates, and retries should reuse the retained audio rather than regenerate it.
proposals.security_concerns: Audio briefings can contain private calendar/mail data. Encrypt retained objects, use per-item expiry and deletion, never expose audio URLs in spoken logs, and distinguish delivered-to-device from actually-played. Urgent retries need an owner-configurable quiet-hours policy.
missing: A durable delivery state machine with hop-level receipts: generated, transferred, decoded, buffered, played, failed, and expired
A pendant-side playback acknowledgement/underrun event and reconnect replay cursor
A relay watchdog that reconciles scheduled-job completion with audio delivery, deduplicates retries, and produces a human-readable missed-item receipt

proposals.user_asks: I’m with other people—switch to discreet mode. From now on, keep private names, message text, account details, and page contents off the speaker and show me only safe summaries or a vibration cue until I turn it off.
proposals.why_useful: The pendant is worn in public, where a normally helpful spoken answer can disclose sensitive information. One explicit physical mode should constrain every surface, not just the voice reply, and should survive a dropped connection.
proposals.model_tier: Deterministic policy enforcement and redaction first; a small background model may classify a response's disclosure risk. Realtime is only for the short safe spoken response.
proposals.latency_budget: The physical toggle must take effect locally in under 100 ms and propagate to relay/Mac/browser within 2 seconds. No network round trip may be required to suppress pendant playback.
proposals.cost_estimate: Negligible per toggle; modest background classification cost only for ambiguous generated content, approximately $0.0005–$0.003 per response.
proposals.security_concerns: Fail closed on unknown mode state: suppress content rather than speak it. Store only mode transitions, not the private text used for redaction. Browser and Mac agents must receive the policy before extraction or display, and the owner must explicitly turn the mode off.
missing: A pendant-local discreet-mode latch and visual/haptic confirmation
A signed policy token propagated to relay, Mac, and browser that gates extraction, display, TTS, and queued replay
A redaction contract with tested categories (people, message bodies, account identifiers, secrets) and an owner-visible audit of what was withheld

proposals.user_asks: I lost my pendant. Lock it and revoke its access everywhere now—stop queued audio, invalidate browser and Mac control, and tell me what was successfully frozen. If it comes back, make me re-pair it before anything resumes.
proposals.why_useful: A wearable carries private audio and acts as an authenticated doorway into the owner's Mac and logged-in browser. Losing it should not leave previously queued briefings playable or an unattended device able to authorize actions.
proposals.model_tier: Use deterministic security logic and signed revocation events; no language-model call is needed except an optional short explanation of the freeze receipt.
proposals.latency_budget: Relay-side revocation within 1 second; propagate to Mac and browser within 5 seconds. The pendant should enter a local locked state on its next contact and never resume automatically after reconnect.
proposals.cost_estimate: Negligible API cost; one small durable security event and delivery receipt per lock/unlock. Main engineering cost is protocol and recovery testing.
proposals.security_concerns: Revocation must be authenticated through a second trusted channel, such as the owner's Mac or an already-authenticated voice session, and must be idempotent. Do not reveal private queued-item names in the lock receipt. Offline pendant behavior needs a local lock timeout or owner-set PIN, with secure deletion of cached audio and credentials.
missing: A device identity and key lifecycle with per-pendant certificates, rotation, and a revocation list
A relay-to-Mac/browser kill switch that cancels queued commands and invalidates active sessions, not merely future requests
A pendant secure-lock state with encrypted cache wipe, reconnect quarantine, and explicit re-pairing ceremony
A signed, cross-surface freeze receipt proving which queues, sessions, and credentials were actually revoked

proposals.user_asks: “Give me one useful update, not five separate briefings—and if I miss it, catch me up without repeating what I already heard.”
proposals.why_useful: The owner currently has several successful daily routines at overlapping times (morning brief, calendar/mail/files, news/research) but no shared attention ledger. This would merge discoveries across Mac, authenticated browser, relay, and pendant into one expiring, prioritized stream; suppress duplicates, remember spoken/acknowledged items, and replay only still-actionable items after a missed connection.
surfaces: relay-realtime receives a live spoken item or a one-button request for catch-up and plays the selected short item
mac-planner runs scheduled collection via /routines/:routineId/run, /briefing, /research and reads machine state through /machine-context
browser-extension reads owner-private tabs through browser_run_actions and POST /research {mode:"page"} without sending or submitting
relay persists a compact attention ledger and delivery receipts, while the Mac leaves a cited review queue/audio artifact for later
proposals.model_tier: Background/scheduled collection uses a cheaper non-realtime model; realtime is used only to choose and phrase the next item during a live pendant interaction. Deduplication and expiry should be deterministic before model summarization.
proposals.latency_budget: Scheduled merge under 30 seconds after source jobs complete; live catch-up decision under 1 second from the compact ledger, with audio beginning within 2 seconds. If the Mac or browser is offline, deliver the last trusted pending item and mark it stale rather than inventing freshness.
proposals.cost_estimate: About $0.01–$0.05 per daily merge, dominated by summarizing genuinely new source text; live selection is a few hundred tokens on the realtime tier. Deterministic hashing, TTL, and receipt checks should cost effectively zero.
proposals.security_concerns: Private browser extracts and calendar/mail content leave the Mac only as compact fact snippets and citations; redact secrets and preserve source sensitivity. Never auto-send mail, submit forms, buy, or delete. A spoken 'skip' or button press should acknowledge only the current item, not erase its source. Require confirmation for any suggested destructive or external action.
missing: A durable cross-surface attention-item schema with source, semantic fingerprint, urgency, expiry, and delivery/acknowledgement receipts
A timezone/quiet-hours authority: current owner preference says America/Chicago while machine-context reports America/New_York
A pendant-local queue/ack marker that survives LTE-M drops and prevents replay storms
A merge endpoint or worker job that can consume existing briefing/research/routine outputs without re-running expensive source collection

proposals.user_asks: “When you do something for me, don’t just say it ran—tell me whether the outside world actually reflects the result, and warn me if it didn’t.”
proposals.why_useful: Today an action can produce a local execution receipt while the real service remains pending, rejects it, changes it, or silently fails. The owner should receive a plain-language outcome such as confirmed, awaiting external confirmation, or could not verify—with the evidence and the next safe step—rather than false closure.
surfaces: relay-realtime asks for approval when a corrective or retry action could have external side effects and speaks the short outcome
mac-planner executes reversible preparation and reads local receipts, mail, calendar, and notifications through the Mac agent
browser-extension revisits the exact authenticated tab/session and checks the service’s postcondition (confirmation number, changed status, sent-state, or error)
relay remains the durable coordinator that correlates intent, execution receipt, and independent postcondition evidence across the Mac and browser
proposals.model_tier: Use deterministic postcondition checks and typed evidence first; use the cheaper background model to map a goal to likely confirmation signals. Reserve realtime for the owner-facing explanation or an approval question, never for background polling.
proposals.latency_budget: Immediate local result in under 2 seconds; verify fast services within 10 seconds and slow services by scheduled follow-up. If verification is unavailable, say so explicitly and do not claim success.
proposals.cost_estimate: Roughly $0.005–$0.03 per completed action, dominated by one authenticated page revisit or notification read; deterministic checks and receipt correlation are negligible. Long-running checks should be scheduled/background, not realtime.
proposals.security_concerns: Revisiting authenticated pages exposes only the minimum needed fields to the coordinator; retain hashes/snippets rather than whole pages. Never retry a potentially duplicate purchase, message, deletion, or submission automatically. Require confirmation before any retry or compensating action, and show the evidence source and timestamp.
missing: A typed intent-to-postcondition contract (expected state, acceptable variants, timeout, and whether duplicate retry is dangerous)
A durable verifier that can reattach to the original browser tab/session or read the relevant Mac notification/email without confusing an old confirmation
A state machine separating locally executed, externally accepted, externally completed, and unverifiable
A user-visible escalation path on the pendant for failed or ambiguous outcomes

proposals.user_asks: “For anything important, have two independent parts of my system agree it happened—or keep it pending and bring me the disagreement.”
proposals.why_useful: A single receipt, DOM click, or UI observation can be falsely positive. An evidence quorum makes high-stakes personal actions dependable: for example, a Mac calendar write is checked by Calendar readback plus a durable job record; a browser submission is checked by the confirmation page plus a later authenticated record. The pendant tells the owner 'confirmed by two sources' or 'pending: sources disagree,' never silently upgrading an attempt to truth.
proposals.model_tier: Cheap deterministic quorum rules first; background planner only resolves entity matching or semantic disagreement; realtime speaks the concise result and asks for help only when the conflict cannot be resolved. No expensive model for routine matching.
proposals.latency_budget: Local two-source checks <1 s; browser/account confirmation 3–10 s. The pendant can say 'still checking' immediately, then deliver a result asynchronously through relay when the owner walks away.
proposals.cost_estimate: <$0.002 typical (mostly two local/browser reads); planner escalation 2–4k tokens only for ambiguous semantic conflicts. Storage is small: signed evidence pointers, hashes, timestamps, and a bounded disagreement record.
proposals.security_concerns: Sources must be genuinely independent (not two views of the same untrusted click result). Store hashes and minimal excerpts, not whole private pages. For money, messages, deletion, or external submissions, quorum confirms outcome but never replaces owner approval. Expose the exact sources, freshness, and missing witness in the dashboard and spoken response.
missing: A typed evidence-witness and independence model (source, claim, timestamp, freshness, confidence, correlation group)
Per-action quorum policies by consequence class, with a safe pending state and expiry rather than auto-retry
Cross-surface disagreement records and a repair workflow that can request a fresh read without repeating the write
Pendant/relay protocol for announcing pending, confirmed, and disputed outcomes after link loss

proposals.user_asks: “When I actually leave home, give me a two-minute departure check tailored to where I’m going—only interrupt me for something I can still fix, and keep the rest queued.”
proposals.why_useful: A scheduled morning briefing arrives at the wrong moment and a generic meeting brief does not know whether the owner has physically started leaving. This would connect the wearable’s real-world transition with the Mac’s live commitments and private browser context: catch the forgotten badge, medication, document, or travel change while there is still time to act, without turning every reminder into noise.
proposals.model_tier: Use a cheap event classifier and deterministic checklist first. Use a background planner to combine calendar, travel, and unfinished-job facts; reserve realtime for one concise, interruptible spoken alert.
proposals.latency_budget: Detect departure within 10–30 seconds; produce a first actionable check within 5 seconds of the event. Anything requiring authenticated browser reads can arrive asynchronously, with no blocking of movement.
proposals.cost_estimate: Usually <$0.003 per departure, dominated by one planner call and private-account reads; deterministic local checks should be free. Battery and cellular sensing are the main non-API costs.
proposals.security_concerns: Location and routine inference are highly sensitive. Keep raw location on the pendant or Mac, send only a coarse transition and destination class to relay, and make the feature opt-in with per-place quiet rules. Never announce sensitive calendar or health details aloud when others may be present; require confirmation before sending or changing anything.
missing: A reliable departure-event source: pendant motion/proximity/GNSS or a paired-phone geofence, with local privacy filtering
A destination and time-window resolver joining calendar, travel, tasks, and unfinished cross-surface jobs
A ranked 'still fixable before leaving' checklist with expiry and quiet/social-context rules
A low-interruption pendant interaction for dismiss, defer, or ask-for-more without opening the Mac

proposals.user_asks: “Stop everything.” (or long-press the pendant button) should immediately silence the pendant, freeze new automation, cancel queued Mac/browser work, and give me a private receipt of what was stopped; “resume” should show the exact next unverified steps before anything continues.
proposals.why_useful: A person wearing an agent needs a physical, reliable boundary when a meeting starts, a private conversation begins, or an automation looks wrong. This is stronger than a conversational promise: it works during a dropped link, prevents queued actions from racing ahead, and makes trust recoverable rather than requiring the owner to remember which surface is active.
proposals.model_tier: No expensive model for the stop path; pendant firmware and relay perform deterministic cancellation. Use the cheap background tier only to summarize the stopped jobs. Use realtime only to speak the one-sentence receipt or ask for resume confirmation.
proposals.latency_budget: Local mute/LED state under 100 ms; relay cancellation and browser/Mac freeze target under 1 s when linked. Offline, the pendant remains muted and records a bounded stop marker until reconnect. Resume requires an explicit owner action and a short evidence/readback pass, not model deliberation.
proposals.cost_estimate: Near-zero API cost for stop/cancel; one short receipt generation is typically <$0.01 and can be omitted. Engineering cost is a firmware event plus authenticated relay fan-out and adapters for existing job/browser/pipeline stores.
proposals.security_concerns: The stop command must be accepted locally without network and authenticated on reconnect; it must not transmit microphone audio while latched. Cancellation should be idempotent and append-only, and receipts should contain job IDs/status—not page contents or secrets. “Resume” must never replay an irreversible step; it must require fresh preconditions and confirmation for send/delete/purchase.
missing: A pendant-local privacy latch with long-press debounce and persistent stop marker (single button/LED is available, but this behavior is not established).
A relay-wide freeze token checked by every new job/action and fan-out cancellation to Mac jobs, browser commands, and audio pipelines.
A durable stop/resume receipt schema that integrates faculty-action's requested/attempted/witnessed/confirmed checkpoint protocol and exposes the next unverified step.
A small owner-facing resume review UI/audio flow; macOS Accessibility remains unnecessary because cancellation can use the existing authenticated routes.

proposals.user_asks: “Private mode” should follow me across the pendant, Mac, and browser: when I tap the pendant or enter a sensitive calendar context, the system should stop speaking private content aloud, prevent private page text from entering model context, pause background jobs that could expose it, and show me a small local indication of the active boundary. When I leave, it should not silently resume disclosure; it should give me a concise review of what was withheld and let me restore normal mode.
proposals.why_useful: Today privacy is a collection of per-surface settings, so the owner must remember whether the pendant is audible, which browser tabs are logged in, and which background jobs are running. A single privacy boundary that travels with the person would let them use an always-listening assistant around other people without gambling that one surface forgot the rule. The important behavior is omission and fail-closed handling, not merely deleting logs afterward.
proposals.model_tier: Deterministic policy evaluation and redaction should handle the hot path; use a cheaper background model to summarize withheld items. Realtime should speak only a generic confirmation such as “Private mode is on,” never the protected content. No model call is needed to enforce the boundary.
proposals.latency_budget: Pendant indication and local microphone/playback policy under 100 ms. Relay and Mac/browser policy propagation under 1 s when connected. On link loss, the pendant remains private and the Mac/browser agents fail closed until an explicit owner-controlled rejoin.
proposals.cost_estimate: Negligible inference cost on enforcement; occasional background summaries are <$0.01 per mode transition. Main cost is a shared policy protocol, redaction boundary in context assembly, and integration tests across reconnects and tab/job races.
proposals.security_concerns: A sensitive mode must not be inferred solely from an untrusted page title or calendar text; explicit pendant action always wins. Store only mode, scope, timestamps, and reason—not protected content. Existing bearer-authenticated sessions need per-mode capability tokens, and every withheld/allowed decision needs an auditable reason. Leaving private mode must require an explicit tap or spoken confirmation and must not replay queued speech or actions automatically.
missing: A signed, device-originated privacy-mode token with scope (audio, browser, Mac jobs, context) and monotonic expiry/revocation.
A policy enforcement point before transcription, before model-context projection, before TTS, and before browser/Mac job execution; current surfaces do not share one fail-closed token.
A redacted withheld-items ledger that can report counts and sources without retaining their contents.
A pendant-local privacy state machine and distinct LED/vibration/audio indication; it must survive a dropped link and reboot safely.
A reconnect protocol that revalidates every paused job and speech item instead of replaying stale private material.

proposals.user_asks: “Did that actually happen?” — for any task you carried out, verify it across the relevant surfaces and tell me in one short spoken sentence whether it is verified, contradicted, or still unknown, with the reason and the next safe step.
proposals.why_useful: Today a Mac action can return success while doing nothing, browser commands can remain pending, and pipeline runs can look terminal while staying processing. The owner should never have to infer reality from an optimistic receipt. This turns the hive into a trustworthy assistant: it checks the world after acting, not merely its own logs.
surfaces: faculty-action creates a typed action/receipt record with one request_id and expected postcondition

faculty-perception independently reads the Mac observation/permissions state, AppleScript-readable entities, browser session/tab state, and pipeline/job state, then compares observed facts to the expected postcondition
mac-planner uses granted AppleScript routes for Calendar, Mail, Finder, Notes, Messages, Safari, and Chrome where available; browser-extension reads authenticated tabs when online
relay-realtime delivers a compact spoken verdict to the pendant, with a cited detail available on the Mac workbench
unified preserves the verdict, evidence timestamps, contradiction, and retry/recovery recommendation as one conversation state
proposals.model_tier: Background/cheap model for polling, normalization, and evidence comparison; realtime model only to interpret an ambiguous user question or speak the final one-sentence verdict.
proposals.latency_budget: Routine reversible actions: 1–3 seconds after the action receipt, then up to 15 seconds for delayed surfaces; say “still checking” rather than block. High-impact actions require the verdict before any send/delete/purchase confirmation. No Accessibility or Screen Recording is required for the AppleScript/browser-readable path; GUI-only tasks remain explicitly unknown/blocked.
proposals.cost_estimate: Roughly $0.001–$0.01 per verification depending on number of surfaces and whether an LLM is needed; most checks are typed comparisons and local reads. Audio delivery and durable evidence storage dominate operational cost, not inference.
proposals.security_concerns: Evidence must be minimized and scoped to the request: store hashes/snippets and provenance, not whole private pages or mail bodies by default. Never treat an optimistic receipt as proof. Contradicted or unknown must not silently retry an irreversible action; ask for confirmation. Authenticated browser content stays on the local agent/workbench unless the owner explicitly requests a cloud summary.
missing: A durable expected-postcondition schema attached to every action (entity, field, before, expected-after, deadline, and acceptable evidence sources).
A read-only cross-surface evidence reconciler that emits verified/contradicted/unknown with confidence, freshness, and contradiction reasons.
A delayed-observation watcher for jobs and browser commands so processing/pending states are revisited without another voice turn.
A small local workbench artifact and pendant receipt format for evidence citations and recovery actions.

proposals.user_asks: “Learn what worked.” After I make a consequential choice through the pendant, Mac, or a logged-in browser, check the result later, ask me once whether it worked for me, and use that answer to improve future recommendations—without keeping the private source material.
proposals.why_useful: Assistants currently remember requests and receipts, but not whether their choices actually helped. The owner should not have to repeat durable preferences such as which meeting buffers, vendors, reply styles, or travel tradeoffs are genuinely good for them. This creates a personal feedback loop from real outcomes rather than guesses or surveillance.
surfaces: faculty-action records a compact prediction at decision time: goal, chosen option, expected benefit, expected downside, and review date; it does not retain full message/page contents
mac-planner and browser-extension later read only the minimum outcome signals from Calendar, Mail, browser tabs, or local files, using the surface that owns the state
faculty-perception compares outcome signals with the prediction and marks outcome evidence as positive, negative, mixed, or unavailable
relay-realtime asks the pendant one short follow-up at a suitable interruption window; the owner can answer satisfied, not satisfied, or skip
unified updates a preference model with the answer and provenance, while faculty-judgement uses it as a soft recommendation—not an automatic rule—on future cross-surface plans
proposals.model_tier: Background/cheap model for scheduled outcome checks and preference updates; realtime model only for the brief follow-up conversation or ambiguity resolution.
proposals.latency_budget: No blocking of the original action. Outcome checks run at the review date or when a relevant surface changes. The spoken follow-up is under 10 seconds and can be deferred indefinitely.
proposals.cost_estimate: About $0.001–$0.02 per reviewed decision, mostly local extraction and occasional summarization; compact preference updates are far cheaper than resending source context.
proposals.security_concerns: Store only structured predictions, outcome labels, and provenance hashes—not raw email, page, or calendar content. Never infer sensitive traits from outcomes. Ask before using a learned preference for a consequential action, and let the owner inspect, correct, or delete each learned preference.
missing: A decision-outcome record linking an action to a future review date and predicted result
Outcome probes that can extract minimal signals without copying private source content
A preference ledger with confidence, expiry, evidence, and explicit owner correction
A quiet follow-up scheduler that avoids repeatedly interrupting the owner
A model-routing rule that keeps this asynchronous and cheap

proposals.user_asks: “Before I head out, make sure this appointment or trip is actually ready.”
proposals.why_useful: It prevents the costly failures a generic morning brief misses: a calendar time that differs from the booking, a changed gate or address buried in logged-in mail, a missing preparation item, or weather/traffic that changes when the owner must leave. The pendant gives a natural, hands-free request; the relay can continue checking after the owner walks away; the Mac and authenticated browser can inspect private sources together.
