depends_on: A signed pendant event envelope and reconnect state reconciliation
Relay enforcement that distinguishes hardware mute from software pause
Cross-surface cancellation of queued audio and speech-dependent jobs
A product pendant revision beyond the current nRF9160 development kit

changes.change: Create a durable obligation-and-conflict event layer between existing context graph/research/briefing routes: normalize commitments from Calendar, Mail, local notes, and authenticated browser extracts into typed obligations; emit idempotent conflict events with source citations, temporal/travel constraints, confidence, expiry, and a ranked set of reversible options. Persist a draft-only resolution packet that the Mac workbench and pendant queue can consume, with explicit owner approval required for any external mutation.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: The owner gets an early, explainable warning that two promises cannot both be kept, plus a ready way out, rather than discovering the collision during a meeting or after a deadline. It turns existing disconnected reads and briefs into dependable life coordination.
changes.effort: Medium-high: schema and D1/R2 persistence, Calendar/Mail/notes/browser adapters, deterministic temporal rules, conflict deduplication, and a review/approval packet rendered by Mac and pendant. Start with calendar + browser deadlines, then add mail and local files.
changes.risk: False conflicts could create alert fatigue; mitigate with confidence thresholds, quiet-hour queueing, evidence links, and a dismiss/merge feedback loop. Never execute a cancellation, send, or reschedule from the detector. If a source is unavailable, mark the conflict incomplete rather than infer absence.
changes.cost_impact: Low recurring storage and rule-evaluation cost; background model extraction is the dominant API cost, approximately cents per scan. No new hardware required.
changes.latency_impact: Event ingestion is near-real-time where hooks exist; reconciliation is seconds to minutes. Spoken delivery waits for a stable packet and should remain under 3 seconds after it is queued.
changes.security_impact: Sensitive source text stays bounded and provenance-tagged; spoken output uses redacted summaries. Approval packets must preserve the exact before/after effect and source evidence, and expired source extracts must be deleted on the retention policy.
depends_on: Durable typed context projection rather than hand-written fleetContext
Authenticated browser command/session reliability and truthful offline status
A durable review queue with acknowledgment, expiry, and approval gates
Calendar/Mail event or polling adapters on the Mac agent

changes.change: Add a negotiation-packet compiler and consequence simulator that accepts a cited incoming request from Mail/browser, resolves only the owner's relevant calendar/account commitments, and produces three explicitly labeled reply variants (accept, counter, decline). For each variant, compute the exact new date, money, access, or communication commitments it would create, show source evidence and unresolved assumptions, and emit an immutable approval token tied to the exact text. Outbound adapters must reject any send or submit lacking that token.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: The owner can respond confidently to difficult requests without manually reconstructing context or accidentally agreeing to something hidden in a polished draft. They see the consequences before committing and can approve only the exact reply they intend.
changes.effort: Medium: packet schema, evidence joiner, deterministic consequence rules, text/version hashing, and adapters for Mac Mail and authenticated browser forms; a Mac review surface and pendant summary are needed.
changes.risk: The model may miss an obligation or misread leverage; expose uncertainty and source excerpts, offer no-answer/ask-for-time variants, and fail closed when evidence is incomplete. Version hashes prevent a later edit from being sent under an earlier approval.
changes.cost_impact: Small persistent storage and hashing cost; roughly cents per packet for extraction and alternatives, with no recurring cost after approval.
changes.latency_impact: Compilation takes tens of seconds for local sources and minutes for multiple private tabs; exact-text approval and send can be immediate once the packet is ready.
changes.security_impact: Sensitive negotiations stay scoped to the selected thread and sources, with redacted voice summaries and short-lived packet retention. Approval tokens are single-use, audience-bound, and cannot authorize unrelated actions.
depends_on: A stable cross-surface source citation format
Draft-only Mac Mail and browser form adapters
Durable versioned approval records and truthful send receipts
Owner-configurable retention and disclosure boundaries

changes.change: Add a durable Handoff Envelope and Re-entry Arbiter between the existing event/capture, job, browser, and execution paths. On a pendant interruption, create one handoffId with the raw intent reference, normalized goal, constraints, uncertainty, stopping point, owner timezone/quiet hours, and expiry. Every downstream job, browser extraction, and prepared action must attach that handoffId and append typed evidence (source, timestamp, freshness, confidence) rather than returning an unlinked result. On reconnect or a chosen quiet window, the arbiter compiles a 3-field decision slate—what changed, what is blocked, next reversible step—and routes exactly one delivery to the pendant or Mac. Approval is a separate state transition; execution receipts and undo references close the same handoff. Expire or cancel must fan out idempotently to jobs and queued audio.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: The owner can say “hold this thought” once and later resume at the exact decision, even if they leave the Mac, lose the browser bridge, or cross an offline interval. They stop getting orphaned job completions and repeated reminders, and never mistake prepared work for approved action.
changes.effort: Medium-high: schema and event migration, idempotent fan-out/cancellation, one arbiter worker, and pendant reconnect handling; can ship read-only decision slates before enabling action execution.
changes.risk: A stale or wrongly merged handoff could prompt the owner about the wrong task. Mitigate with explicit handoff IDs, source/timestamp display, confidence thresholds, owner confirmation on ambiguous re-entry, expiry, and a global cancel. If a downstream surface disappears, preserve the handoff as blocked rather than silently completing it.
changes.cost_impact: Small durable storage and queue overhead; approximately one compact background-model call per handoff plus existing browser/Mac costs. No need to resend full transcripts.
changes.latency_impact: Sub-second acknowledgement; background processing is asynchronous. Re-entry compilation should be under 2 seconds from fresh evidence, with stale evidence clearly marked.
changes.security_impact: Keep raw private page text on the owning surface where possible; relay stores references, hashes, and minimal excerpts. Never place secrets in pendant audio. Approval tokens are single-use, scoped to handoffId and action hash.
depends_on: A typed cross-surface event schema with correlation IDs
A durable job cancellation/expiry primitive
A decision-slate and approval-state representation
A pendant reconnect/offline marker path

changes.change: Insert a Disclosure Preflight stage before /plan, browser extraction, model invocation, or /execute. It should build a typed manifest of every proposed input and destination (pendant, relay, model tier, Mac app, browser origin, external recipient), run local redaction on the Mac/extension, replace raw values with minimized excerpts or salted proof hashes, and issue a single-use disclosure token bound to the exact payload hash, destination set, and expiry. Downstream routes must reject requests without a matching token; any changed tab, target, field, or model destination invalidates it. Store only the manifest and approval decision in receipts, never the unredacted payload.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: The owner gets a real, enforceable boundary instead of a reassuring prompt: private account pages, unrelated messages, credentials, and personal files cannot silently become model context just because a task crossed surfaces. They can approve a useful minimized request without choosing between total automation and total refusal.
changes.effort: High: define the manifest schema, implement local scanners/redactors in the Mac and browser bridge, enforce token checks in relay routes, add safe failure behavior, and add compact pendant/dashboard rendering. Start with known credential/PII classes and expand classifiers after telemetry proves low false-negative rates.
changes.risk: Over-redaction can make tasks fail or produce misleading results; under-redaction is a privacy breach. Fail closed for secrets and unknown destinations, show what was omitted, and allow the owner to explicitly widen scope by category—not by blindly forwarding the original page. Recovery is to re-run preflight after edits; never fall back to raw capture.
changes.cost_impact: Low per-request compute for local scanning; modest storage for manifests and hashes. It may reduce model token cost by shrinking context, while adding engineering and maintenance cost for classifiers.
changes.latency_impact: Adds roughly 0.5–2 seconds for local preflight; remote/model work starts only after approval. Cached classification for unchanged pages can make repeat requests near-instant.
changes.security_impact: Strongly improves least-privilege and auditability, but the classifier and token verifier become security-critical. Keep manifests redacted, isolate keys, rotate token signing keys, and ensure logs cannot reconstruct sensitive values.
depends_on: A shared typed cross-surface payload manifest and destination taxonomy
Mac/browser local redaction and proof-hash services
Relay enforcement of scoped disclosure tokens
Owner-visible privacy preview and approval UI/audio

changes.change: Replace the prototype’s 15,625 Hz I2S microphone/clock path with a production audio front end that captures 24 kHz (preferably a 48 kHz digital MEMS mic plus deterministic decimation, or a native 24 kHz I2S clock), and carry an explicit audio-format contract through firmware, relay transcoding, and Mac playback. Keep 24 kHz Opus decode on playback, but stop advertising the path as superwideband when uplink capture is physically limited to 15,625 Hz. Add an end-to-end test fixture that records a swept 8–12 kHz signal and verifies sample rate, timestamps, packet loss concealment, and intelligibility at the pendant.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: The owner gets genuinely clearer speech and more reliable recognition of names and consonants in noisy everyday use, rather than a 24 kHz label applied to narrowband input. It also makes the wearable’s answer sound consistent in both directions and exposes failures before they become confusing conversations.
changes.effort: High: select and layout a mic/clock, update nRF9160 I2S/DMA and Opus framing, update relay resampling/metadata, and run acoustic plus LTE-M power validation. Treat the current Nordic DK as a bring-up fixture, not the final enclosure.
changes.risk: A clock/DMA mismatch can produce drift, buffer overruns, or dropped packets; higher-rate capture may expose the already-heavy CPU budget (encode ~15 ms per call and encode+decode about 87% of one core). Roll out behind a negotiated format bit and retain the current 16 kHz uplink fallback. If LTE-M power or CPU is unacceptable, capture at 48 kHz locally but downsample to a verified 24 kHz frame before encoding.
changes.cost_impact: Roughly $3–$15 incremental BOM for a better digital mic/clock and power regulation in volume (more for a redesigned board); modest additional LTE-M airtime and RAM/DMA buffers, plus engineering/test cost. API cost is unchanged if transcoding stays deterministic.
changes.latency_impact: Potentially +5–15 ms for resampling and larger buffers; preserve 60 ms Opus framing and negotiate down to 16 kHz on weak links.
changes.security_impact: No new data class, but higher-fidelity audio can reveal more ambient detail. Keep existing transport encryption, avoid retaining raw PCM, and make format negotiation and recording retention observable in receipts.
depends_on: A verified 24 kHz end-to-end acceptance test and explicit format metadata in POST /pipeline/audio and GET /pipeline/:pipelineId/audio/:direction
Firmware CPU/RAM and LTE-M power measurements on the target wearable, not only the development kit
Relay and Mac playback updates that reject mislabeled sample rates instead of silently resampling twice

changes.change: Add a local departure-signal subsystem to the wearable: GNSS-capable location sampling with geofence evaluation and a low-power motion trigger, keeping exact coordinates in volatile/on-device storage and emitting only a named/coarse place-transition event upstream. Include a physical privacy-disable gesture and a bounded local checklist cache for disconnected operation.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: The owner can receive a timely, private “before you leave” checklist without carrying the phone or remembering to ask. It catches forgotten items and preparation steps at the only moment they are still fixable, while avoiding a permanent location trail in the cloud.
changes.effort: High: select or enable GNSS on the nRF9160 design, characterize acquisition and LTE-M coexistence, implement geofence/motion firmware, privacy controls, encrypted local state, and relay event semantics. Product enclosure and antenna redesign may be required.
changes.risk: GNSS can be slow indoors, inaccurate in cities, and power-hungry; false departures could annoy the owner. Use hysteresis, motion confirmation, named-place confidence, quiet hours, and a local disable latch. If GNSS is unavailable, fall back to owner-triggered place changes and never claim certainty.
changes.cost_impact: Approximately $2–$10 incremental BOM if the modem/antenna can be reused, potentially more for RF and enclosure redesign. GNSS acquisition adds intermittent power draw and may increase LTE-M airtime only when a place transition is confirmed.
changes.latency_impact: Cold fixes may take tens of seconds, so motion-triggered prediction and cached geofences should provide an immediate provisional event; final confirmation can arrive later. No impact on ordinary voice latency.
changes.security_impact: Materially increases the sensitivity of the device. Exact coordinates must not leave the pendant by default; retain only coarse place IDs and short-lived transition records upstream. Privacy disable must be locally enforceable even with a compromised relay.
depends_on: A typed place-transition event contract shared by pendant, relay, Mac, and dashboard
A durable privacy policy for location retention and source disclosure
A local checklist cache and delivery acknowledgement protocol
A destination/context joiner that consumes the coarse event without requiring raw coordinates

changes.change: Add a decision-oriented `departure_check` orchestration path rather than routing this through the generic briefing flow. In parallel, query Mac observation/status, AppleScript Calendar/Mail summaries, authenticated browser reservation tabs when available, and public weather; normalize each result into `{claim, source, observedAt, expiresAt, confidence, sensitivity}`; apply a 20-second-departure policy; return complete/partial/blocked sections with a reason and a next retry time. Stream the first safe facts to relay, and persist only the compact packet plus provenance for a resumable follow-up.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: When standing at the door, the owner gets a useful answer even if one account or the browser is unavailable, instead of waiting or hearing an opaque failure. They can trust which facts are fresh and know exactly what must be checked manually.
changes.effort: Medium: new fan-out route and schema, Calendar/Mail extraction adapters, weather query, partial-result policy, and relay audio handoff; reuse existing job/receipt and browser result primitives.
changes.risk: Stale or wrongly interpreted event/travel data could cause a missed commitment. Mitigate with explicit timestamps, conservative wording ('I cannot verify'), no inferred travel time without a configured destination, and no action side effects. Recover by retaining the packet and retrying only failed sources.
changes.cost_impact: Low incremental API cost: parallel cheap extraction plus one short realtime synthesis; no need to transmit raw private page or mail bodies.
changes.latency_impact: Parallel fan-out should reduce wall-clock latency; first safe result in ~2–5 seconds, full result bounded at ~15 seconds, with a partial response if a source times out.
changes.security_impact: Private data stays on Mac/browser until reduced to sensitivity-labeled fields. Weather query may reveal coarse location; use configured city or coarse region, never exact coordinates by default. Store packet with short TTL.
depends_on: Pendant reconnection and audio delivery acknowledgement
Browser Bridge online for reservation/account checks
A configured coarse location or destination/travel-time provider
Existing typed context/provenance service or equivalent compact evidence schema

changes.change: Replace the prototype's single LED-only notification path with a production pendant notification module: a low-power LRA haptic actuator behind the enclosure, a protected driver, and a firmware-visible event queue with one-tap acknowledge/two-tap defer. Keep the LED as a secondary visual cue and make patterns generic (not content-bearing).
changes.why_useful_to_owner: They can know that an important result or approval is waiting without pulling out a phone, interrupting a conversation, or broadcasting private audio. A tap at the wrist is noticeable but discreet, and local acknowledgement still works when the network briefly drops.
changes.effort: Medium hardware spin plus firmware driver, enclosure vibration testing, battery characterization, and relay/event integration. Validate patterns across clothing and avoid confusing ordinary movement with a notification.
changes.risk: False or excessive taps could erode trust, and vibration may be uncomfortable or audible on hard surfaces. Bound daily notification volume, add quiet hours and a physical stop gesture, use escalating patterns sparingly, and retain a delivery/ack receipt for recovery after reconnect.
changes.cost_impact: Approximately $3–$8 incremental production BOM, a small driver footprint, and roughly 0.1–0.5 mAh per tap depending on actuator and pulse; no per-event model cost.
changes.latency_impact: Local queue and playback are sub-100 ms once an event arrives; relay delivery remains network-dependent. A queued event should expire rather than vibrate late.
changes.security_impact: No message text or secret should be encoded in vibration patterns. Correlation IDs and acknowledgement state should be encrypted and short-lived; an approval gesture must never itself authorize a destructive action.
depends_on: A normalized cross-surface attention-event schema from Mac jobs, browser results, and calendar watchers
Pendant reconnectivity and a reliable relay push/ack channel
Owner-configurable quiet hours and a local universal stop latch

changes.change: Add an energy-and-link-aware work lease coordinator between pendant, relay, and Mac. It polls authenticated health/ops telemetry, assigns every queued job a deadline, reversibility, required surface, and checkpoint cursor, then uses hysteresis thresholds to checkpoint and lease safe work to the relay/Mac before pendant loss. On reconnect it reconciles leases by idempotency key and emits one compact recovery receipt; it must never silently transfer an irreversible step.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: A dying or disconnected pendant would stop being a cliff. The owner would hear only the few things that truly cannot wait, while ordinary research, briefings, and drafts finish elsewhere and are ready when the pendant returns.
changes.effort: Medium-high: typed job schema and migrations, relay coordinator, pendant telemetry event, Mac handoff endpoint, reconnect reconciliation, failure-injection tests for power loss and duplicate execution.
changes.risk: A stale battery reading could migrate too late or wake the Mac unnecessarily; use hysteresis, timestamps, conservative defaults, and leases. Duplicate work is contained by idempotency keys; unresolved jobs remain visibly pending rather than claiming success. Recovery is cancel/undo where supported plus a receipt explaining the boundary.
changes.cost_impact: Small relay storage and polling overhead; occasional Mac wake/network traffic. No meaningful per-request model cost if urgency and thresholds are deterministic.
changes.latency_impact: Adds seconds of checkpoint overhead only near a risk threshold; normal interactive requests unchanged. Reconnect recovery should be available within one health poll.
changes.security_impact: Authenticated device-to-relay telemetry only; do not replicate private page contents unless the job already authorized it. Preserve per-surface provenance and require owner confirmation at irreversible checkpoints.
depends_on: A durable cross-surface job/checkpoint contract
Pendant battery and link telemetry
Owner-approved urgency and quiet-hours policy
Typed receipts and idempotency already present in the job runner

changes.change: Replace the prototype pendant’s single-button/single-LED interaction with a physical two-position microphone privacy switch that electrically disconnects the microphone bias line, plus a high-visibility LED driven from the same hardware state. Add a small fuel-gauge/RTC-backed event counter so firmware can report privacy transitions and power state after reconnect; the relay and Mac must treat a hardware-muted interval as authoritative and reject audio capture or deferred transcription from it.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: The owner can be certain—without trusting an AI explanation—that the pendant is not listening. They can enter a meeting, bedroom, or private conversation with one tactile motion, see the state, and later verify exactly when it was muted. That trust is unavailable from software mute alone.
changes.effort: High: revise the wearable PCB/enclosure and microphone power path, validate pop/noise behavior, add sealed tactile switch and LED visibility tests, implement firmware state/event logging, and thread the authoritative state through relay, Mac, and dashboard. The current nRF9160 development kit is explicitly provisional, so this belongs in the product hardware rather than a workaround.
changes.risk: A damaged or ambiguous switch could leave the owner uncertain; use hard two-state detents, a fail-quiet electrical design, startup self-test, and a visible disagreement fault. Cutting microphone power may require codec reinitialization and lose the first audio frame after unmute; announce readiness with haptic/LED feedback. Recovery is physical switch movement, not a hidden software override.
changes.cost_impact: Roughly $2–6 BOM increase for switch, LED driver, fuel gauge/RTC support, PCB/enclosure changes, plus validation NRE; negligible steady-state power increase and likely a small power saving while muted. No API/model cost.
changes.latency_impact: Unmute-to-ready may add 100–300 ms for codec startup; mute is immediate at the electrical path. Privacy-state propagation to relay/Mac should be best-effort and never delay the local cutoff.
changes.security_impact: This is a defense-in-depth boundary: audio cannot leave the device while the switch is muted. Log only transition timestamps/counters, not audio; authenticate state events and make the physical state higher priority than server commands.
depends_on: A firmware privacy-state event and durable transition counter
Relay/Mac audio pipelines honoring hardware mute as an authoritative deny
Dashboard/briefing UI that shows the last observed physical privacy state and any telemetry gap

changes.change: Add an interruption-escrow coordinator between the existing planner, job runner, browser queue, receipts, and pendant audio pipeline. At every irreversible boundary and on link loss, atomically write a checkpoint containing intent hash, completed action receipts, browser tab/session IDs, evidence references, next safe step, required confirmation, expiry, and a monotonic resume token. Expose a compact spoken resume queue and a dashboard diff; resuming revalidates page freshness and job state before executing anything.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: A dropped connection or sudden distraction would stop being a lost half-finished task. The owner can hear one accurate sentence later and continue exactly where they left off, without duplicate clicks or stale submissions.
changes.effort: Medium-high: coordinator/state machine, transactional hooks in Mac and browser runners, pendant queue protocol, and crash/replay tests.
changes.risk: A bad checkpoint could replay an action twice or present stale evidence. Default to no-op on uncertainty, require confirmation for irreversible steps, use idempotency keys and receipts, and allow discard/undo. Recovery is to invalidate the resume token and leave the underlying job untouched.
changes.cost_impact: Negligible storage/compute; one small background summarization call per interrupted packet, with optional TTS cost only when surfaced.
changes.latency_impact: Under 1 second to checkpoint; 1–3 seconds to produce a spoken resume card. No added latency on ordinary completed actions beyond a small write.
changes.security_impact: Persist references and hashes rather than raw page content or secrets; enforce per-owner auth and short TTL; redact sensitive fields from spoken summaries.
depends_on: Durable job runner and browser command queue must emit atomic action receipts
Pendant delivery acknowledgement/offline queue
Cross-surface state persistence and stale-evidence revalidation

changes.change: Replace the prototype's fixed 15,625 Hz I2S microphone clock path with a clocked 24 kHz-capable digital MEMS microphone (or add an ASRC front end) and a shared clock plan that keeps Opus encode at true 24 kHz while preserving the existing 31.25 kHz playback wire clock. Add firmware capability negotiation so the relay never labels 15.625 kHz capture as 24 kHz, and fall back explicitly when the old board is attached.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: The pendant would capture speech with the same superwideband bandwidth it can already play, improving recognition and natural turn-taking instead of silently upsampling narrowband audio.
changes.effort: High: board spin or audio front-end redesign, Zephyr I2S/clock driver work, Opus 24 kHz encode tuning, relay negotiation, and acoustic/regression testing.
changes.risk: Clock drift, increased CPU/RAM use, battery impact, and incompatibility with the prototype bridge. Recover with negotiated 16 kHz mode, watchdog-reset-safe buffering, and an explicit sample-rate badge in diagnostics.
changes.cost_impact: Prototype redesign roughly $5–$15 in added audio/clock components per unit and perhaps 10–25 mW while recording; API cost is unchanged or slightly lower if 24 kHz Opus replaces server resampling.
changes.latency_impact: Potentially +10–20 ms capture buffering; tune to retain under 200 ms end-to-end turn latency.
changes.security_impact: No new data class; audio remains encrypted in transit. Diagnostics should report sample rate without retaining raw audio.
depends_on: 24 kHz acceptance criteria and relay codec negotiation
Measured CPU headroom for simultaneous encode/decode on the nRF9160
A/B acoustic test against the current 15,625 Hz microphone

changes.change: Add a local 'place-memory capsule' to the pendant: a long-press captures up to 10 seconds of audio plus timestamp, monotonic event ID, and coarse device/location context; encrypts it at rest, keeps a bounded ring of the newest entries, and uploads only after an explicit sync policy permits. The server returns a signed receipt and can tombstone individual entries; retrieval must work from the local ring when offline.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: The owner can preserve a fleeting physical-world fact with one deliberate gesture and recover it later even when the network or Mac is unavailable, without keeping the microphone continuously active.
changes.effort: Medium firmware plus relay protocol work; requires encrypted storage, button debounce/UI feedback, upload retry, tombstones, and a small retrieval endpoint.
changes.risk: Accidental captures, sensitive recordings, flash wear, and lost keys could expose private information. Mitigate with a short fixed maximum, LED/haptic/audio acknowledgement, retention limits, authenticated encryption with device-bound keys, and an unmistakable delete gesture.
changes.cost_impact: No API cost for local capture; roughly 1–3 MB flash reserved for a bounded ring depending on codec. Estimated under 5 mW average while recording, plus brief radio upload cost.
changes.latency_impact: Immediate local acknowledgement; upload is deferred and must not block conversation. Offline retrieval is sub-second for recent entries.
changes.security_impact: This creates a new sensitive data class (location-linked personal memory). Encrypt locally and in transit, minimize metadata precision, prohibit background capture, and require explicit owner opt-in before cloud sync.
depends_on: A device key/secure-storage abstraction
A relay endpoint for signed, idempotent memory receipts and deletion tombstones
Owner retention and sync policy

changes.change: Ship a negotiated 24-kHz superwideband Opus profile end to end: capture at the actual 15,625-Hz I2S rate, resample once with a fixed-point polyphase stage to 24 kHz, encode mono Opus at an explicit 24-kHz/24–32-kbps profile, and advertise that profile in the session handshake. Keep the existing 16-kHz/16-kbps mode as a fallback selected by measured CPU/packet-loss budget. On the relay, remove any implicit 16-kHz downsample, preserve the profile in queued audio jobs and receipts, and validate decoded sample rate/frame duration before delivery. On playback, retain the existing 24-kHz decode but replace the 31,250-Hz wire-clock assumption with a negotiated rate conversion contract so the ESP32's mandatory 44.1-kHz SBC path remains the only final resample. Add loopback fixtures for tones, speech, packet loss, and clock drift; reject a session rather than silently claiming 24 kHz when a stage falls back.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: The pendant would sound intelligibly fuller and less muffled for both live replies and queued briefings, with no false promise that '24 kHz' survived the trip. Calls remain usable when bandwidth or battery is poor because fallback is explicit, not a broken half-upgrade.
changes.effort: Medium-high: firmware resampler/profile and handshake, relay transcode/schema updates, ESP32 clock-contract update, and hardware-in-the-loop audio fixtures. The current implementation is a prototype and the owner explicitly asked to ship this path.
changes.risk: A second resampler and higher Opus bitrate can increase CPU, latency, airtime, and dropouts; current hardware reports ~87% of one core when encode and decode both run. Mitigate by benchmarking encode-only/decode-only separately, selecting profile before streaming, bounded jitter buffers, and automatic fallback. Never silently mix 16-kHz and 24-kHz timestamps. Recovery is reconnect into the legacy profile.
changes.cost_impact: No API-model cost change. Rough firmware/storage work fits existing flash but needs profiling; 24–32 kbps uses about 1.5–2x radio airtime versus 16 kbps, with corresponding modem energy increase. A production device may need a better audio codec/DSP if the nRF9160 cannot sustain duplex headroom.
changes.latency_impact: Target unchanged 60-ms frames plus <=20 ms resampling; expect roughly 5–15 ms extra buffering during negotiation and possibly higher airtime latency. Keep live voice on the realtime tier; queued audio can use the cheaper background path.
changes.security_impact: Audio remains encrypted in the existing authenticated session; profile metadata and loopback diagnostics should exclude raw speech by default. Store only hashes/metrics in receipts, apply short retention to generated audio, and require explicit opt-in before uploading diagnostic clips.
depends_on: Relay must expose and persist negotiated audio profile rather than assuming 16 kHz
Firmware needs a fixed-point 15,625→24,000 resampler and CPU/RAM benchmark
ESP32 bridge must accept the negotiated wire-clock contract while retaining its 44.1-kHz SBC constraint
End-to-end loopback and packet-loss test fixture

changes.change: Add a durable Handoff Envelope that links one departure snapshot across /capture, /plan, /execute, Mac job receipts, browser session/tab IDs, pipeline audio items, and pendant delivery state. The envelope stores a redacted task summary, source references and hashes, precondition/evidence timestamps, expiration, owner approval scope, and a resume policy. Packing is append-only; returning first revalidates each source and marks changed/missing tabs or files for review instead of replaying stale actions. Expose one status/undo/delete operation so the owner can say 'what did I pack?', discard it, or resume the safe subset.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: It turns the proposed leave/return experience from a collection of jobs into one trustworthy bookmark. The owner can walk away without losing the thread and can see exactly why a return action was or was not resumed, even when the browser was offline or the Mac rebooted.
changes.effort: Medium: shared schema plus adapters around existing capture/planning/job/session/audio receipts, durable storage, and a small resume UI/voice vocabulary. No new model is required.
changes.risk: Adapters may disagree about identifiers or accidentally replay stale actions. Use immutable envelope IDs, source hashes, TTL, explicit 'changed' state, and default to read-only resume; destructive actions remain confirmation-gated. If one surface fails, preserve the envelope and deliver a partial handoff.
changes.cost_impact: Negligible API cost; one compact background summary and optional audio render per envelope. Storage is small metadata plus references, not copied private pages or screenshots.
changes.latency_impact: Packing adds roughly 1–3 seconds for metadata and 5–60 seconds for optional summary/audio. Return begins with a fast receipt lookup, then revalidation in background; no need to block spoken acknowledgment.
changes.security_impact: Improves security by centralizing redaction, TTL, deletion, and provenance. Do not duplicate authenticated content into relay prompts; retain tab/file references and hashes, encrypt any audio, and log access without raw contents.
depends_on: A durable pendant audio queue/marker and delivery acknowledgment
The negotiated 24-kHz audio contract (or explicit fallback metadata)
Browser bridge reconnect/offline queue with stable session and tab affinity
Faculty-action checkpoint/receipt protocol for any resumed mutation

changes.change: Add a commitment-collision compiler between capture/pipeline and the existing Mac/browser execution surfaces. On a spoken “can I take this on?” event, normalize the request into a candidate commitment, retrieve dated evidence from Calendar/Mail/Notes/reminders and authenticated browser tabs, classify each item as hard/soft/unknown, compute time and deadline collisions with explicit freshness, and persist a signed decision packet containing sources, assumptions, three options (accept/defer/decline), and an expiry. The relay speaks only the conclusion; the Mac creates a draft or reminder only after the owner chooses. Emit status and receipt events so a delayed browser result cannot overwrite a newer decision.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: The owner gets an answer at the moment of commitment instead of discovering the conflict later, with a defensible explanation and a ready draft—but no accidental acceptance or message send.
changes.effort: Medium-high: typed schema plus evidence adapters, temporal/conflict scoring, packet persistence, stale-result handling, and a small review UI/audio renderer. Start with Calendar + reminders + one browser session, then add Mail and task boards.
changes.risk: False collision or missed promise could cause the owner to decline something valuable; stale private-page data could mislead. Mitigate by labeling uncertainty, quoting evidence timestamps, defaulting to “needs review,” and keeping all outward actions drafts until explicit approval. Recover by packet versioning and undo for reminders/drafts.
changes.cost_impact: Low recurring model cost if extraction is cached; roughly $0.01–$0.05 per decision, with browser reads and long context dominating. Storage is a small JSON packet plus redacted evidence hashes.
changes.latency_impact: Warm local answer 2–5 seconds; authenticated browser evidence may take 10–30 seconds and should complete asynchronously with a spoken provisional answer.
changes.security_impact: Expands correlation of sensitive commitments across surfaces. Encrypt packets, minimize quoted content, enforce per-source scopes, expire raw snippets quickly, and require explicit confirmation for any draft creation or external change.
depends_on: A typed commitment/obligation schema and provenance-aware context projection
A durable decision-packet inbox/review endpoint
Authenticated browser bridge availability for private pages (currently owner must reconnect it)
A clear owner policy for working hours, buffers, and protected commitments

changes.change: Add a coin vibration motor (or low-power LRA with driver), a second tactile button, and a physical microphone-mute/privacy slider to the pendant revision. Expose a tiny local event protocol: short buzz = pending decision, double buzz = evidence ready, long press = mute/cancel and queue acknowledgement offline. Keep audio unchanged; the nRF9160's GPIO/SPI budget and 211,608 B app RAM are sufficient, while the motor driver isolates current spikes from the modem/audio rail.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: The owner can notice and control an important decision in a meeting, street, or quiet room without broadcasting speech or looking at a screen; the mute slider gives an immediate, trustworthy privacy boundary even when software is confused.
changes.effort: Low-to-medium hardware spin: motor, driver transistor/IC, button, slider, enclosure and firmware event mapping; requires board revision and power characterization on the prototype DK before productizing.
changes.risk: Vibration can annoy or drain the battery, and accidental presses could cancel a task. Use intensity/duty limits, quiet hours, distinct patterns, and require a deliberate long press for cancellation; if the motor fails, LED/audio remain available. Validate modem transmit current and audio noise during vibration.
changes.cost_impact: Approximately $2–$6 BOM increase in volume (more on prototype), with brief vibration bursts adding tens of mA for under a second; negligible idle draw if switched off.
changes.latency_impact: Immediate local feedback (<100 ms) for mute, cancel, and acknowledgement; no network round trip required.
changes.security_impact: The physical mute slider should gate microphone power locally, not merely set a software flag. Record only coarse mute/unmute events, never raw audio; keep cancellation local and idempotent when replayed.
depends_on: Define the cross-surface attention/decision event schema
Pendant firmware event queue and offline replay
Power/audio coexistence test on the nRF9160 development hardware

changes.change: Create a consent-scoped relationship memory layer distinct from generic capture/context-graph storage. A local bookmark event opens a bounded audio segment; the relay derives a structured card with three physically separate provenance classes—heard directly, owner-confirmed, and externally sourced—plus retention/deletion deadlines and an identity-confidence score. Before any card is spoken, a resolver must match it to a calendar/contact candidate and require correction when confidence is low. Pre-meeting delivery retrieves only the fields selected by the owner, never raw audio, and every card supports one-button purge from the pendant.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: The owner can remember people and context naturally after a meaningful interaction, then receive a useful reminder before seeing them again, without trusting an opaque permanent recording or being surprised by an invented fact.
changes.effort: High: pendant bookmark firmware and local indicators, bounded audio handling, entity resolution, provenance-aware schema, encryption/retention jobs, correction UI, and pre-meeting delivery integration.
changes.risk: Misidentification or a hallucinated personal detail could damage a relationship; accidental recording could violate privacy. Mitigate with explicit start/stop consent, short automatic deletion of unconfirmed clips, confidence thresholds, source citations, no sensitive-attribute inference, and default silence when identity is unresolved.
changes.cost_impact: Moderate per saved interaction: transcription and optional enrichment are the main costs, approximately $0.02–$0.10; storage stays small after deleting raw audio. Hardware cost is unchanged if existing button/LED can signal bookmarking, otherwise a dedicated haptic/privacy control is needed.
changes.latency_impact: Bookmark acknowledgement is local and immediate; card generation is asynchronous. Pre-meeting retrieval should be under 3 seconds, with a compact spoken summary rendered once and cached.
changes.security_impact: This creates a sensitive social-memory dataset. Encrypt it separately from ordinary notes, enforce per-card retention, audit every read, keep raw audio ephemeral, and make physical mute/delete override all server state as soon as connectivity returns.
depends_on: A firmware-level explicit bookmark/delete event and recording indicator
A provenance and privacy-aware relationship-card schema
Calendar/contact identity resolver with owner correction
Durable encrypted retention and purge processing
A pre-meeting scheduler that can target the pendant

changes.change: Add a cross-surface Truth Ledger and gate every spoken brief/action plan on it. Each observation becomes a typed claim {subject,predicate,value,source,observedAt,expiresAt,confidence,sensitivity}; reconciliation marks claims current, stale, contradicted, or unreachable. For contradictions, retain both evidence records, prefer direct live probes over cached/generated artifacts, and require a fresh probe before any dependent action. The formatter must say 'I have conflicting reports' rather than selecting a plausible value. Add a repair transaction that refreshes the relevant source, re-evaluates preconditions, and records a receipt without replaying queued browser commands.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: The pendant would stop telling you that Mail needs a grant when the live Mac snapshot says it has one, stop calling a dead browser online, and stop treating a half-open pipeline as completed. You get a short, honest answer and a safe recovery path instead of discovering later that the system acted on stale state.
changes.effort: Medium: typed claim schema, a small D1/local JSON ledger, reconciliation rules, and adapters for existing status/briefing/pipeline/browser routes; then add a pre-speech and pre-action hook.
changes.risk: Incorrect TTLs could make the assistant over-cautious or hide a real update. Recover by preserving raw evidence, allowing an explicit 'refresh and decide' command, and failing closed only for irreversible actions. Avoid deleting existing records.
changes.cost_impact: Negligible storage and small-model classification cost; compact claims reduce repeated context tokens. Live refreshes add API calls only when a claim is stale or action-critical.
changes.latency_impact: No noticeable delay from cached reconciliation; 1–10 seconds for source refresh, with immediate provisional wording if the owner is waiting.
changes.security_impact: Improves security by preventing stale/private browser evidence from being presented as current and by keeping page contents on their owning surface. Claim sensitivity labels must prevent secrets from entering shared prompts or audio.
depends_on: A durable cross-surface event/receipt identity shared by relay, Mac, browser, and pendant
A freshness policy for each source and explicit precedence rules
Existing /ops/status, /briefing/latest, /browser/status, /pipeline, and job receipt adapters

changes.change: Introduce a visibly separate `REHEARSE` conversation state spanning pendant, relay, Mac, and browser. In this state, all retrieved facts are assembled into an immutable scenario snapshot; the judge may branch alternatives and calculate consequences, but the action router is structurally unable to enqueue mutations. The owner can say `make this real` only after reviewing a compact delta that lists every proposed change, affected surface, evidence age, uncertainty, and duplicate risk; that phrase creates a new action plan rather than upgrading the rehearsal in place.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: They can explore consequential choices while walking or away from the Mac without fear that asking 'what if?' will send a message, alter a calendar, replay a browser command, or spend a scarce approval. The owner gets understandable alternatives first and deliberate execution second.
changes.effort: Medium-to-large: add a scenario snapshot and branch format to the relay protocol, propagate mode through planner and browser requests, enforce a deny-by-construction mutation guard, then add a review-to-action transition with fresh preconditions.
changes.risk: A stale snapshot could produce an attractive but wrong rehearsal. Show observation times, mark unknowns, refresh volatile facts before conversion to action, and expire snapshots quickly. If mode metadata is lost, fail closed as read-only.
changes.cost_impact: Small persistent metadata and one additional synthesis call when branching alternatives; no mutation or browser-action cost during rehearsal. Realtime speech remains limited to acknowledgement and summary.
changes.latency_impact: Immediate local acknowledgement; 5–20 seconds for scenario assembly depending on private-source refreshes. Conversion adds a final precondition check.
changes.security_impact: Strongly reduces accidental side effects and prevents scenario text from being mistaken for executable intent. Sensitive evidence remains source-local and only redacted claims enter the scenario snapshot.
depends_on: A cross-surface typed fact/obligation projection
Stable provenance and freshness metadata
A mutation-deny guard enforced below the planner, not merely in prompts
Existing job, browser, pipeline, and receipt identifiers

changes.change: Add an event-boundary audio adaptation service: compute 10 Hz bands/level/noise-floor/clipping features locally, classify quiet/voice-noise/music/wind with hysteresis, and publish only a signed profile recommendation (not raw audio) over the existing audio/events path. Keep two profiles and a rollback record in flash; apply only between utterances and expose a physical-button long-press to freeze the current profile.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: Speech remains understandable without the owner fiddling with settings, while a long press gives them an immediate, dependable way to stop automation in a sensitive environment.
changes.effort: Medium firmware work plus relay contract and Mac/browser adapters; 2–3 weeks including acoustic acceptance tests.
changes.risk: A wrong classifier could make audio worse or change during a call. Hysteresis, confidence thresholds, utterance-boundary application, profile rollback, and a freeze gesture recover safely; default profile remains unchanged on link loss.
changes.cost_impact: No meaningful API cost; roughly 8–16 KB code, under 6 KB RAM, and negligible flash writes if recommendations are rate-limited. Hardware cost $0 on prototype.
changes.latency_impact: Feature windows add 100 ms; profile changes take effect within 1 s but never mid-utterance.
changes.security_impact: Only coarse acoustic features and signed recommendations leave the pendant; no raw room audio is retained. Freeze gesture is local and works offline.
depends_on: A versioned cross-surface audio-profile schema and relay state machine
A 24 kHz intelligibility/clipping acceptance scorer
Mac/browser profile apply-and-verify adapters

changes.change: For the product revision (not the current nRF9160 DK prototype), add a matched dual-microphone pair with physical windscreen/acoustic isolation and a low-power audio codec path capable of verified 24 kHz capture/playback; retain the single button as the local profile-freeze/stop control.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: The pendant would remain intelligible outdoors and while walking, rather than asking software to recover speech that a single exposed microphone never captured cleanly.
changes.effort: Product-level acoustic/mechanical redesign, codec validation, enclosure spin, and firmware driver work; prototype evaluation in 4–6 weeks.
changes.risk: More acoustic tuning and power draw; two microphones can amplify enclosure mismatch. Recover by shipping a single-mic fallback profile and factory self-test, with no automatic dual-mic use when confidence is low.
changes.cost_impact: Approx. $3–8 BOM increase at volume for microphones, codec/analog front end, and acoustic parts; estimated 10–25 mW additional active audio power, subject to codec choice.
changes.latency_impact: Negligible codec latency change if designed around the existing low-latency path; beamforming adds under 10 ms with a fixed-point implementation.
changes.security_impact: No new network data; local second-mic signals are processed transiently and never retained by default.
depends_on: 24 kHz end-to-end audio acceptance criteria
Audio-profile schema and runtime adaptation state machine
Acoustic enclosure and wind-noise test fixtures

changes.change: Introduce a first-class 'uncertain span' transaction state between perception and action. The planner must carry the original intent and all resolved slots, mark only low-confidence spans, ask one targeted spoken repair, then re-run validation and produce a diff before releasing the action. If the link drops, the pendant stores a compact repair token and gives a local retry tone; it never guesses or expires into execution.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: A clipped name, number, or date no longer forces the owner to repeat an entire request or risk the wrong real-world action. They get a fast, understandable repair and continuity across the pendant, relay, Mac, and browser.
changes.effort: Medium protocol and UX work across perception/action/relay plus a small firmware queue; extensive adversarial tests for stale repairs, duplicate delivery, and destructive actions.
changes.risk: A stale correction could be attached to the wrong request, or repeated prompts could annoy the owner. Bind every repair to an intent hash, tab/job/session ID, and short expiry; cap retries at one and fall back to a clear failure receipt.
changes.cost_impact: Minimal persistent storage (under 1 KB per pending repair); one additional realtime turn only on uncertain speech; no new hardware required.
changes.latency_impact: Adds under 700 ms when repair is needed; zero added latency to high-confidence utterances.
changes.security_impact: This is a safety barrier: uncertain destructive fields cannot pass. Sensitive transcript spans remain encrypted and expire; only the disputed span is spoken or displayed.
depends_on: Typed utterance-repair protocol
Pre-action slot-confidence validator
Durable intent hash and job/session binding
Offline pendant retry token

changes.change: Replace the prototype's implicit audio assumptions with an explicit negotiated profile and loopback contract: pendant advertises capture/playback rates, frame duration, Opus mode, battery/thermal headroom, and firmware version; relay selects a profile, stamps every segment with profile+sequence+CRC, and runs a nightly fixture test that compares a 24 kHz source through uplink/transcode/decode/I2S output. Fail closed to a clearly labeled narrowband profile when the 15,625 Hz microphone path cannot satisfy superwideband, rather than upsampling and calling it 24 kHz.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: The owner gets audio that is genuinely 24 kHz when promised, and an honest fallback when this development kit cannot provide it. Regressions become visible before they turn into a day of muffled or missing pendant speech.
changes.effort: Medium-high: firmware capability packet and sequence metadata, relay negotiation/transcode changes, deterministic test fixture, and one hardware measurement pass. Product hardware may need a microphone/clock path capable of 24 kHz capture; software alone cannot recover information absent from 15,625 Hz capture.
changes.risk: A negotiation bug could strand older firmware or cause silence. Keep a backward-compatible profile, require an explicit ACK before switching, and retain a server-side narrowband fallback. Test with packet loss and reconnects.
changes.cost_impact: No meaningful per-request model cost; modest relay CPU/storage for loopback tests. Hardware prototype cost roughly $10–$30 for a suitable codec/mic/clock change, with power impact to be measured; current Opus encode+decode already consumes about 87% of one core when simultaneous.
changes.latency_impact: Capability exchange adds <100 ms. 24 kHz encode/decode remains bounded by existing 60 ms framing; fixture tests run off-path.
changes.security_impact: Telemetry contains device/firmware/profile and sequence metadata, not message content. Encrypt any diagnostic audio fixtures and expire them quickly; never retain owner speech for QA by default.
depends_on: A durable audio delivery acknowledgement/bookmark layer
An end-to-end audio acceptance test and the owner's decision on whether this development kit may be called superwideband
Physical microphone/clock redesign if true 24 kHz capture is required

changes.change: Add a spoken quality/provenance preamble only when needed: the relay tells the pendant whether this item is verified 24 kHz, resampled playback, or narrowband fallback, and attaches a one-tap 'repeat / resume / read text on Mac' control. Store the claim with the briefing item so later retries cannot silently change the promised quality.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: The owner can trust what they hear and recover quickly when a weak link affects playback; they no longer have to guess whether silence, distortion, or a shortened brief means the system failed.
changes.effort: Small-medium: profile metadata in briefing/audio events, a concise pendant prompt, and Mac text fallback routing. No new model behavior is required.
changes.risk: Too many notices would annoy the owner. Speak only on a profile change, failed delivery, or explicit request; keep the default to one short sentence.
changes.cost_impact: Negligible API cost and tiny metadata storage; one extra short TTS utterance only on exceptions.
changes.latency_impact: No impact on normal playback; exception notice adds under 1 second.
changes.security_impact: Quality metadata is non-sensitive. Text fallback must retain the existing authenticated-session and TTL protections for private briefings.
depends_on: Negotiated audio profile metadata
Per-item delivery acknowledgement and resume offset
Existing /briefing/latest and /pipeline/audio wiring

changes.change: Add a low-power haptic actuator with a dedicated interrupt-capable driver and a small nonvolatile attention latch (plus a physical acknowledge/stop input) to the wearable. Define three patterns—urgent, time-sensitive, and informational—whose waveform carries no message content; the relay sends only a signed event class and expiry, while the pendant can signal urgent events during a link outage and report acknowledgement after reconnect.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: The owner can receive a private, glance-free warning in public or while hands are occupied, without a speaker announcing sensitive content and without losing an important event just because Wi-Fi or the Mac went to sleep.
changes.effort: Hardware revision plus firmware driver, battery characterization, enclosure/acoustic isolation tests, relay event signing, and a small user calibration flow. This deliberately adds a capability rather than pretending the current single-LED/button prototype can provide reliable private urgency levels.
changes.risk: False alarms could erode trust; missed alarms could be serious. Start with advisory notifications, require explicit owner-selected sources, expose a physical universal stop, expire stale latches, and log every trigger/acknowledgement for review. Haptic vibration can affect battery life and comfort.
changes.cost_impact: Rough prototype addition: approximately $2–$8 for actuator, driver, and passives, plus PCB/enclosure changes; brief pulses likely add tens of milliwatts while active, with negligible average draw at low event rates. No model cost for delivery.
changes.latency_impact: Local haptic onset can be under 100 ms after a signed event arrives; event arbitration and Mac/browser ingestion remain network-bound.
changes.security_impact: The pendant receives only an authenticated class, expiry, and event identifier—not message text. Protect the latch against spoofing and ensure a stolen pendant cannot reveal private content through pattern semantics beyond the owner-configured vocabulary.
depends_on: A cross-surface urgency/deduplication policy and event stream
Owner-configured quiet hours, source allowlist, and confidence threshold
Delivery receipt and explanation records for every haptic event

changes.change: Add an audio-session capability handshake and resumable playback cursor to the pendant protocol: advertise supported Opus rates/frame sizes, report coarse CPU/battery/link buckets, accept a mode switch only at a packet boundary, persist the current sentence ID plus sequence number in a tiny journal, and expose an explicit reconnect/resume event. Pair this with relay-side mode arbitration and a Mac preflight that selects 24 kHz, 16 kHz, or a pre-rendered fallback before delivery.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: Briefings and replies would remain understandable instead of glitching or restarting when the owner moves between coverage or the pendant is busy. The owner gets one continuous conversation and can resume a long briefing where they stopped.
changes.effort: Medium-high: protocol versioning, nRF9160 Opus scheduling, relay jitter/transcode state, Mac preflight, and network fault-injection tests across the four surfaces.
changes.risk: A bad mode switch could produce silence, duplicated speech, or an unrecoverable cursor. Mitigate with capability-version negotiation, boundary-only switches, a watchdog fallback to the known 16 kHz path, journal checksum, and server-side duplicate suppression. Roll back by disabling negotiation and using the current fixed profile.
changes.cost_impact: Negligible model cost; modest relay CPU for dual-variant transcode and temporary boundary metadata. Firmware flash/RAM impact should stay small (roughly 8–16 kB flash and under 4 kB RAM if the journal is compact).
changes.latency_impact: Adds under 300 ms at session setup; recovery adds at most one short buffered segment. Normal speech should not gain a model round trip.
changes.security_impact: Only coarse device telemetry and opaque sentence/sequence IDs leave the pendant; no transcript is added. Resume journals on SD must obey the existing rule that SD is a failure buffer, with bounded expiry and encryption if it contains audio references.
depends_on: A versioned audio control message path between pendant, ESP32 bridge, and relay
Relay adaptive jitter/transcode state and sentence-boundary indexing
A Mac offline/preflight hook
End-to-end audio loss/reconnect tests

changes.change: Add a low-power LRA haptic actuator with a DRV2605-class I2C driver, plus a battery fuel gauge and (optionally) an ambient-light/proximity sensor. Reserve three local patterns: short pulse = completed, double pulse = approval needed, long pulse = blocked/connection lost. Keep the existing button as cancel/acknowledge and the LED as a secondary diagnostic channel.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: They can receive private, actionable status while in public, driving, or talking to someone, instead of hearing account names and task details aloud or missing an important blocked action. Battery-aware escalation can also avoid silently draining the wearable.
changes.effort: Prototype wiring is modest because I2C is explicitly free; add board support, haptic patterns, event acknowledgements, enclosure and power tests. Product revision needs mechanical/acoustic validation and accessibility testing.
changes.risk: Extra current draw and mechanical buzz could annoy the wearer; a bad pattern could be mistaken for an approval. Default to conservative patterns, allow disabling, require an explicit button press for approval, and fall back to LED/audio when the haptic self-test fails.
changes.cost_impact: Approximately $4–$12 BOM increase (motor, driver, gauge, passives, sensor) and a few mA during pulses; no per-call API cost. Fuel gauge reduces uncertainty but adds always-on quiescent current.
changes.latency_impact: Local acknowledgment is sub-100 ms once an event reaches the pendant; no model latency. Haptic queue must survive LTE reconnects without replaying expired events.
changes.security_impact: Improves privacy by removing sensitive audio from routine status. Do not encode semantic content in patterns beyond urgency/state; encrypt and authenticate event IDs, and expire approval challenges.
depends_on: A typed relay-to-pendant notification event and acknowledgement protocol
Privacy-mode routing in the pipeline
Cross-surface job receipts with idempotent event IDs and expiry

changes.change: Implement a durable Quiet-Intent channel: when the owner says 'quietly', unified issues a signed mode lease (scope, expiry, allowed surfaces, speech suppression) to relay; Mac and browser jobs publish typed lifecycle events; relay reduces them to redacted state changes and delivers exactly-once pendant notifications. A button press acknowledges or cancels the lease; bridge reconnects must not replay expired events. Approval-required events carry only a nonce and human-safe label, with full details retrieved after an intentional spoken interaction.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: This turns 'quietly' into a dependable behavior rather than a best-effort promise: private work continues across the Mac, logged-in browser, and sleeping relay, while the wearer gets only the minimum signal needed to act and can recover from a lost connection without duplicate actions.
changes.effort: Medium: define event and lease schemas, add relay D1 tables/TTL, adapt job/browser receipts, add reconnect reconciliation and tests for duplicate/out-of-order events, then add one voice command and dashboard history.
changes.risk: A stale lease could suppress speech when the owner expects it, or a lost event could hide a blocked task. Leases must expire quickly, surface a visible current-mode indicator in the dashboard, and default to normal speech after expiry; every event remains queryable in receipts.
changes.cost_impact: Negligible storage and relay compute; roughly $0.001–$0.01 per background event batch, with no realtime model call. Context cost drops because only redacted state is injected into voice turns.
changes.latency_impact: Local mode acknowledgment under 1 s; event delivery normally under 2 s, with reconnect reconciliation on next heartbeat. No added model round trip for ordinary completions.
changes.security_impact: Strong privacy gain: browser content never crosses into the haptic/status payload. Signed leases prevent a tab or stale job from changing speech policy; enforce owner-scoped authorization and redact labels.
depends_on: Cross-surface transaction coordinator from faculty-action
Durable browser job runner and typed receipts
A pendant notification/acknowledgement transport
Owner interruption and quiet-hours policy

changes.change: Add a read-only consequence projection engine that accepts a proposed commitment as an untrusted hypothetical, resolves affected time windows and obligations across local Calendar/Reminders/Mail metadata, browser sessions, and active jobs, and returns a provenance-linked displacement graph. It must preserve competing interpretations instead of forcing one identity or deadline, assign confidence/expiry to every edge, and expose a compact spoken rendering plus an audit payload.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: They can ask about a decision before making it and receive an honest answer such as 'this fits only if you give up lunch and delays the current browser task by two hours,' rather than discovering the conflict after committing.
changes.effort: Medium-to-high: schema and graph algorithms, local AppleScript readers, browser extraction adapters, hypothetical simulation tests, and a voice renderer. Start read-only with synthetic fixtures, then add live sources one at a time.
changes.risk: False conflicts could make the owner avoid worthwhile commitments; missed obligations are more dangerous. Show evidence and confidence, distinguish hard calendar conflicts from soft estimates, allow source-by-source inspection, and never write to external systems.
changes.cost_impact: Low recurring storage; roughly $0.01–$0.08 per preview after cached extraction. The main cost is model synthesis over several normalized claims, not raw source reads.
changes.latency_impact: Local extraction can begin immediately; a first estimate in seconds, full reconciliation under a minute. It must degrade to a partial answer when a source is unavailable rather than blocking.
changes.security_impact: Read-only by design. Keep source text and account identifiers on the Mac/browser; relay receives redacted claim IDs, timestamps, confidence, and hashes. Hypothetical proposals must not be persisted as commitments unless the owner explicitly confirms.
depends_on: Typed task-relevant context projection with provenance and TTL
A normalized local obligation/time representation
Authenticated browser read/extract adapters
A read-only planning endpoint that accepts hypothetical inputs

changes.change: Add a low-power haptic actuator and a 6-axis IMU to the pendant, with a tiny local acknowledgement state machine: distinct vibration patterns for ordinary reminder, repeated reminder, and pre-authorized escalation; a double-tap or button press acknowledges or cancels. Log only event type, monotonic time, and acknowledgement—not motion traces or audio. Expose the acknowledgement over the existing WebSocket when connected and persist a compact offline queue in the existing microSD failure buffer.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: The owner can acknowledge an important prompt silently in a meeting, while walking, or when headphones are unavailable; missed prompts remain recoverable after an LTE drop instead of escalating blindly.
changes.effort: Prototype I2C/SPI driver, enclosure revision, power characterization, and a small Zephyr state machine; then add relay reconciliation and test patterns with the existing ESP32 audio bridge.
changes.risk: False taps, accidental acknowledgements, extra battery drain, and confusing patterns. Require a deliberate gesture/button chord for cancel, repeat critical prompts after timeout, and fall back to audio/LED if haptic self-test fails.
changes.cost_impact: Roughly $3–8 in components and modest assembly cost; haptic bursts are low duty-cycle but LTE remains the dominant power draw. Negligible model/API cost.
changes.latency_impact: Local acknowledgement is sub-100 ms; network reconciliation is deferred during modem contention and does not add to the audio path.
changes.security_impact: Improves privacy by enabling silent prompts. Do not infer location, activity, or identity from IMU data; keep raw motion off-device and retain only acknowledgement events.
depends_on: A durable obligation/escalation policy and acknowledgement receipt path
A defined pendant-to-relay event message and offline replay protection
Owner-approved haptic patterns and cancellation gesture

changes.change: Revise the pendant enclosure to include an owner-triggered camera module with a physical shutter, a bright capture indicator, a dedicated capture/hold gesture, and a low-power local ISP path for crop, face/screen redaction, and OCR before LTE upload. Keep the existing mic/I2S/audio path independent so visual capture cannot starve live speech.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: They gain eyes-free help with real objects and printed instructions while preserving a clear physical boundary against accidental or ambient recording.
changes.effort: Select a low-power sensor and lens, add secure capture and redaction firmware, revise enclosure and power budget, define a bounded frame protocol in the relay, and validate speech-plus-image modem contention.
changes.risk: Privacy leaks, poor lighting, incorrect guidance, heat, and LTE contention. Shutter/indicator must fail closed; no frame upload without a deliberate trigger; cap burst length and fall back to OCR-only/offline behavior when the link is weak.
changes.cost_impact: Approximately $15–40 prototype BOM increase plus enclosure redesign; camera/ISP bursts add substantial peak power, so battery capacity and thermal testing are required. Vision inference adds per-use API cost.
changes.latency_impact: Local capture/redaction in tens to hundreds of milliseconds; remote interpretation adds roughly 1–3 seconds and must yield to live audio bandwidth.
changes.security_impact: Physical shutter and local redaction reduce bystander and document exposure. Encrypt frames in transit, avoid persistent storage by default, and provide a visible deletion receipt for any saved frame.
depends_on: A secure owner-triggered frame-upload protocol
A relay vision endpoint and short-lived frame storage
A spoken answer contract that distinguishes observation from inference

changes.change: Add a meeting-close coordinator: subscribe to Calendar event end, open a 90-second private debrief window on relay, accept a pendant button/phrase, then fan out one typed decision packet to Notes, reminders, browser drafts, and a durable follow-up watch. Require owner confirmation for every extracted commitment and expire the packet after 24 hours.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: The owner leaves a meeting with decisions captured and next steps ready instead of reconstructing them later or forgetting who promised what.
changes.effort: High: calendar event subscription, debrief state machine, typed packet schema, and adapters for Notes/reminders/browser drafts.
changes.risk: False extraction could create noisy reminders or embarrassing drafts; keep all outputs staged, show source excerpts, and support one-tap discard. If relay is down, retain only a local pending marker and retry.
changes.cost_impact: Small relay storage and one background extraction per meeting; roughly $0.01–$0.05 per debrief.
changes.latency_impact: A short prompt at meeting end; downstream filing can be asynchronous.
changes.security_impact: Meeting-derived text is sensitive; encrypt at rest, short retention, and do not retain raw audio after transcript extraction.
depends_on: calendar-end event hook
timestamped audio/debrief capture
decision packet schema
approval and expiry semantics

changes.change: Create a transaction comparison sandbox spanning authenticated browser tabs and Mac calendar: normalize candidate prices, dates, cancellation terms, and account state into cited evidence; run conflict and regret checks; generate an expiring draft transaction that cannot submit until a fresh spoken approval names the exact target and total.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: Before spending money or cancelling something, the owner gets a clear comparison that accounts for their actual schedule and commitments—not just the first option the browser shows.
changes.effort: High: cross-tab extraction recipes, terms parser, calendar conflict model, evidence citations, and a hard approval gate in the browser executor.
changes.risk: Terms may be incomplete or stale; label unknowns, timestamp evidence, re-fetch immediately before approval, and never treat a draft as booked.
changes.cost_impact: ~$0.05–$0.30 per comparison, mostly authenticated extraction and synthesis.
changes.latency_impact: 2–5 minutes for comparison; final approval check under 30 seconds.
changes.security_impact: Payment and credential fields must be redacted; private-page content is scoped to the job and drafts auto-delete on expiry.
depends_on: typed browser extraction results
calendar/commitment read interface
transaction draft sandbox
fresh-evidence approval gate

changes.change: Add a pendant-native 'save the last minute' gesture that marks the local audio ring buffer without uploading it by default. The relay then requests only the bounded excerpt, returns a transcript with highlighted candidate commitments and source timestamps, and waits for a spoken correction before persisting anything.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: The owner can recover the exact wording of a promise while it is still fresh, without recording every conversation or opening an app.
changes.effort: Medium-high: firmware ring buffer/marker, UART protocol, relay upload handshake, transcript UI/voice confirmation, and retention enforcement.
changes.risk: Accidental capture or third-party privacy concerns; require deliberate gesture, audible/private-mode feedback, strict 60–90 second bounds, and automatic deletion on timeout.
changes.cost_impact: Low device storage/RAM overhead; ~$0.01–$0.03 per approved excerpt for transcription.
changes.latency_impact: 5 seconds to return candidate commitments; filing is asynchronous.
changes.security_impact: Raw audio is ephemeral and encrypted in transit; only owner-approved transcript/excerpt persists with a short TTL.
depends_on: audio implementation truth
bounded ring-buffer firmware support
capture approval route
commitment extraction and correction flow

changes.change: Create a durable event-to-consequence engine. Normalize calendar/mail/browser/job events into versioned entities, compute affected reminders, conflicts, drafts, and pending jobs, and emit one deduplicated impact packet with evidence links and proposed reversible repairs. Keep the engine deterministic; invoke a background model only to phrase or rank ambiguous consequences.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: When life changes, the owner hears what they must do next—not five unrelated alerts—and can approve a coherent repair plan.
changes.effort: High: event schema, entity linking, temporal rules, provenance, and a review surface across relay and Mac.
changes.risk: False joins could suggest the wrong repair or hide a real conflict. Recover with evidence-first packets, confidence thresholds, no automatic irreversible actions, and a complete undo/ignore path.
changes.cost_impact: Low steady-state compute and storage; roughly $0.01–$0.05 only for ambiguous impact summaries.
changes.latency_impact: Seconds for local event joins; up to minutes for authenticated browser refreshes.
changes.security_impact: Processes calendar, mail metadata, and private pages. Minimize to changed fields and hashes, encrypt packets, and apply per-source retention.
depends_on: A durable event ingress beyond ad-hoc /pipeline/events
A typed entity/provenance store
A review/approval packet UI

changes.change: Add a local speaker-privacy latch to the nRF9160 audio state machine: a button gesture or signed server command immediately blocks decoded PCM from reaching the ESP32, persists across reconnects and reboot, exposes only a visible LED pattern, and allows an explicit long-press to clear. Incoming items are represented by opaque counters until the Mac-side encrypted queue is available.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: The owner can prevent an embarrassing private sentence from being spoken in a room even when LTE, the Mac, or the relay is unavailable.
changes.effort: Medium firmware plus ESP32 bridge protocol work; test every transition during packet loss, reboot, and active playback.
changes.risk: A stuck latch could make the pendant appear broken. Provide a distinct LED acknowledgment, local status query, watchdog-safe default, and a clearly documented long-press recovery.
changes.cost_impact: No API cost; negligible RAM (a few bytes of state) and power. Requires firmware/bridge integration and field testing.
changes.latency_impact: Under 100 ms from gesture to speaker mute; no network round trip.
changes.security_impact: Fail closed for speech output; authenticate remote clear commands and never allow a queued private payload to be decoded locally without the latch being open.
depends_on: A defined button gesture and LED status contract
ESP32 bridge mute command with acknowledgment
Encrypted Mac-side notification queue

changes.change: Add a tab-identity quarantine before any authenticated read or mutation: require a fresh extension heartbeat whose tabId, URL, title, session binding, and content hash agree with the durable session record; on contradiction, freeze commands, mark the tab orphaned, and ask the owner to choose the authoritative tab.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: Prevents the system from reading or changing the wrong logged-in page. Today the live Safari tab says example.com/Failed to open page while the durable session says Gmail, so a confident action could target the wrong account context.
changes.effort: Medium: identity record, heartbeat comparison, quarantine state, and explicit recovery UI.
changes.risk: A stale heartbeat may pause legitimate work; recover by re-heartbeating and requiring owner selection. Never auto-rebind on URL alone.
changes.cost_impact: Negligible API cost; a few D1/local records per heartbeat.
changes.latency_impact: Adds under 300 ms to browser jobs when heartbeat is fresh; may require human recovery on mismatch.
changes.security_impact: Strongly reduces confused-deputy risk and prevents cross-account tab mixups.
depends_on: authenticated browser session records
browser heartbeat and typed command queue
dashboard display of quarantined tabs

changes.change: Create an event-scoped evidence bundle that joins a pendant utterance/button timestamp, relay job ID, Mac job and receipt IDs, browser tab evidence, and final audio state into one immutable timeline; expose a plain-language outcome such as captured, planned, executed, rendered, uploaded, delivered, or played.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: When the owner asks “did that happen?”, the answer should be a proof, not a hopeful status. It makes late/offline behavior understandable and lets them safely retry without duplicating actions.
changes.effort: High: shared correlation ID propagation, append-only event schema, and a small owner-facing receipt view.
changes.risk: Partial or duplicated events could produce misleading certainty; require explicit unknown states and idempotent event IDs, with raw event drill-down for recovery.
changes.cost_impact: Low storage and background processing; no extra model call for normal events.
changes.latency_impact: No meaningful hot-path delay if events append asynchronously.
