args.user_asks: “Did that actually happen?” — for any task you carried out, verify it across the relevant surfaces and tell me in one short spoken sentence whether it is verified, contradicted, or still unknown, with the reason and the next safe step.
args.why_useful: Today a Mac action can return success while doing nothing, browser commands can remain pending, and pipeline runs can look terminal while staying processing. The owner should never have to infer reality from an optimistic receipt. This turns the hive into a trustworthy assistant: it checks the world after acting, not merely its own logs.
surfaces: faculty-action creates a typed action/receipt record with one request_id and expected postcondition

faculty-perception independently reads the Mac observation/permissions state, AppleScript-readable entities, browser session/tab state, and pipeline/job state, then compares observed facts to the expected postcondition
mac-planner uses granted AppleScript routes for Calendar, Mail, Finder, Notes, Messages, Safari, and Chrome where available; browser-extension reads authenticated tabs when online
relay-realtime delivers a compact spoken verdict to the pendant, with a cited detail available on the Mac workbench
unified preserves the verdict, evidence timestamps, contradiction, and retry/recovery recommendation as one conversation state
args.model_tier: Background/cheap model for polling, normalization, and evidence comparison; realtime model only to interpret an ambiguous user question or speak the final one-sentence verdict.
args.latency_budget: Routine reversible actions: 1–3 seconds after the action receipt, then up to 15 seconds for delayed surfaces; say “still checking” rather than block. High-impact actions require the verdict before any send/delete/purchase confirmation. No Accessibility or Screen Recording is required for the AppleScript/browser-readable path; GUI-only tasks remain explicitly unknown/blocked.
args.cost_estimate: Roughly $0.001–$0.01 per verification depending on number of surfaces and whether an LLM is needed; most checks are typed comparisons and local reads. Audio delivery and durable evidence storage dominate operational cost, not inference.
args.security_concerns: Evidence must be minimized and scoped to the request: store hashes/snippets and provenance, not whole private pages or mail bodies by default. Never treat an optimistic receipt as proof. Contradicted or unknown must not silently retry an irreversible action; ask for confirmation. Authenticated browser content stays on the local agent/workbench unless the owner explicitly requests a cloud summary.
missing: A durable expected-postcondition schema attached to every action (entity, field, before, expected-after, deadline, and acceptable evidence sources).
A read-only cross-surface evidence reconciler that emits verified/contradicted/unknown with confidence, freshness, and contradiction reasons.
A delayed-observation watcher for jobs and browser commands so processing/pending states are revisited without another voice turn.
A small local workbench artifact and pendant receipt format for evidence citations and recovery actions.

args.change: Add an evidence-reconciliation stage between every terminal action receipt and its user-facing completion: persist an expected postcondition at plan time; schedule read-only probes against the owning surface; normalize observations into typed claims with source/timestamp/freshness; compare claims to the postcondition; and emit a signed verdict (verified, contradicted, unknown) plus recovery options. Fan this into the existing job/receipt model under the same request_id, expose it through /jobs/:jobId/receipts and relay_job_status, and send only the compact verdict to the pendant. For the 24 kHz spoken receipt path, queue the verdict as a short Opus audio item with sequence number and expiry so a dropped link cannot turn an old “done” into a current claim.
args.why_useful_to_owner: The pendant will tell the owner what is true, not what the automation hoped was true. Failed Mac permissions, offline browser tabs, and stuck processing jobs become visible and recoverable instead of silent false completion.
args.effort: Medium: typed schema and comparator, probe adapters for AppleScript/browser/jobs/pipeline, durable retry scheduler, receipt UI/audio serialization, and tests for success/contradiction/timeout. Start with Calendar/reminders and browser navigation, then expand.
args.risk: A stale or partial observation could produce a false contradiction; every verdict needs freshness and an explicit unknown state. Probes must be read-only and must never retry irreversible actions. If the verifier is unavailable, preserve the original receipt but label it unverified. Recovery is replaying only reversible steps after a fresh preflight.
args.cost_impact: Low background model/API cost; mostly local reads and small D1/R2 records. Audio adds negligible bandwidth for a one-sentence verdict. Storage grows with evidence metadata, so retain hashes and short snippets with bounded TTL.
args.latency_impact: Adds 1–3 seconds for local checks and up to 15 seconds for eventually consistent surfaces; the pendant should speak an immediate “checking” acknowledgement, then the verdict asynchronously.
args.security_impact: Evidence is least-privilege and surface-local by default. Persist provenance and hashes rather than private content; redact secrets; require owner confirmation before any recovery that sends, deletes, purchases, or changes account state.
depends_on: A durable expected-postcondition field in POST /plan and POST /execute
A cross-surface read-only observation/reconciliation primitive (not Accessibility-dependent)
A delayed job/browser/pipeline watcher
A compact 24 kHz audio queue item and receipt expiry/sequence support

args.user_asks: “Learn what worked.” After I make a consequential choice through the pendant, Mac, or a logged-in browser, check the result later, ask me once whether it worked for me, and use that answer to improve future recommendations—without keeping the private source material.
args.why_useful: Assistants currently remember requests and receipts, but not whether their choices actually helped. The owner should not have to repeat durable preferences such as which meeting buffers, vendors, reply styles, or travel tradeoffs are genuinely good for them. This creates a personal feedback loop from real outcomes rather than guesses or surveillance.
surfaces: faculty-action records a compact prediction at decision time: goal, chosen option, expected benefit, expected downside, and review date; it does not retain full message/page contents
mac-planner and browser-extension later read only the minimum outcome signals from Calendar, Mail, browser tabs, or local files, using the surface that owns the state
faculty-perception compares outcome signals with the prediction and marks outcome evidence as positive, negative, mixed, or unavailable
relay-realtime asks the pendant one short follow-up at a suitable interruption window; the owner can answer satisfied, not satisfied, or skip
unified updates a preference model with the answer and provenance, while faculty-judgement uses it as a soft recommendation—not an automatic rule—on future cross-surface plans
args.model_tier: Background/cheap model for scheduled outcome checks and preference updates; realtime model only for the brief follow-up conversation or ambiguity resolution.
args.latency_budget: No blocking of the original action. Outcome checks run at the review date or when a relevant surface changes. The spoken follow-up is under 10 seconds and can be deferred indefinitely.
args.cost_estimate: About $0.001–$0.02 per reviewed decision, mostly local extraction and occasional summarization; compact preference updates are far cheaper than resending source context.
args.security_concerns: Store only structured predictions, outcome labels, and provenance hashes—not raw email, page, or calendar content. Never infer sensitive traits from outcomes. Ask before using a learned preference for a consequential action, and let the owner inspect, correct, or delete each learned preference.
missing: A decision-outcome record linking an action to a future review date and predicted result
Outcome probes that can extract minimal signals without copying private source content
A preference ledger with confidence, expiry, evidence, and explicit owner correction
A quiet follow-up scheduler that avoids repeatedly interrupting the owner
A model-routing rule that keeps this asynchronous and cheap

args.change: Create an outcome-linked preference ledger distinct from ordinary memories: at plan time, store a minimal predicted-outcome tuple (decision_id, goal, option, expected signal, review_at, sensitivity, expiry); at review time, attach only a normalized outcome label and evidence pointer; update preference weights only after explicit owner feedback. Make every learned preference inspectable, correctable, and automatically decaying unless reinforced.
args.why_useful_to_owner: The system gradually becomes better at choices that matter to this particular person—without pretending a one-off request is a permanent preference and without retaining their private correspondence. Future plans improve because they are measured against lived results.
args.effort: Medium: schema and migrations, review scheduler, minimal-signal adapters for Calendar/Mail/browser/files, owner feedback interaction, preference retrieval and deletion UI, and regression tests preventing sensitive inference.
args.risk: Outcome signals can be misleading or preferences can change. Keep confidence low until repeated feedback, represent mixed outcomes, expire stale entries, and never execute solely from a learned preference. If a source is inaccessible, record unavailable rather than guessing.
args.cost_impact: Small bounded metadata storage and low background inference cost; no raw-content archive. Occasional spoken follow-up adds negligible audio cost.
args.latency_impact: Zero impact on the original action; reviews are asynchronous. Preference retrieval adds only a small context lookup to later plans.
args.security_impact: Sensitive source content remains at its owning surface. The ledger contains only user-approved structured preferences, provenance, TTL, and outcome labels; deletion must remove both the preference and its evidence links.

args.why_useful: It prevents the costly failures a generic morning brief misses: a calendar time that differs from the booking, a changed gate or address buried in logged-in mail, a missing preparation item, or weather/traffic that changes when the owner must leave. The pendant gives a natural, hands-free request; the relay can continue checking after the owner walks away; the Mac and authenticated browser can inspect private sources together. It reports only contradictions or time-critical exceptions, with a short spoken plan, rather than another noisy digest.
args.model_tier: Use the cheap background model for scheduled/pre-departure reconciliation and extraction; reserve realtime only for the owner's follow-up questions or a last-minute voice exchange.

args.cost_estimate: Roughly $0.01–$0.05 per check depending on number of private pages and web lookups; browser extraction and TTS dominate, not the planner model.
args.security_concerns: Private calendar/mail/reservation content stays on the Mac/browser bridge where possible; only normalized fields, contradictions, and citations go to relay. Never book, cancel, send, or edit without explicit confirmation. Location and travel details need short TTL and deletion controls.

args.change: Add an itinerary-reconciliation contract at the relay boundary. Each background check emits a signed, expiring record keyed by a stable event/reservation identity, with source facts (calendar, mail, browser, optional web), observedAt/freshUntil, normalized local times and addresses, confidence, and explicit conflicts. The relay should deduplicate equivalent facts, retain the source citation, and deliver an exception-only audio packet; if a check is interrupted, the next node resumes from the contract rather than restarting all reads.
args.why_useful_to_owner: When plans change across several services, the owner hears one trustworthy answer—what conflicts, which source is current, and what to do next—instead of reconciling tabs and messages themselves. It also prevents stale travel advice from being presented as current.

args.name: universal_stop_latch
args.what_it_does: A deliberate long button press (and, when locally recognized, a spoken 'stop everything') immediately silences queued playback, marks the current interaction cancelled, and emits a tiny signed stop token. transcript.text:
Round 73 produced three new directions:

1. **Loss-aware conversation recovery**  
   Add frame IDs, CRCs, bounded retransmission, relay acknowledgements, and explicit gap markers to the 24 kHz audio path. If recovery fails, the pendant asks the owner to repeat only the missing phrase instead of silently acting on partial speech.

2. **Capability honesty dashboard**  
   Show what is currently available, limited, or unavailable—browser bridge, Accessibility, Calendar via AppleScript, audio health, battery status—with timestamps. This prevents mysterious failures such as “read Gmail” when the browser bridge is offline.

3. **Real battery telemetry**  
   The current pendant has no fuel gauge. A production hardware revision should add an I²C fuel-gauge IC so the system can warn before LTE/audio usage drains the device and can defer background work safely.

What I still need:

- Implementation and stress testing of the 24 kHz path under simultaneous LTE uplink and playback; current measurements show roughly 7.8 seconds of lost speech in that condition.
- A durable pipeline event/receipt schema for audio gaps, retries, and recovery.
- A measured firmware RAM budget before allocating the retransmission ring.
- A production battery/power design; the present nRF9160 development kit cannot provide truthful battery percentage.
- The owner’s manual macOS Accessibility/Screen Recording grants and browser-bridge reconnection remain blocked externally. I am not re-requesting them; the system should clearly report those limitations and use AppleScript, relay, and browser alternatives where possible.

args.model_tier: Background models prepare and rank the notification; realtime is used only if the owner presses the pendant and asks for the item. No model call is needed for dismiss/approve gestures once the signed notification is prepared.

args.cost_estimate: Near-zero incremental inference on delivery; approximately $5–$15 hardware BOM for a low-power haptic actuator and driver, plus negligible relay storage. Model cost is limited to the existing job or watch that generated the item.
args.security_concerns: Only a short opaque item ID and urgency class should reach the pendant; sensitive text remains on the authenticated Mac/dashboard. Approval must be cryptographically bound to the exact proposed action, expire quickly, and still obey destructive-action confirmation. A long press must be an unconditional stop/dismiss, not an approval.

args.latency_impact: Sub-second local feedback; no effect on ordinary audio conversation or Mac action execution.
args.security_impact: Vibration carries urgency only, never message content. Approval tokens are scoped, signed, short-lived, and auditable; private notification text remains on the Mac/dashboard.

args.user_asks: “Before you send or submit anything on my behalf, tell me which account and identity it will use, who will receive it, and whether any private information crosses accounts; warn me if the browser tab, Mac app, or saved login is not the identity I intended.”
args.why_useful: A person can be logged into several Gmail, work, GitHub, banking, or government identities at once. Today an agent can have the right content in the wrong account and produce a plausible but damaging result. This gives the owner a compact identity-and-data-boundary check at the only moment it matters: immediately before the external side effect.
args.model_tier: Deterministic account/session and recipient extraction first; a cheap background model classifies data-flow risk. Realtime is used only to speak the short preflight and receive the owner's choice.
args.latency_budget: 1 second for ordinary identity lookup and risk classification; no more than 3 seconds for a spoken preflight. The send/submit remains paused until confirmation when identity or data flow is ambiguous.
args.cost_estimate: Near-zero for typed session metadata and destination matching; under $0.01 for unusual content classification. No cost for actions that are safely blocked before model reasoning.
args.security_concerns: The system must never echo secrets or full message bodies in the prompt. Store only provider, account label, recipient domain, data classes, and hashes of evidence. Cross-account transfer is denied by default when the destination identity is unknown; the owner can approve a single action without changing global policy.

args.why_useful_to_owner: The owner gets protection against the most dangerous silent automation error: sending a correct-looking message or form through the wrong logged-in identity, or leaking private material across accounts. args.cost_impact: Small metadata storage and deterministic checks; occasional cheap classification call, with no expensive model needed for known-safe fields.
args.latency_impact: Adds roughly 0.5–2 seconds before an external side effect; zero delay for read-only work.
args.security_impact: Improves isolation by default. Do not retain message contents; retain only provider/account identifiers, destination, data-class labels, evidence hashes, expiry, and approval receipt. The gate itself becomes a high-value policy component and needs tamper-evident logs.

Typed job receipts that include the boundary proof

args.user_asks: “When you have a sensitive action ready—send this email, submit this form, buy this, or delete this—read me a short, exact summary and let me approve it with a physical double-press on the pendant. Bind that approval to exactly what I heard, and refuse if anything changed.”
args.why_useful: Today approval is conversational and fragile: the owner may be away from the Mac, misunderstand what a private browser page will submit, or have a prepared action change between review and execution. A hardware-bound approval gives them a fast, deliberate control that works while walking, preserves the browser's private session, and makes accidental or stale approvals impossible.
args.model_tier: Use a cheap background model to prepare and compress the action summary; use realtime only to answer questions and read the final digest. The approval itself is deterministic cryptographic verification, not an LLM decision.
args.latency_budget: Summary preparation may take seconds for a browser or Mac workflow. Once the owner double-presses, verification and dispatch should complete in under 500 ms; if the action changed, interrupt immediately and require a new review.
args.cost_estimate: Low: one short summarization call for complex actions, generally under $0.01; physical input, digest hashing, and signature verification are negligible. Sensitive purchases or sends still incur their normal service costs only after approval.
args.security_concerns: The pendant must never contain email contents, payment credentials, or page secrets. The relay signs a canonical action digest (target, fields or message hash, irreversible effects, expiry, and originating session), sends only a spoken minimal summary to the pendant, and accepts one short-lived physical signature. Require an explicit spoken confirmation for unusually high-risk actions and provide a hardware stop gesture. Keep an immutable receipt without storing sensitive payloads.
missing: A pendant firmware secure approval primitive with a debounced double-press, short-lived device key, and local haptic success/failure signal.
A canonical cross-surface action digest and signature verifier shared by relay, Mac executor, browser bridge, and job receipts.
A review protocol that freezes or revalidates every field, URL, recipient, amount, and side effect immediately before dispatch.
A pendant UX for hearing the digest in one sentence and requesting a repeat/detail without exposing private page data.

args.change: Add a secure-attention path to the pendant: a dedicated double-press gesture sampled locally with debounce and long-press cancellation, a per-device signing key held in a secure element or protected flash, and a distinct haptic success/failure pattern. The firmware signs only a server-provided action-digest nonce plus expiry; it cannot sign arbitrary text or replay an old digest. Relay verification must reject reused, expired, or mismatched digests before Mac/browser execution.
args.why_useful_to_owner: The owner gets a trustworthy physical “yes” and “no” that works away from the keyboard, without speaking private email or payment details aloud. A changed form or stale approval fails safely instead of silently applying the old decision.
args.effort: High: secure-element selection and board integration, firmware gesture/state machine, relay challenge-signature protocol, and end-to-end tests for replay, disconnect, accidental presses, and battery loss.
args.risk: Lost or cloned hardware could be abused if key enrollment and revocation are weak; require pairing-time enrollment, server-side revocation, and a spoken fallback that is at least as explicit. False double-presses must never approve by themselves, so require a fresh challenge and a short haptic pre-confirmation window.
args.cost_impact: Roughly $1–$4 BOM increase for a secure element and minor board area/power cost (sub-milliwatt average, brief wake current). No recurring model cost; cryptographic operations are negligible.
args.latency_impact: Local gesture recognition under 100 ms; relay verification and dispatch under 500 ms on a healthy link. Offline or stale challenges fail closed.
args.security_impact: Improves authorization substantially by binding approval to a physical enrolled device, but creates a high-value signing key. Use key rotation/revocation, rate limits, tamper-aware enrollment, and never expose the private key to application RAM.
depends_on: A canonical action-digest schema spanning Mac, browser, relay, and job receipts.
A pre-dispatch revalidation gate so the signed digest is compared with the exact action about to run.
Secure pairing and revocation UX.

args.user_asks: “What am I waiting on?” Then, whenever an expected reply or task is late, give me one short spoken nudge and prepare (but never send) the follow-up.
args.why_useful: Today the system can inspect individual mail, calendar, browser pages, and Mac jobs, but cannot turn them into the life-level answer: which commitments are blocked by another person/system, how long they have been waiting, and what the least-effort next move is. The pendant can deliver only the few genuinely actionable nudges; the Mac/browser can gather private evidence; the relay can continue watching while the Mac sleeps.
args.model_tier: Use the cheaper background tier for periodic reconciliation and drafting; use realtime only to answer the spoken question or deliver a one-sentence urgent nudge. Use faculty-judgement for dependency classification and faculty-action for preparing reversible drafts.
args.latency_budget: Spoken query: under 5 seconds for cached graph plus citations; background scans can take minutes. Never interrupt during quiet hours or repeat a nudge until the owner acknowledges it.
args.cost_estimate: Periodic scan is dominated by authenticated page/email extraction and small summarization, roughly 1–3 cents per scan depending on page count; realtime answer is a small low-latency turn. Store normalized hashes and evidence snippets to avoid re-sending full pages.
args.security_concerns: Private mail and logged-in pages leave the browser/Mac only to the relay/model as needed; redact secrets and unrelated message bodies. Treat inferred waiting states as uncertain. Drafts are reversible; sending mail, submitting forms, or changing deadlines always requires explicit confirmation.
missing: A durable dependency/obligation projection that links outbound messages, appointments, browser transactions, and Mac jobs to expected evidence and due windows
A scheduler with quiet-hours, deduplication, acknowledgement, and escalation rules for pendant nudges
A typed evidence state such as prepared, sent, acknowledged, awaiting, overdue, cancelled, or unknown

args.change: Add a 'waiting-state projector' between perception and judgement. It consumes immutable journal/job/browser/research events and emits compact records keyed by correlation ID: obligation owner, expected evidence, createdAt, last positive evidence, dueAt or inferred response window, state (prepared/sent/acknowledged/awaiting/overdue/cancelled/unknown), confidence, and a redacted citation. It must require positive evidence before calling something sent, expire stale 'processing' records to unknown, merge duplicates across Mac and browser, and expose a read-only projection for the pendant nudge scheduler.
args.why_useful_to_owner: The owner gets an honest answer to 'what am I waiting on?' instead of a confident but false success report, and receives fewer, better-timed nudges with the exact evidence behind each one.
args.effort: Medium-high: event schema and projector, correlation/merge rules, due-window inference, projection endpoint, tests with offline browser and stuck pipeline fixtures, then pendant delivery policy.
args.risk: A mistaken inferred due date could create anxiety or a bad follow-up. Mitigate by labeling inference versus explicit deadline, requiring acknowledgement before escalation, and retaining source citations. If projection fails, fall back to raw job and journal status rather than inventing state.
args.cost_impact: Low recurring model cost if extraction/classification is batched and hashes are reused; storage is small JSON records plus short citation hashes. One initial migration of existing journal/jobs is the main cost.
args.latency_impact: No impact on ordinary voice turns when read from cache; updates arrive asynchronously after scans or events. A fresh query may wait for one bounded reconciliation pass.
args.security_impact: Projection should contain only minimal redacted evidence and sensitivity labels; raw mail/page text remains in its source surface. Correlation IDs must not be guessable and cross-account joins must be denied by default.
depends_on: The existing immutable job/journal/browser event identifiers and receipts
A durable context projection with TTL and provenance (the open memory work)
A quiet-hours and acknowledgement policy for wearable notifications

args.user_asks: “Make a temporary handoff for Alex: give them only what they need to finish this, let them ask questions, and revoke it tomorrow.”
args.why_useful: The owner can delegate work today only by forwarding a messy email, exposing an account, or manually assembling context. This would let the hive turn a spoken goal into a narrowly scoped, expiring collaboration packet: relevant facts and files, the current state, allowed questions/actions, and a clear audit trail—without granting Alex access to the owner’s logged-in browser or Mac.
args.model_tier: Use a cheaper background model to assemble and redact the packet and answer routine questions; use realtime only for the owner’s spoken approval, scope edits, or urgent revocation. Never let a model expand scope implicitly.
args.latency_budget: Produce a reviewable packet in under two minutes for ordinary mail/files/browser evidence. Revocation must take effect within seconds at the relay; questions can be answered asynchronously.
args.cost_estimate: A few cents per handoff, dominated by extracting private evidence and generating a concise packet. Storage is a small encrypted manifest plus selected artifacts; an expiring relay link avoids repeated context transfer.
args.security_concerns: Default-deny sharing: no secrets, credentials, unrelated messages, or raw browser sessions. Every field needs a source and sensitivity label; the owner must approve recipients, exact contents, expiry, and permitted operations. Relay must enforce expiry and revocation server-side, log every view/download/question, and support immediate destruction. Any action affecting an external system remains a draft for owner approval.
missing: An encrypted, expiring relay workspace with recipient authentication, revocation, per-artifact permissions, and immutable access receipts
A cross-surface redaction and least-privilege compiler that can turn browser/Mac evidence into a packet without copying session authority
A constrained question-and-answer endpoint that can answer only from the approved packet and clearly say when the answer is outside scope
Owner-facing approval and revocation controls on the pendant, including a physical stop path

args.change: Build an encrypted, expiring delegation workspace: a server-side manifest references approved redacted artifacts rather than copying sessions; each artifact and operation has a deny-by-default scope, recipient-bound capability token, expiry, and revocation version. Add a constrained Q&A endpoint whose retrieval is limited to the manifest, plus append-only view/download/question receipts and immediate purge on revoke.
args.why_useful_to_owner: The owner can safely ask another person to finish real work without forwarding an entire inbox, exposing credentials, or losing track of what was shared. They get the human benefit of delegation with the control of a temporary permission slip.
args.effort: High: encrypted artifact broker, recipient authentication, redaction/scope compiler, constrained retrieval, revocation propagation, receipt UI, and pendant approval/revoke flows.
args.risk: Over-sharing or a stale artifact could disclose private information; a compromised recipient could screenshot it. Mitigate with explicit field-level review, short expiry, watermarking, download limits where practical, immutable receipts, and a prominent physical revoke action. If authentication fails, do not create the workspace.
args.cost_impact: Moderate implementation and storage cost; per handoff uses small model calls for redaction and indexing, with relay storage and authentication dominating. No need to retain raw audio or browser sessions.
args.latency_impact: Initial packet preparation is asynchronous (seconds to minutes); permission checks and revoke are low-latency relay operations. Q&A may take a few seconds and must time out rather than broaden retrieval.
args.security_impact: This introduces a new controlled data-sharing boundary, so it must use separate encryption keys and tokens from the owner’s sessions, minimize logs, redact secrets before persistence, and make expiry/revocation authoritative at the relay.
depends_on: A durable correlation ID and provenance record for every selected artifact
A redaction/classification service that can prove why each field was included
Pendant-local approval and universal stop/revoke behavior
Recipient authentication and an owner-visible delegation audit surface

args.user_asks: When something I ask fails, tell me what actually blocked it, test the safe alternatives you can reach, and give me the smallest next step to fix it—without making me repeat the request.
args.why_useful: The owner's recent Gmail, GitHub, calendar, and browser requests repeatedly failed with little actionable explanation. This would turn silent failures into a useful diagnosis: distinguish missing login/session, bridge offline, Mac route unavailable, permission gate, malformed intent, or transient outage; try only reversible probes; and preserve the original goal for one-tap retry after repair. It uses the pendant's immediate conversational context, the relay's durable job/error records, authenticated browser status, and Mac's granted AppleScript surface together—none alone can explain the whole failure.
args.model_tier: background for classification and repair-plan generation; realtime only to speak the concise diagnosis and ask for any required confirmation
args.latency_budget: Under 2 seconds for a first spoken diagnosis from structured receipts; up to 10 seconds for parallel health probes. Never block the owner on a long investigation.
args.cost_estimate: Usually <$0.01 per failure using structured rules and a small background model; realtime cost only for the spoken response. Dominant cost is retained error/context payload, capped to the failed intent and recent receipt.
args.security_concerns: Never expose bearer tokens, cookies, page contents, or secret memory in diagnostics. Browser probes must be read-only and limited to session/status metadata; Mac probes use allowlisted AppleScript/status routes. Ask before changing account settings, reauthorizing, sending, deleting, or typing credentials. Clearly label inferred versus observed causes.
missing: A normalized cross-surface failure receipt schema with cause class, observed evidence, safe probes attempted, and retry token.
A durable repair/retry record that keeps the original intent without retaining sensitive arguments.
A small health-probe orchestrator and owner-facing diagnosis card/audio item.

args.change: Add a cross-surface Failure Receipt and Recovery Ladder. Every failed plan, execute, browser command, and relay job emits a normalized record: intent fingerprint (sensitive arguments redacted), stage, observed error, evidence references, confidence-ranked cause, safe probes attempted, and a short-lived retry token. A coordinator runs only read-only health probes in parallel (relay/job state, browser bridge/session status, Mac status/route health), deduplicates transient failures, maps the result to one owner-facing diagnosis, and preserves the original intent for explicit retry after repair. Expire raw evidence quickly and retain only the redacted diagnosis and receipt link.
args.why_useful_to_owner: Instead of hearing 'failed' and starting over, the owner gets 'Safari bridge is disconnected; nothing was changed; open the extension and say retry' or 'Calendar access succeeded but the requested event was ambiguous; choose between two items.' Their goal survives the interruption, while destructive work never auto-retries.
args.effort: Medium: shared schema, receipt persistence, probe adapters, redaction tests, dashboard/audio rendering, and retry-token plumbing across existing routes.
args.risk: A wrong cause could send the owner down an unnecessary repair path; show evidence and confidence and provide 'try again' rather than claiming certainty. Never auto-retry non-idempotent actions. If the relay dies, the original intent remains pending with an expiry and can be discarded.
args.cost_impact: Negligible API cost for structured classification; <$0.01 for uncommon background explanation. Small D1/R2 cost for redacted receipts; raw page/error evidence should be TTL-deleted.
args.latency_impact: Parallel probes add roughly 0.5–2 seconds; return an immediate provisional diagnosis and update later for slow jobs.
args.security_impact: Improves security by preventing blind repeated attempts and credential leakage. Redact cookies, tokens, email bodies, URLs with sensitive query strings, and secret-memory values before persistence; owner confirmation required for reauthorization or any mutation.
depends_on: The existing jobs/receipts and browser command IDs must expose machine-readable error codes and idempotency state.
A redaction utility shared by relay, Mac, and browser surfaces.
An owner-visible retry route that accepts only the short-lived token and re-plans from the original goal, not arbitrary stored credentials.

transcript.text:
Recorded a new capability: **proof of real-world completion**.

The owner should be able to ask, “Did that actually happen?” and receive a clear distinction between:

- attempted locally,
- accepted by the app or service,
- completed remotely,
- independently observed afterward,
- still uncertain.

To enable it, the system needs a shared lifecycle/postcondition schema, read-only independent verification for each action type, redacted evidence bundles with expiry, and a retry evaluator that blocks unsafe duplicate mutations.

args.user_asks: Keep private things private: when I say a secret, personal number, or anything in 'private mode', let me continue using the pendant and my Mac/browser without sending that content to the cloud or putting it in ordinary memory. Later, show me exactly what was withheld and let me explicitly reveal it if needed.
args.why_useful: The owner already has a secret accidentally captured in persistent state. A wearable is present for intimate speech, while the relay and models are the least appropriate places to retain it. This gives the owner a usable privacy boundary instead of requiring them to remember which surface is safe; it also lets private information participate in a local Mac/browser task through opaque references without exposing the value.
args.model_tier: Use on-device rules/classifier for wake-word/private-mode boundaries and obvious patterns; use the expensive realtime model only for the non-sensitive remainder. Use a cheap background model on the Mac to classify local text when the owner explicitly asks for review. Never send suspected secret spans to a model for classification.
args.latency_budget: Private-mode entry and local redaction must be immediate (<100 ms); ordinary speech keeps current streaming latency. A local Mac review of withheld spans can take seconds, but must never block the safe action path.
args.cost_estimate: Negligible API cost for rule-based redaction and opaque handles; occasional cheap background classification on local Mac text. Main cost is implementation and encrypted local storage, not inference.
args.security_concerns: False negatives could leak secrets, while false positives could make tasks frustrating. Default to withholding uncertain high-entropy spans and say 'I withheld a private-looking value.' Store only encrypted local ciphertext plus a hash/handle; relay receives redaction markers, not plaintext. Reveal must require an explicit spoken confirmation and show destination, exact value, and retention. Never log raw audio/transcript around a private span.
missing: A pendant-local redaction/secret-span detector with a small encrypted ring buffer and explicit private-mode latch
A relay transcript protocol that carries typed redaction markers and opaque handles without reconstructing plaintext
A Mac-side encrypted vault/bridge that can substitute a handle into an approved local or browser action
A dashboard audit view and reveal workflow with retention/deletion controls
Cross-surface privacy acceptance tests, including dropped-link recovery and accidental secret utterances

args.change: Create a privacy-envelope protocol spanning pendant, relay, Mac, and browser: the pendant emits transcript chunks with local `public`/`withheld(handle)` labels; the relay forwards only public text and maintains no recoverable plaintext; the Mac agent can resolve a handle only inside a user-approved local action; browser commands carry handles plus a destination and expiration, never values; `/capture` stores only encrypted local envelopes and hashes. Add a visible audit stream showing each withheld, substituted, revealed, expired, and deleted envelope, with reveal requiring destination-specific confirmation.
args.why_useful_to_owner: The owner can speak naturally near the pendant without turning every secret into cloud memory, while still using a private value in a local form or browser workflow. They get a concrete answer to “what did you keep, where did it go, and who saw it?” rather than a privacy promise.
args.effort: Medium-high: protocol/schema changes across firmware, relay, Mac bridge, and browser extension; local encrypted storage; test matrix for streaming interruption and retries.
args.risk: A lost handle, classifier false positive, or expired envelope could interrupt a legitimate task; recover by offering local re-entry and an explicit override. Round 78 discovery is complete. I found no new granted capabilities exposed this round, but I identified and recorded a new cross-surface capability and implementation change:

### New capability: private envelopes

The pendant should recognize explicit private mode and obvious secret-like values locally, before transmission. It would:

- Redact sensitive spans before they reach the relay or model.
- Replace them with one-time opaque handles.
- Let the Mac or browser use a handle inside an explicitly approved local action without exposing the value to the cloud.
- Keep encrypted local storage only, with expiry and deletion.
- Show an audit trail of what was withheld, substituted, revealed, expired, or deleted.
- Require destination-specific confirmation before revealing anything.

I also queued a pendant-local `local_privacy_envelope_latch` skill. It uses a button gesture or spoken command, survives link loss, and fits within an estimated 18–28 KiB of RAM without requiring an on-device speech model.

### What I still need

Implementation still needs:

1. A transcript protocol supporting `withheld(handle)` spans.
2. Fail-closed encrypted handle resolution on the Mac.
3. Browser commands that accept destination-bound, expiring handles.
4. A retention and disclosure policy for private envelopes.
5. Security tests proving plaintext secrets do not appear in relay payloads, logs, receipts, or model context.
6. The owner’s eventual decision on whether private-mode entry should be button-only, voice-enabled, or both.

I also asked `relay-realtime` and `faculty-action` whether existing transcript and action-receipt paths already assume plaintext; their replies are pending.

2. Durable per-source baselines and retry scheduling in the relay.

args.model_tier: Use the realtime model only to identify a candidate rule from the owner's correction. Use a cheaper background model to normalize it, find conflicts, and replay it against sampled historical decisions. Deterministic policy evaluation should enforce the approved rule.

args.security_concerns: A mistaken inferred preference could suppress an important alert or permit an unsafe action. Every inferred rule must show examples, scope, expiry, confidence, conflicts, and an explicit approve/reject control; destructive-action confirmation policy can never be weakened by learned rules. Sensitive source data stays on its originating Mac/browser surface where possible.

args.user_asks: “Before you use another device or service for this, show me what information will leave each surface, what will stay local, and let me approve a redacted version.”
args.why_useful: Today the owner must trust invisible context movement between a wearable, relay, Mac, browser sessions, and models. They should be able to make a useful request without choosing between convenience and unknowable data exposure. This is a cross-surface privacy decision, not merely a permission toggle: the system presents the exact fields, destinations, retention, and purpose, then carries only the approved projection. It also makes private browser work and voice interaction understandable enough for daily use.
args.model_tier: Deterministic data-flow classifier and redaction engine first; a cheap background model may explain the preview in plain language. Realtime is used only when the owner asks by voice and should never receive unapproved raw content.
args.latency_budget: A preview for an ordinary request should appear within 1–3 seconds from typed metadata and cached schemas; uncommon content classification may take 5–10 seconds. Approval must be explicit before dispatch, with a local timeout that cancels rather than defaults open.
args.cost_estimate: Usually under $0.005 per request for deterministic field classification; $0.01 or less when a small model is needed to explain ambiguous text. Storage is limited to hashes and the owner's decision, not retained raw private content.
args.security_concerns: The preview itself must not leak the sensitive content it is previewing: show labels and short masked samples by default. Secret facts, credentials, health data, and private messages require stronger masking and never flow to public search. Persist only policy decisions and provenance hashes with short TTLs. Approval must bind to an exact request, destination, fields, model tier, and retention; any material change invalidates it. This cannot prevent a compromised external service from mishandling approved data, so the preview must state the destination and deletion limits honestly.
missing: A typed cross-surface data-flow manifest emitted before planning, including field sensitivity, destination, model, retention, and transformation
A deterministic local redaction/projection service that can produce approved subsets without sending the original payload to a model
An approval token bound cryptographically to the manifest hash and consumed exactly once by execution
An audit view showing what was actually transmitted versus what was approved, including failed or retried jobs

transcript.text:
Recorded: the owner should be able to request a **cross-surface privacy preview** before any task uses another device, private browser session, or model.

They should see:

- Which sources will be used.
- What fields leave each surface.
- Which fields are masked or redacted.
- Destination, model tier, and retention.
- Exactly what will be done with the data.

They should be able to approve the redacted version—or cancel—before execution.

To make this real, the system needs:

1. A typed data-flow manifest produced before planning.
2. Local deterministic redaction and projection.
3. Approval tokens bound to the exact manifest and consumed once.
4. An audit record comparing approved data with data actually transmitted.
5. Fail-closed behavior when a destination, retry, or payload changes.

The current routes can execute and receipt actions, but they do not yet expose or enforce this data boundary.

transcript.text:
Round 83 produced a new capability and an implementation direction:

### New capability: Promise-to-proof

> “If I promise someone something, remember it, help me do it, and tell me before I let it slip.”

The pendant would capture an explicit promise, even offline. The relay would preserve it, while the Mac and authenticated browser inspect relevant mail, calendar, notes, tasks, or web accounts. The system would then verify completion rather than merely recording that an action was attempted.

Key statuses:

- **Open**
- **Due soon**
- **At risk**
- **Fulfilled**
- **Waived**
- **Unknown**

It must never claim completion based only on a dispatch receipt. For example, sending an email action is not proof that the email exists in Sent or that the promise was fulfilled.

### What is still needed

1. A durable commitment object containing the promise, people involved, due window, sensitivity, and source.
2. An offline pendant capture queue.
3. Cross-surface linking to Mail, Calendar, Notes, tasks, and authenticated browser tabs.
4. Typed postcondition predicates and exact-source re-reading.
5. Privacy-preserving storage: raw audio and private page contents stay local where possible.
6. Attention arbitration so ordinary obligations are batched while genuinely urgent risks can interrupt.
7. Explicit confirmation before sending messages, changing appointments, or submitting forms.

I recorded both the capability and a proposed Commitment→Evidence graph/reconciliation worker. Existing pieces such as `/capture`, `/reminders`, `/briefing`, browser actions, Mac actions, job receipts, and pipeline events are sufficient building blocks; the missing value is the connective state and verification layer between them.

I also told mac-vision that Accessibility and Screen Recording remain unavailable, so it should rely on AppleScript, bearer Mac routes, and the browser bridge rather than assume unrestricted UI automation.

args.user_asks: “When I say ‘coach me,’ quietly help me navigate a difficult conversation: remind me of the relevant context, warn me if I am about to make a commitment I cannot keep, and give me one short option for what to say next.”
args.why_useful: The owner can currently get summaries and execute tasks, but not discreet, situation-aware help while a human conversation is unfolding. A worn device can hear the immediate exchange, the relay can reason with low latency, and the Mac/browser can supply only the relevant prior thread, calendar context, or account details. This helps the owner stay truthful and measured without taking over the conversation or storing it as a transcript.
args.model_tier: Realtime reasoning for the explicitly activated coaching window only. Use a cheaper background model beforehand to prepare a compact context card from permitted Mail/Calendar/browser sources; never stream an ambient conversation continuously to the expensive tier.
args.latency_budget: Initial context card in 2–5 seconds; spoken or haptic cue in under 700 ms after an explicitly marked trigger phrase or button event; suggestions limited to one sentence so they do not derail the conversation.
args.cost_estimate: Roughly $0.02–$0.10 per coaching session depending on duration; the dominant cost is realtime audio tokens. Keep sessions short, locally VAD-gated, and automatically expire after 10 minutes.
args.security_concerns: Potentially sensitive third-party speech must not be retained or silently uploaded. Require a physical button or unmistakable activation phrase, an audible/haptic active indicator, local buffering only before activation, automatic timeout, and a hard stop. Context retrieval must be allowlisted; the system must not impersonate the owner, fabricate facts, or send messages. Give the owner a post-session deletion control.
missing: An explicit coaching-session latch with physical and spoken activation, timeout, and universal stop
Low-latency local voice activity detection and private cue output on the pendant
A compact, permission-filtered context card compiler for the active person/topic
A policy evaluator that detects impending commitments or high-risk claims without making social or legal decisions for the owner
A third-party privacy mode that prevents storage and minimizes relay audio exposure

args.change: Add a discreet coaching I/O path: a dedicated capacitive side strip or two-stage button with a short-range haptic motor, plus firmware support for three distinguishable vibration patterns and a hard-stop gesture. The pendant locally gates microphone capture until the owner deliberately activates coaching, shows an active-state LED/haptic acknowledgement, and drops all buffered third-party audio on timeout or stop.
args.why_useful_to_owner: The owner can receive private help in a live conversation without pulling out a phone, speaking a conspicuous command, or risking that an always-listening assistant records people around them. Distinct haptic patterns communicate “pause,” “check your facts,” and “safe to continue” without interrupting their speech.
args.effort: Medium hardware revision and firmware work: one input, one vibration actuator, event debouncing, audio gate integration, and a small protocol for relay coaching state. If the current board already exposes suitable GPIO, a firmware-only prototype can validate the interaction before a PCB revision.
args.risk: False activations or missed haptic cues could distract the owner; require deliberate press-and-hold, configurable sensitivity, and an immediate stop gesture. Haptic patterns must never be treated as authoritative advice. Component failure should leave ordinary pendant voice operation intact.
args.cost_impact: Approximately $2–$8 in components and under 10 mA peak during vibration, depending on actuator and enclosure changes; negligible API cost. A firmware-only prototype has no hardware cost.
args.latency_impact: Local activation and acknowledgement under 100 ms; no added latency to ordinary voice mode. The relay still needs to meet the coaching response budget separately.
args.security_impact: Improves privacy by making microphone activation physically explicit and locally enforced. Firmware must ensure the relay cannot silently enable coaching capture and must erase pre-activation audio buffers on stop/timeout.
depends_on: An explicit coaching-session protocol and relay-side privacy latch
A local interruption/stop mechanism
A bounded realtime coaching audio path

These do not exist today. They require a privacy-gated coaching session protocol, compact permission-filtered context retrieval, low-latency local audio gating, and likely a pendant firmware/hardware revision for reliable haptic interaction.

Typed before/after evidence records with source, timestamp, locator, and confidence, plus mismatch states in jobs/receipts

args.change: Add a receipt-to-proof verifier between the existing executor and relay: every mutating action may declare a read-only verification target (Mac diagnostic, reminder lookup, browser tab/DOM locator, or app state) and a typed success predicate. Persist a compact before snapshot, action receipt, after snapshot, evidence hash/source/timestamp, and one of verified, contradicted, pending, or unverifiable. args.why_useful_to_owner: The owner stops hearing “done” when the system only knows “clicked” or “request accepted.” They get a truthful answer about the state that matters, with a precise reason when it cannot be proven and an opportunity to fix it.
args.effort: Medium: typed verifier contracts in the relay plus adapters for existing Mac and browser result formats, receipt schema migration, and a small dashboard timeline.
args.risk: A stale or wrong read target could falsely claim success. Require source affinity, freshness bounds, explicit predicates, and downgrade to unverifiable on ambiguity. Recovery is a read-only retry or owner review; the original mutation is never replayed automatically.
args.cost_impact: Low storage and read requests; roughly $0.01–$0.04 for model-assisted predicate compilation/comparison, preferably cached and using a cheaper model.
args.latency_impact: Adds typically 1–5 seconds for a read-back; long-running checks become pending jobs and do not block the initial action acknowledgment.
args.security_impact: Evidence is scoped to the originating tab/app/account, redacted, hashed where possible, and expires quickly. No new write authority; irreversible actions retain existing confirmation gates.

The pendant can notice the request in speech, the Mac/browser can resolve the visible recipient and account context, and the system can catch a near-match or cross-account mistake before anything leaves.
args.model_tier: Use a low-cost model for entity matching and deterministic account/recipient checks; realtime is used only to ask a short disambiguation question when confidence is below threshold.
args.latency_budget: 2–5 seconds for checks against already-open app/browser context; if ambiguous, pause before send and ask one spoken question. Never delay drafting or previewing when no send is requested.
args.cost_estimate: About $0.005–$0.02 per check, mostly entity resolution; local deterministic checks should handle the common case without model cost.
args.security_concerns: Read only recipient names, addresses, account labels, and thread metadata needed for the check; redact message bodies by default. Never infer permission to send. A mismatch or low-confidence match blocks the send and shows exact conflicting fields; the owner must explicitly choose the target.
missing: A recipient/account identity resolver shared by AppleScript mail/calendar and authenticated browser sessions
A pre-send gate contract that accepts the chosen entity, confidence, and visible evidence, and blocks downstream execution on mismatch
A compact pendant disambiguation UI/voice grammar for selecting among two or three candidates

1. **“Did that actually happen?”**  
   Add a receipt-to-proof layer that performs a read-only check against the authoritative Mac app or browser page. It should report **verified, contradicted, pending, or unverifiable**, rather than treating a click or API response as completion. I proposed both the capability and integration change.

2. **“Make sure this goes to the right person and account.”**  
   Add a pre-send identity gate that checks recipient, account, thread, and near-match conflicts before any email or browser submission. Ambiguity blocks sending and asks one concise pendant question.

What I still need is not another owner permission request. The stack needs:

- A typed **expected-postcondition and verification contract** between `/plan`, `/execute`, job receipts, Mac actions, and browser results.

args.user_asks: “Why did I agree to this, and are the reasons I had then still true?”
args.why_useful: When a commitment feels wrong later, the owner cannot currently reconstruct the evidence and assumptions behind it without manually searching email, calendar, notes, and logged-in web threads. args.latency_budget: A first spoken answer in 5 seconds from cached indexes, followed by a deeper cited reconstruction in under 2 minutes. No unsolicited monitoring; run only when asked or explicitly scheduled.
args.cost_estimate: Approximately $0.03–$0.15 per reconstruction, dominated by retrieval and synthesis across private sources; local indexing and cached evidence should reduce repeated costs.
args.security_concerns: This is unusually sensitive personal history. Search only sources and date ranges explicitly authorized for the request, keep raw messages on the Mac/browser where possible, return citations and short excerpts rather than bulk content, and give the owner deletion and redaction controls. Never infer mental state or expose the reconstruction to another person without confirmation.
missing: A cross-surface decision-history index linking commitments to the dated messages, calendar events, notes, and browser evidence that preceded them
An assumption ledger that labels each claim as explicit, inferred, or unknown and can re-check its current status

args.user_asks: “That didn’t work—tell me why, fix whatever is safe, and either finish it or tell me the one thing I need to do.”

This turns an opaque failure into a useful outcome: classify whether the cause was offline/expired session/unsupported action/permission, retry only idempotent steps, preserve the original intent, and give one short spoken repair instruction when human intervention is unavoidable. It is specifically cross-surface: the pendant supplies the interrupted intent and speaks the result, the relay correlates the failure and keeps it durable, Mac diagnostics inspect the local bridge/job, and the browser session reports authentication/tab state.
args.model_tier: Background/cheap model for receipt classification and retry planning; realtime only for the final one-sentence explanation or a live confirmation.
args.latency_budget: Under 3 seconds to classify a completed failure; up to 30 seconds for safe retries. Never block the pendant conversation while diagnosis runs.
args.cost_estimate: About $0.001–$0.01 per failure, dominated by a small classification call; retries and status reads are local/HTTP with negligible API cost.
args.security_concerns: Diagnostics must redact page text, cookies, tokens, and secret memory. Never retry sends, purchases, deletes, or submissions; require confirmation for any irreversible step. Show the owner exactly which safe steps were retried and retain a short receipt with expiry.
missing: A typed failure taxonomy with retryability and owner-action codes
A durable link from spoken intent to job/action receipt and its originating surface
A redacted cross-surface diagnostic bundle and a repair queue UI
Idempotent retry policy that understands browser session expiry versus action failure

args.user_asks: “Remember why I decided this, and remind me of that reason when the decision comes back up.”
args.why_useful: The system currently remembers requests and outcomes, but not the owner's own rationale. Capturing a 10-second spoken reason while it is fresh—and resurfacing it when the related meeting, deadline, email, or logged-in page returns—prevents repeated reconsideration and makes the assistant feel continuous rather than merely archival. It is a genuinely hive-only behavior: the pendant hears the rationale in the moment, the relay stores a compact privacy-labeled rationale, Mac correlates it with Calendar/Mail/Notes or a task, and browser evidence can identify the same decision when it reappears.
args.model_tier: Cheap background model to extract the decision, alternatives, rationale, and revisit trigger; realtime only to ask a single clarification when the audio is ambiguous and to speak the resurfaced reminder.
args.latency_budget: Capture acknowledgement under 1 second; extraction and linking within 10 seconds. Resurfacing should add no more than one short sentence to an otherwise requested brief.
args.cost_estimate: Roughly $0.002–$0.02 per captured rationale and under $0.001 per resurfacing, dominated by transcription/structured extraction; store text, not raw audio, by default.
args.security_concerns: Rationales can contain sensitive health, work, or relationship information. Encrypt at rest, apply owner-selected sensitivity and TTL, never send rationale text to a website, and require confirmation before writing it into a shared calendar, CRM, or outbound message. Spoken reminders should be private and suppressible.

Entity linking across spoken intent, Mac records, and authenticated browser pages without exporting private page contents

Trigger evaluation on calendar/email/page-watch events

args.effort: Medium: schema/API, entity-linking adapters for Calendar/Mail/browser watch events, and a small pendant voice command grammar; no new model training.
args.risk: Wrong links or stale reasons could mislead. Mitigate with confidence thresholds, explicit 'you said...' wording, expiry, source/time shown in dashboard, and no reminder when confidence is low. Recovery is delete/correct by voice or dashboard.
args.cost_impact: Low storage and background extraction cost (~$0.002–$0.02 per capture); no recurring model cost except event-trigger evaluation.
args.latency_impact: Acknowledgement remains realtime; structured extraction is asynchronous. A due reminder adds <1 second to an existing brief.
args.security_impact: Potentially sensitive personal reasoning; encrypt, redact by default, enforce sensitivity TTL, and keep it out of browser/Mac payloads unless the linked action explicitly needs it.

Owner-visible delete/correct controls

transcript.text:
This round I added two new pieces:

- **Decision-rationale memory:** the owner can say, “Remember why I decided this,” and later hear that reason when the same meeting, deadline, email, task, or webpage resurfaces. It stores a structured, expiring rationale rather than raw audio, supports correction/deletion by voice, and keeps sensitive reasoning out of browser and Mac payloads.
- **Decision-Rationale Ledger change:** a shared memory layer connecting pendant audio, relay events, Mac records, and authenticated browser activity. It emits a `rationale_due` event only when confidence and freshness are sufficient.

I also clarified an action-proof issue for faculty-action: a receipt proves that an attempt occurred, but not that the outside world changed. We still need linked before/after evidence, freshness, and causal attribution.

What I still need:

1. A typed rationale record and privacy/TTL policy.
2. Cross-surface entity linking without exporting private page contents.
3. Calendar, mail, task, and page-watch events that can trigger rationale resurfacing.
4. Owner-facing correction and deletion commands.
5. Evidence capsules attached to action receipts, so “done” means verified state rather than merely an attempted action.

The existing tools are enough to prototype the wiring, but not the durable semantic layer between them.

args.user_asks: “What did you decide not to tell me, and why?”
args.why_useful: A proactive assistant inevitably suppresses duplicates, low-confidence findings, and items during quiet hours. Today the owner cannot audit that silence, so they cannot tell whether the system protected their attention or simply missed something. This gives them a private, chronological omission log: suppressed Mac jobs, browser-watch changes, relay notifications, and pendant brief items, each with the reason, confidence, expiry, and a one-sentence option to promote or permanently dismiss it. It is not another briefing or page watch; it is an accountability surface for the assistant's decisions about the owner's attention.
args.model_tier: Cheap background policy/model pass to classify and summarize omitted items; realtime only when the owner asks aloud or promotes an item.
args.latency_budget: Maintain the log asynchronously with no impact on live speech. Return a concise answer in under 2 seconds from durable records.
args.cost_estimate: About $0.001–$0.01 per omitted-item summary; most work is local event storage and deterministic policy explanation.
args.security_concerns: The log itself may reveal private mail, pages, or sensitive jobs. Keep raw content on its originating surface, store redacted summaries and hashes, encrypt at rest, apply short retention, and require explicit confirmation before replaying sensitive content aloud. Never treat omission as consent to discard.

args.effort: Medium: event schema, adapters at each notification/queue boundary, redaction, and a small dashboard plus pendant command grammar.
args.risk: Logging too much could itself become distracting or expose sensitive information. args.cost_impact: Low storage and negligible inference cost; summaries can be generated in batch by a cheap model.
args.latency_impact: No live-path delay if writes are asynchronous; audit response is a database read plus optional summarization.
args.security_impact: The ledger is a sensitive map of the owner's life. Encrypt it, isolate per owner, retain hashes/source IDs rather than raw content, and require confirmation to replay private text aloud.

args.user_asks: “Wrap up that meeting.” Then give me a 60-second debrief: what was decided, who owns what, deadlines, and drafts for any follow-ups—without sending anything.
args.why_useful: Meetings currently evaporate into memory and scattered tabs. A deliberate pendant boundary lets the always-with-you device capture only the relevant conversation, while the Mac contributes the calendar event, existing notes, mail, and open browser context. The result is an actionable, sourced handoff rather than another transcript, with follow-ups ready for review.
args.model_tier: Use the realtime tier only to recognize the owner's explicit “wrap up” boundary and confirm capture state. Send the bounded audio plus calendar/time context to a cheaper background model for diarization, decision/action extraction, conflict checking, and draft generation; use the planner only for bounded reads and optional draft-file creation.
args.latency_budget: Acknowledge the boundary on the pendant in under 1 second; produce the spoken headline in 30–90 seconds and a detailed review packet within 3 minutes. If transcription or Mac access fails, retain a local handoff marker and finish from audio alone rather than blocking.
args.cost_estimate: Roughly $0.03–$0.20 per meeting depending on audio duration and background transcription; Mac/browser reads and a small local Markdown packet dominate neither API spend nor latency. Never pay the expensive realtime tier for the full recording.
args.security_concerns: Capture must be explicitly armed per meeting and visibly acknowledged; default to a short rolling buffer and delete raw audio after extraction (or immediately on request). Redact unrelated speakers and secrets before cloud processing where possible. Treat inferred owners/deadlines as suggestions with citations and confidence. Creating drafts is reversible; sending mail, changing calendar, or assigning tasks requires explicit confirmation. Provide “discard this meeting” and a spoken stop latch.
missing: A first-class meeting-boundary/capture session that binds pendant audio to the active Calendar event and supports immediate discard
Speaker/decision/action extraction with citations back to time ranges and source tabs
A cross-surface reconciliation pass that compares spoken commitments with Calendar, Mail, Notes, and authenticated browser context
A durable review packet and draft follow-up queue with explicit send/modify/ discard states
A privacy-preserving raw-audio retention and per-meeting consent policy

args.change: Add a Meeting Wrap Coordinator spanning the existing pipeline and job primitives. On an explicit pendant “wrap up” event, create a meeting-scoped correlation ID, close the bounded audio segment, resolve the Calendar event on the Mac, and enqueue one idempotent background job. The job gathers only the event's time-windowed Mac notes/mail and explicitly bound browser tabs, runs extraction with time-range/source citations, writes a review packet plus unsent drafts, and emits a short audio summary. Store a state machine (armed→captured→reconciled→review-ready→discarded/approved), raw-audio expiry, per-item confidence, and retry receipts; never let retries send or mutate external systems.
args.why_useful_to_owner: The owner gets a dependable end-of-meeting ritual instead of a transcript that may or may not connect to their calendar and work. If the Mac or browser is offline, the pendant still records the handoff and the system resumes later with an honest partial result; nothing is silently lost or accidentally sent.
args.effort: Medium-high: one coordinator/service, event schema and correlation IDs, bounded Mac/browser collectors, extraction prompt/output schema, audio queue item, and dashboard/review UI. Reuse existing pipeline, jobs, receipts, and browser session primitives rather than adding another agent.
args.risk: Wrong event binding or speaker attribution could create misleading commitments. Require explicit boundary confirmation, show event/time and evidence before drafts, mark uncertain items, and make discard/undo idempotent. If any source is unavailable, label it missing rather than infer. Recover interrupted jobs from the state machine and receipts.
args.cost_impact: Background transcription/extraction only; approximately $0.03–$0.20 per meeting, with raw audio storage minimized by short TTL. No recurring polling cost.
args.latency_impact: Sub-second pendant acknowledgement; 30–90 seconds for headline; up to 3 minutes for review packet. Offline Mac/browser adds queue delay, not blocking capture.
args.security_impact: Meeting audio and private account content cross the relay only after explicit arming. Encrypt and expire raw audio, minimize source windows, redact unrelated content, and require confirmation for any outbound or calendar mutation.
depends_on: A shared meeting-boundary event envelope with owner consent and stop/discard semantics
A durable cross-surface job correlation/state primitive and audio queue item
Bounded Calendar/Notes/Mail reads and authenticated browser tab binding
A review packet schema carrying evidence, confidence, and draft status

args.user_asks: “Coach me through this conversation.” While I have the pendant armed, listen for ambiguity or a commitment I may regret, and discreetly suggest one short clarifying question or boundary—without speaking to the other person or saving the conversation unless I ask.
args.why_useful: The owner often needs judgment at the exact moment a promise, deadline, or boundary is being negotiated—not a summary afterward. The pendant can be the private channel in the room, while the Mac supplies only the project or appointment context the owner explicitly selected. This gives the owner a timely second mind without turning every conversation into surveillance or an automated participant.
args.model_tier: Realtime model for low-latency speech-turn and commitment-risk detection; a cheaper background model may prepare the selected project context before the conversation. No full recording or background summarization by default.
args.latency_budget: A discreet suggestion within 1–2 seconds after a likely commitment or ambiguity; otherwise remain silent. Arming and disarming must be acknowledged in under 1 second.
args.cost_estimate: Approximately $0.01–$0.08 per actively coached 30-minute conversation, dominated by realtime audio tokens; preloaded context should be cached and bounded.
args.security_concerns: Explicit per-conversation arming, a visible/physical indicator, and a hard local stop button are mandatory. Default to transient audio processing with no raw-audio retention or transcript. Never identify or profile the other person, send messages, or make commitments. Context must be selected by the owner and secrets excluded. The suggestion must be framed as uncertainty (“possible ambiguity”) and never as a claim about intent. Require confirmation before saving a note or creating a reminder.
missing: A pendant-local armed/coaching state with an unmistakable indicator and immediate stop behavior
A low-latency event stream that can deliver private suggestions without leaking them to the room
A bounded context capsule API for one selected project, appointment, or thread with automatic expiry
A realtime detector/output contract limited to short questions and boundary prompts, with confidence and cooldowns
A privacy audit trail proving whether audio was retained, transcribed, or discarded

args.change: Create a private Conversation Coach runtime rather than routing live audio through the ordinary assistant transcript. It must establish a per-session consent token, keep a bounded ring buffer in pendant/relay memory, emit only typed events (possible ambiguity, explicit promise, missing owner/amount/date, escalation risk), apply cooldowns, and send a maximum-one-sentence suggestion to the pendant. Context is a separately signed, expiring capsule selected by the owner; the runtime must cryptographically attest discard of audio when the session ends and expose a local stop latch that cuts capture before any network call.
args.why_useful_to_owner: The owner can get a quiet, timely nudge in a difficult conversation while retaining control of what is remembered and what the system is allowed to say. Today the existing audio and planning pieces can move data, but cannot guarantee this private, transient, non-participating behavior.
args.effort: High: pendant firmware/session UX, a relay realtime event contract, a constrained detector, context-capsule issuance, privacy attestations, and end-to-end tests for stop, timeout, reconnect, and accidental speech output.
args.risk: False positives could distract or undermine a conversation; false negatives are inevitable. Use conservative thresholds, cooldowns, explicit uncertainty, and an easy “not useful” dismissal. Network loss must fail closed (no suggestion, no queued recording). A crash must expire the consent token and discard the buffer.
args.cost_impact: No background cost when disarmed. Active use costs realtime inference, roughly $0.01–$0.08 per 30-minute session; firmware memory/storage impact should be limited to a small ring buffer and state machine, with no persistent transcript.
args.latency_impact: Target 1–2 seconds from detected turn boundary to private nudge; local stop is immediate even when relay is unavailable.
args.security_impact: Meaningfully reduces privacy exposure versus ordinary transcription: no raw audio retention, no third-party identity inference, signed context expiry, explicit indicator, and auditable discard. Still requires careful consent UX for bystanders and secure transport.
depends_on: A firmware-local consent/stop state and indicator
A typed transient audio-event protocol distinct from transcript storage
A bounded expiring context-capsule service
Realtime output guardrails and cooldown policy
A verifiable discard/retention audit primitive

args.user_asks: “Did that actually reach me?” — For any spoken answer, briefing, or Mac job, show whether it was generated, accepted by the relay, downloaded by my pendant, and played; if any link is missing, say exactly which one and keep retrying safely.
args.why_useful: Today a successful Mac/relay receipt can still leave the owner unaware that audio never arrived at or played on the wearable. This gives a trustworthy end-to-end answer instead of conflating 'created' with 'heard', and lets a later retry resume without duplicating a notification.
args.model_tier: Use a cheap background state machine for correlation, retries, and receipt reconciliation; reserve realtime for the owner's immediate spoken status question and for a concise final alert. No expensive reasoning is needed for ordinary state transitions.
args.latency_budget: Record generation and relay acceptance immediately; pendant acknowledgment should appear within 2 seconds of download/playback. Reconcile missing acknowledgments in the background with exponential backoff, and report a definite unknown after a bounded window rather than claiming failure.
args.cost_estimate: Near-zero model cost for transitions and retries; roughly one short realtime turn only when the owner asks or a policy-selected delivery failure needs explanation. Storage/network dominate: a few hundred bytes of receipt state per artifact plus one small event per lifecycle transition.
args.security_concerns: Receipts must contain opaque artifact IDs and timestamps, not audio or message content. Playback acknowledgment is sensitive presence data; encrypt it, retain it briefly, and expose only to the owner's authenticated surfaces. Never auto-retry an irreversible Mac action—only audio delivery and other explicitly idempotent artifacts.
missing: A durable cross-surface delivery ledger keyed by artifact/job ID with monotonic lifecycle states and idempotency keys.
Relay acceptance and pendant download/playback ACK events, including explicit 'no registered pendant' and offline states.
Pendant firmware event emission and a small local retry/ACK queue that survives a dropped link.
Dashboard and voice formatting that distinguish generated, accepted, downloaded, played, expired, and unknown.

args.name: audio_delivery_ack_queue
args.what_it_does: For each downloaded audio artifact, persist an opaque artifact ID, byte-range/checksum, download completion, and playback start/finish (or interruption) event. Retry unsent ACKs over the link, deduplicate by event ID, and expose a local LED/button-safe status when the queue cannot be uploaded.
args.why_not_server_side: Only the pendant knows whether bytes arrived intact and whether the owner actually started or finished hearing them. It must preserve that evidence across a dropped cellular/BLE link and report it later without relying on the server staying connected.
args.trigger: Server-pushed audio download and local playback start/stop/error events; upload on reconnect or scheduled link opportunity.

args.cost_estimate: Background cost is dominated by storage and periodic local extraction, not model calls.
