args.change: Replace the prototype pendant’s single-button/single-LED interaction with a physical two-position microphone privacy switch that electrically disconnects the microphone bias line, plus a high-visibility LED driven from the same hardware state. Add a small fuel-gauge/RTC-backed event counter so firmware can report privacy transitions and power state after reconnect; the relay and Mac must treat a hardware-muted interval as authoritative and reject audio capture or deferred transcription from it.
args.why_useful_to_owner: The owner can be certain—without trusting an AI explanation—that the pendant is not listening. They can enter a meeting, bedroom, or private conversation with one tactile motion, see the state, and later verify exactly when it was muted. That trust is unavailable from software mute alone.
args.effort: High: revise the wearable PCB/enclosure and microphone power path, validate pop/noise behavior, add sealed tactile switch and LED visibility tests, implement firmware state/event logging, and thread the authoritative state through relay, Mac, and dashboard. The current nRF9160 development kit is explicitly provisional, so this belongs in the product hardware rather than a workaround.
args.risk: A damaged or ambiguous switch could leave the owner uncertain; use hard two-state detents, a fail-quiet electrical design, startup self-test, and a visible disagreement fault. Cutting microphone power may require codec reinitialization and lose the first audio frame after unmute; announce readiness with haptic/LED feedback. Recovery is physical switch movement, not a hidden software override.
args.cost_impact: Roughly $2–6 BOM increase for switch, LED driver, fuel gauge/RTC support, PCB/enclosure changes, plus validation NRE; negligible steady-state power increase and likely a small power saving while muted. No API/model cost.
args.latency_impact: Unmute-to-ready may add 100–300 ms for codec startup; mute is immediate at the electrical path. Privacy-state propagation to relay/Mac should be best-effort and never delay the local cutoff.
args.security_impact: This is a defense-in-depth boundary: audio cannot leave the device while the switch is muted. Log only transition timestamps/counters, not audio; authenticate state events and make the physical state higher priority than server commands.
depends_on: A firmware privacy-state event and durable transition counter
Relay/Mac audio pipelines honoring hardware mute as an authoritative deny
Dashboard/briefing UI that shows the last observed physical privacy state and any telemetry gap

args.user_asks: If I get interrupted halfway through something, save exactly where we were and let me safely resume it later from the pendant.
args.why_useful: Today a conversation, browser tabs, and a half-filled form can all be lost when attention shifts. This creates a durable, human-readable escrow: the original request, evidence gathered, reversible changes already made, exact next step, expiry/deadline, and what still needs approval. The owner can resume without repeating themselves or accidentally sending a stale action.
args.model_tier: Realtime model only for the brief spoken interruption/resume exchange and final approval question; a cheaper background model compiles evidence and a deterministic state machine validates and resumes the plan.
args.latency_budget: Capture interruption in under 1 second; resume card spoken in under 3 seconds. Background compilation may take minutes while the owner is away.
args.cost_estimate: Roughly $0.01–$0.05 per background packet, dominated by private-page extraction and audio generation; resume voice turn uses the normal realtime budget.
args.security_concerns: Private tab contents and draft data leave the browser only through the authenticated relay. Never persist secrets or raw screenshots by default. Sending, deleting, purchasing, or submitting remains a fresh confirmation. Expire stale packets and provide one-tap discard.
missing: A durable interruption-escrow state machine with explicit states (captured, awaiting-owner, stale, resumed, discarded)
Atomic checkpointing of Mac jobs and browser command queues so a checkpoint cannot claim an action that did not complete
A pendant-readable resume queue with offline acknowledgement and replay protection
Owner-visible packet diff showing what changed since capture

args.change: Add an interruption-escrow coordinator between the existing planner, job runner, browser queue, receipts, and pendant audio pipeline. At every irreversible boundary and on link loss, atomically write a checkpoint containing intent hash, completed action receipts, browser tab/session IDs, evidence references, next safe step, required confirmation, expiry, and a monotonic resume token. Expose a compact spoken resume queue and a dashboard diff; resuming revalidates page freshness and job state before executing anything.
args.why_useful_to_owner: A dropped connection or sudden distraction would stop being a lost half-finished task. The owner can hear one accurate sentence later and continue exactly where they left off, without duplicate clicks or stale submissions.
args.effort: Medium-high: coordinator/state machine, transactional hooks in Mac and browser runners, pendant queue protocol, and crash/replay tests.
args.risk: A bad checkpoint could replay an action twice or present stale evidence. Default to no-op on uncertainty, require confirmation for irreversible steps, use idempotency keys and receipts, and allow discard/undo. Recovery is to invalidate the resume token and leave the underlying job untouched.
args.cost_impact: Negligible storage/compute; one small background summarization call per interrupted packet, with optional TTS cost only when surfaced.
args.latency_impact: Under 1 second to checkpoint; 1–3 seconds to produce a spoken resume card. No added latency on ordinary completed actions beyond a small write.
args.security_impact: Persist references and hashes rather than raw page content or secrets; enforce per-owner auth and short TTL; redact sensitive fields from spoken summaries.
depends_on: Durable job runner and browser command queue must emit atomic action receipts
Pendant delivery acknowledgement/offline queue
Cross-surface state persistence and stale-evidence revalidation

args.user_asks: When I leave something somewhere or put something on hold, let me ask later where it is and what I was supposed to do with it.
args.why_useful: People lose physical objects and the intention attached to them, not just the objects themselves. A quick pendant button press or spoken 'remember this' would create a private, time-and-place memory; later the pendant can answer 'where are my passport and the forms I still need to send?' instead of forcing the owner to reconstruct the moment.
args.model_tier: Realtime only for capture confirmation and the later short answer. A cheaper background model performs entity linking and summarizes the memory; vision runs only when the owner explicitly asks to inspect a photo or scene.
args.latency_budget: Capture acknowledgement under 500 ms locally, even without connectivity. Retrieval answer under 3 seconds when online; offline retrieval from the pendant's recent index under 1 second.
args.cost_estimate: About $0.005–$0.03 per memory after capture, dominated by optional transcription/vision embedding; negligible cost for offline text-only entries.
args.security_concerns: This can reveal home layout, possessions, travel documents, and locations. Store recent entries encrypted, default to coarse location and short retention, never upload a scene/photo without explicit consent, and require confirmation before sharing a location or acting on an attached intention.
missing: A pendant-local encrypted memory capsule with button-triggered audio/text capture and bounded retention
A cross-surface entity-and-intention linker that can join a spoken capture to Mac notes, calendar, email, browser pages, and optional photos

args.change: Add a local 'place-memory capsule' to the pendant: a long-press captures up to 10 seconds of audio plus timestamp, monotonic event ID, and coarse device/location context; encrypts it at rest, keeps a bounded ring of the newest entries, and uploads only after an explicit sync policy permits. The server returns a signed receipt and can tombstone individual entries; retrieval must work from the local ring when offline.
args.why_useful_to_owner: The owner can preserve a fleeting physical-world fact with one deliberate gesture and recover it later even when the network or Mac is unavailable, without keeping the microphone continuously active.
args.effort: Medium firmware plus relay protocol work; requires encrypted storage, button debounce/UI feedback, upload retry, tombstones, and a small retrieval endpoint.
args.risk: Accidental captures, sensitive recordings, flash wear, and lost keys could expose private information. Mitigate with a short fixed maximum, LED/haptic/audio acknowledgement, retention limits, authenticated encryption with device-bound keys, and an unmistakable delete gesture.
args.cost_impact: No API cost for local capture; roughly 1–3 MB flash reserved for a bounded ring depending on codec. Estimated under 5 mW average while recording, plus brief radio upload cost.
args.latency_impact: Immediate local acknowledgement; upload is deferred and must not block conversation. Offline retrieval is sub-second for recent entries.
args.security_impact: This creates a new sensitive data class (location-linked personal memory). Encrypt locally and in transit, minimize metadata precision, prohibit background capture, and require explicit owner opt-in before cloud sync.

A relay endpoint for signed, idempotent memory receipts and deletion tombstones
Owner retention and sync policy

args.change: Ship a negotiated 24-kHz superwideband Opus profile end to end: capture at the actual 15,625-Hz I2S rate, resample once with a fixed-point polyphase stage to 24 kHz, encode mono Opus at an explicit 24-kHz/24–32-kbps profile, and advertise that profile in the session handshake. Keep the existing 16-kHz/16-kbps mode as a fallback selected by measured CPU/packet-loss budget. On the relay, remove any implicit 16-kHz downsample, preserve the profile in queued audio jobs and receipts, and validate decoded sample rate/frame duration before delivery. On playback, retain the existing 24-kHz decode but replace the 31,250-Hz wire-clock assumption with a negotiated rate conversion contract so the ESP32's mandatory 44.1-kHz SBC path remains the only final resample. Add loopback fixtures for tones, speech, packet loss, and clock drift; reject a session rather than silently claiming 24 kHz when a stage falls back.
args.why_useful_to_owner: The pendant would sound intelligibly fuller and less muffled for both live replies and queued briefings, with no false promise that '24 kHz' survived the trip. Calls remain usable when bandwidth or battery is poor because fallback is explicit, not a broken half-upgrade.
args.effort: Medium-high: firmware resampler/profile and handshake, relay transcode/schema updates, ESP32 clock-contract update, and hardware-in-the-loop audio fixtures. The current implementation is a prototype and the owner explicitly asked to ship this path.
args.risk: A second resampler and higher Opus bitrate can increase CPU, latency, airtime, and dropouts; current hardware reports ~87% of one core when encode and decode both run. Mitigate by benchmarking encode-only/decode-only separately, selecting profile before streaming, bounded jitter buffers, and automatic fallback. Never silently mix 16-kHz and 24-kHz timestamps. Recovery is reconnect into the legacy profile.
args.cost_impact: No API-model cost change. Rough firmware/storage work fits existing flash but needs profiling; 24–32 kbps uses about 1.5–2x radio airtime versus 16 kbps, with corresponding modem energy increase. A production device may need a better audio codec/DSP if the nRF9160 cannot sustain duplex headroom.
args.latency_impact: Target unchanged 60-ms frames plus <=20 ms resampling; expect roughly 5–15 ms extra buffering during negotiation and possibly higher airtime latency. Keep live voice on the realtime tier; queued audio can use the cheaper background path.
args.security_impact: Audio remains encrypted in the existing authenticated session; profile metadata and loopback diagnostics should exclude raw speech by default. Store only hashes/metrics in receipts, apply short retention to generated audio, and require explicit opt-in before uploading diagnostic clips.
depends_on: Relay must expose and persist negotiated audio profile rather than assuming 16 kHz
Firmware needs a fixed-point 15,625→24,000 resampler and CPU/RAM benchmark
ESP32 bridge must accept the negotiated wire-clock contract while retaining its 44.1-kHz SBC constraint
End-to-end loopback and packet-loss test fixture

args.user_asks: “I’m leaving—pack up what I’m doing so I can continue from the pendant, and pick it back up when I return.”
args.why_useful: Today leaving the desk severs context: open Mac work, authenticated browser tabs, and half-finished plans are not converted into something usable while walking. This creates an intentional, privacy-bounded handoff: a short spoken queue for the commute, a resumable workspace on the Mac, and a clear return point rather than a vague promise that an agent kept working.
args.model_tier: Use the realtime tier only to hear the short departure/return command and deliver the first acknowledgment. Use a cheaper background model to summarize the captured workspace and rank next steps; use the local Mac planner for app/browser state and no cloud model for raw private page contents unless the owner permits it.
args.latency_budget: Acknowledge in under 1 second. Capture Mac/browser state in 5–15 seconds, produce a 30–90 second audio queue in under 60 seconds, and make the return workspace available as soon as the Mac reconnects. Offline pendant playback must not wait for the Mac.
args.cost_estimate: One small background summarization per handoff (roughly a few cents or less depending on transcript/page volume); realtime cost is limited to two short utterances. Dominant costs are private-page extraction and audio generation, not orchestration.
args.security_concerns: Snapshot only the active window, selected browser tabs, task text, and provenance—not arbitrary screenshots or full page bodies. Redact secrets and mark authenticated excerpts as private. Never send mail, submit forms, or alter files as part of packing. Returning may reopen sensitive tabs, so require a local button press or spoken confirmation if the snapshot contains private browser sessions. Expire the handoff after 24 hours and provide one-tap deletion.
missing: A first-class handoff snapshot schema tying Mac window/app state, browser tab/session IDs, plan/job IDs, and pendant audio-item IDs together
A local pendant queue/marker that survives a dropped link and reports played/paused/expired state
A return-time revalidation step that checks tabs/files have not changed before reopening or continuing
Reliable browser bridge connectivity and explicit offline behavior (current home-chrome is offline with pending commands)
A compact audio renderer/acknowledgment path with the negotiated 24-kHz profile

args.change: Add a durable Handoff Envelope that links one departure snapshot across /capture, /plan, /execute, Mac job receipts, browser session/tab IDs, pipeline audio items, and pendant delivery state. The envelope stores a redacted task summary, source references and hashes, precondition/evidence timestamps, expiration, owner approval scope, and a resume policy. Packing is append-only; returning first revalidates each source and marks changed/missing tabs or files for review instead of replaying stale actions. Expose one status/undo/delete operation so the owner can say 'what did I pack?', discard it, or resume the safe subset.
args.why_useful_to_owner: It turns the proposed leave/return experience from a collection of jobs into one trustworthy bookmark. The owner can walk away without losing the thread and can see exactly why a return action was or was not resumed, even when the browser was offline or the Mac rebooted.
args.effort: Medium: shared schema plus adapters around existing capture/planning/job/session/audio receipts, durable storage, and a small resume UI/voice vocabulary. No new model is required.
args.risk: Adapters may disagree about identifiers or accidentally replay stale actions. Use immutable envelope IDs, source hashes, TTL, explicit 'changed' state, and default to read-only resume; destructive actions remain confirmation-gated. If one surface fails, preserve the envelope and deliver a partial handoff.
args.cost_impact: Negligible API cost; one compact background summary and optional audio render per envelope. Storage is small metadata plus references, not copied private pages or screenshots.
args.latency_impact: Packing adds roughly 1–3 seconds for metadata and 5–60 seconds for optional summary/audio. Return begins with a fast receipt lookup, then revalidation in background; no need to block spoken acknowledgment.
args.security_impact: Improves security by centralizing redaction, TTL, deletion, and provenance. Do not duplicate authenticated content into relay prompts; retain tab/file references and hashes, encrypt any audio, and log access without raw contents.
depends_on: A durable pendant audio queue/marker and delivery acknowledgment
The negotiated 24-kHz audio contract (or explicit fallback metadata)
Browser bridge reconnect/offline queue with stable session and tab affinity
Faculty-action checkpoint/receipt protocol for any resumed mutation

args.user_asks: “Stay with me quietly in this conversation. When I ask you something, check my private notes and logged-in work pages, then whisper only a short, sourced answer through the pendant.”
args.why_useful: The owner can participate in a meeting or conversation without stopping to search their Mac. The pendant provides the ears and discreet audio; the Mac and authenticated browser provide reach into private material; the relay keeps the interaction low-latency. This is different from a meeting brief or a background digest: it answers a question arising now, with citations and a deliberate silence when evidence is insufficient.
args.model_tier: Realtime handles the short spoken request and final one-sentence response. A cheaper background/local model retrieves and ranks notes and authenticated pages; the Mac/browser agents perform only read-only searches. Escalate to the expensive model only when sources conflict or the owner asks for synthesis.
args.latency_budget: Acknowledge within 300 ms and return a sourced answer within 3 seconds for cached/local notes, or 8 seconds for authenticated browser retrieval. The pendant must say 'I don't have enough evidence' rather than fill silence with a guess.
args.cost_estimate: Usually one short realtime turn plus a low-cost retrieval/reranking call, well under a few cents per question; browser extraction and repeated audio delivery dominate, not the model reasoning.
args.security_concerns: Requires an explicit session start and a visible/audio recording indicator; default to no raw meeting-audio retention. Only search allowlisted notes and currently selected browser sessions, never arbitrary mail or accounts. Cite source title and freshness without reading sensitive excerpts aloud unless requested. args.user_asks: “Can I take this on?” When I mention a new request or opportunity, compare it with my real commitments and deadlines, tell me the tradeoff in one short spoken answer, and—if it does not fit—draft a polite renegotiation or decline for my approval.
args.why_useful: People accept work conversationally before seeing the collision. This would turn the pendant into a timely decision aid: it checks calendar, existing promises, open tasks, and the relevant logged-in thread, then makes the cost visible without silently committing or sending anything.
args.model_tier: Use the realtime tier only to capture the request and ask one clarification; use a cheaper background model to reconcile commitments and draft alternatives. Mac/browser agents retrieve evidence; the relay persists a decision packet and schedules a follow-up if the owner says “later.”
args.latency_budget: A spoken feasibility answer within 5 seconds when local context is warm; up to 30 seconds for authenticated browser evidence. If evidence is slow, say what is known, continue in background, and return a cited packet rather than blocking the conversation.
args.cost_estimate: About $0.01–$0.05 per evaluation depending on browser pages and draft length; browser extraction and re-sent context dominate, not the brief spoken response.
args.security_concerns: Read-only access to calendar, mail, task systems, and logged-in pages is needed; private snippets should stay in the relay's short-lived encrypted packet and be minimized in audio. Never send, accept, decline, or create a commitment without explicit confirmation. Treat deadlines and availability as uncertain when stale, and show source/time for consequential claims.
missing: A first-class commitment/obligation index joining Calendar, Mail, Notes, reminders, and authenticated browser evidence
A decision packet with evidence, alternatives, expiry, and explicit approve/edit/reject state
A cross-surface impact scan that detects schedule/deadline collisions and distinguishes hard commitments from tentative ideas
Owner-configurable workload assumptions (working hours, buffers, protected time, and what counts as an automatic no)

args.change: Add a commitment-collision compiler between capture/pipeline and the existing Mac/browser execution surfaces. On a spoken “can I take this on?” event, normalize the request into a candidate commitment, retrieve dated evidence from Calendar/Mail/Notes/reminders and authenticated browser tabs, classify each item as hard/soft/unknown, compute time and deadline collisions with explicit freshness, and persist a signed decision packet containing sources, assumptions, three options (accept/defer/decline), and an expiry. The relay speaks only the conclusion; the Mac creates a draft or reminder only after the owner chooses. Emit status and receipt events so a delayed browser result cannot overwrite a newer decision.
args.why_useful_to_owner: The owner gets an answer at the moment of commitment instead of discovering the conflict later, with a defensible explanation and a ready draft—but no accidental acceptance or message send.
args.effort: Medium-high: typed schema plus evidence adapters, temporal/conflict scoring, packet persistence, stale-result handling, and a small review UI/audio renderer. Start with Calendar + reminders + one browser session, then add Mail and task boards.
args.risk: False collision or missed promise could cause the owner to decline something valuable; stale private-page data could mislead. Mitigate by labeling uncertainty, quoting evidence timestamps, defaulting to “needs review,” and keeping all outward actions drafts until explicit approval. Recover by packet versioning and undo for reminders/drafts.
args.cost_impact: Low recurring model cost if extraction is cached; roughly $0.01–$0.05 per decision, with browser reads and long context dominating. Storage is a small JSON packet plus redacted evidence hashes.
args.latency_impact: Warm local answer 2–5 seconds; authenticated browser evidence may take 10–30 seconds and should complete asynchronously with a spoken provisional answer.
args.security_impact: Expands correlation of sensitive commitments across surfaces. Encrypt packets, minimize quoted content, enforce per-source scopes, expire raw snippets quickly, and require explicit confirmation for any draft creation or external change.
depends_on: A typed commitment/obligation schema and provenance-aware context projection
A durable decision-packet inbox/review endpoint
Authenticated browser bridge availability for private pages (currently owner must reconnect it)
A clear owner policy for working hours, buffers, and protected commitments

args.change: Add a coin vibration motor (or low-power LRA with driver), a second tactile button, and a physical microphone-mute/privacy slider to the pendant revision. Expose a tiny local event protocol: short buzz = pending decision, double buzz = evidence ready, long press = mute/cancel and queue acknowledgement offline. Keep audio unchanged; the nRF9160's GPIO/SPI budget and 211,608 B app RAM are sufficient, while the motor driver isolates current spikes from the modem/audio rail.
args.why_useful_to_owner: The owner can notice and control an important decision in a meeting, street, or quiet room without broadcasting speech or looking at a screen; the mute slider gives an immediate, trustworthy privacy boundary even when software is confused.
args.effort: Low-to-medium hardware spin: motor, driver transistor/IC, button, slider, enclosure and firmware event mapping; requires board revision and power characterization on the prototype DK before productizing.
args.risk: Vibration can annoy or drain the battery, and accidental presses could cancel a task. Use intensity/duty limits, quiet hours, distinct patterns, and require a deliberate long press for cancellation; if the motor fails, LED/audio remain available. Validate modem transmit current and audio noise during vibration.
args.cost_impact: Approximately $2–$6 BOM increase in volume (more on prototype), with brief vibration bursts adding tens of mA for under a second; negligible idle draw if switched off.
args.latency_impact: Immediate local feedback (<100 ms) for mute, cancel, and acknowledgement; no network round trip required.
args.security_impact: The physical mute slider should gate microphone power locally, not merely set a software flag. Record only coarse mute/unmute events, never raw audio; keep cancellation local and idempotent when replayed.
depends_on: Define the cross-surface attention/decision event schema
Pendant firmware event queue and offline replay
Power/audio coexistence test on the nRF9160 development hardware

I recorded and proposed:

1. **“Can I take this on?”** — compare a conversationally mentioned opportunity against calendar, reminders, mail, notes, and authenticated pages; explain the tradeoff and prepare (but never send) an accept/defer/decline response.
2. **Commitment-collision compiler** — a concrete integration layer that creates versioned, evidence-backed decision packets with freshness, uncertainty, alternatives, expiry, and explicit approval.
3. **Hardware revision** — add a low-power haptic actuator, acknowledgement button, and physical microphone-mute slider so the owner can handle private prompts without speaking aloud.

What is still needed:

- Reconnect the browser bridge manually on the Mac; the earlier automation attempts failed because the bridge is offline and the generated action payloads were malformed.
- A typed commitment/obligation index spanning Calendar, Mail, Notes, reminders, and browser evidence.
- A durable decision-packet inbox with approve/edit/reject state and stale-result protection.

args.user_asks: “Who was that person I just spoke with, and what should I remember for next time?” After I explicitly mark a conversation as worth remembering, identify the meeting or contact from my calendar/Mac, assemble a private relationship card from what was actually said plus clearly separated public context, and make it available from the pendant before my next interaction.
args.why_useful: People lose valuable social context because names, roles, promises, and personal details arrive while their hands are occupied. This gives the owner durable, privacy-respecting continuity without requiring note-taking during a conversation. It must distinguish observed facts from inference and let the owner correct or delete the card.
args.model_tier: Realtime handles only the explicit “remember this” marker and a short confirmation. A cheaper background model extracts facts, links the conversation to a calendar/contact candidate, and summarizes public context. The relay stores the result and serves a short pre-meeting audio reminder later.
args.latency_budget: A local acknowledgement under 1 second; a preliminary identity candidate within 10 seconds; enrichment and relationship-card construction can take minutes asynchronously. Before the next meeting, deliver a 15–30 second spoken card.
args.cost_estimate: Roughly $0.02–$0.10 per saved conversation, dominated by transcription, entity resolution, and optional web enrichment. Most retrievals should be cached and text-only.
args.security_concerns: Conversation audio and relationship data are highly sensitive. Recording must require an explicit local gesture or spoken confirmation, with a visible/haptic recording indicator and an immediate cancel/delete control. Never record continuously by default, never infer sensitive traits, and never send a message or expose the card to another person without confirmation. Public enrichment must be source-labeled and limited to the identified person.
missing: An explicit, local conversation-bookmark event with start/stop boundaries and a deletion window
On-device or relay-side short audio capture/transcription that can retain only the bookmarked segment
Calendar/contact identity resolution with ranked candidates and an owner correction flow
A relationship-card data model separating direct observations, owner-entered facts, and public sources with independent retention controls
A pre-meeting trigger that can deliver a selected card to the pendant without replaying private conversation audio

args.change: Create a consent-scoped relationship memory layer distinct from generic capture/context-graph storage. A local bookmark event opens a bounded audio segment; the relay derives a structured card with three physically separate provenance classes—heard directly, owner-confirmed, and externally sourced—plus retention/deletion deadlines and an identity-confidence score. Before any card is spoken, a resolver must match it to a calendar/contact candidate and require correction when confidence is low. Pre-meeting delivery retrieves only the fields selected by the owner, never raw audio, and every card supports one-button purge from the pendant.
args.why_useful_to_owner: The owner can remember people and context naturally after a meaningful interaction, then receive a useful reminder before seeing them again, without trusting an opaque permanent recording or being surprised by an invented fact.
args.effort: High: pendant bookmark firmware and local indicators, bounded audio handling, entity resolution, provenance-aware schema, encryption/retention jobs, correction UI, and pre-meeting delivery integration.
args.risk: Misidentification or a hallucinated personal detail could damage a relationship; accidental recording could violate privacy. Mitigate with explicit start/stop consent, short automatic deletion of unconfirmed clips, confidence thresholds, source citations, no sensitive-attribute inference, and default silence when identity is unresolved.
args.cost_impact: Moderate per saved interaction: transcription and optional enrichment are the main costs, approximately $0.02–$0.10; storage stays small after deleting raw audio. Hardware cost is unchanged if existing button/LED can signal bookmarking, otherwise a dedicated haptic/privacy control is needed.
args.latency_impact: Bookmark acknowledgement is local and immediate; card generation is asynchronous. Pre-meeting retrieval should be under 3 seconds, with a compact spoken summary rendered once and cached.
args.security_impact: This creates a sensitive social-memory dataset. Encrypt it separately from ordinary notes, enforce per-card retention, audit every read, keep raw audio ephemeral, and make physical mute/delete override all server state as soon as connectivity returns.
depends_on: A firmware-level explicit bookmark/delete event and recording indicator
A provenance and privacy-aware relationship-card schema
Calendar/contact identity resolver with owner correction
Durable encrypted retention and purge processing
A pre-meeting scheduler that can target the pendant

transcript.text:
Recorded a new capability and implementation change: **consent-based relationship memory**.

The owner should be able to explicitly bookmark a meaningful conversation, have the system identify the person and meeting, separate directly heard facts from owner-confirmed and public information, and receive a short private reminder before the next interaction.

It would require:

- A local start/stop bookmark gesture with visible or haptic recording feedback.
- Bounded audio capture and rapid deletion of unconfirmed clips.
- Calendar/contact identity resolution with confidence and correction.
- Provenance-separated relationship cards.
- Independent retention, encryption, audit, and physical purge controls.
- Pre-meeting pendant delivery of selected card fields, never raw conversation audio.

args.user_asks: Before you brief me or act, tell me what is actually true across my pendant, Mac, browser, and relay—flag contradictions and stale status instead of confidently repeating them, and give me one safe next step to repair each problem.
args.why_useful: Today the system can simultaneously report a completed/healthy workflow, an offline browser with queued commands, a stale pipeline stuck in processing, and a briefing claiming Calendar/Mail grants are missing even though the live permission snapshot says automation is granted. The owner needs a trustworthy decision, not a fluent synthesis of conflicting records.
args.model_tier: Background/cheap model performs claim extraction, timestamp comparison, and contradiction clustering; realtime is used only to speak the short, owner-facing verdict when requested. Escalate to the expensive tier only when contradictions affect an irreversible action.
args.latency_budget: Under 2 seconds from cached snapshots; under 10 seconds when refreshing Mac/browser/relay evidence. Never block an urgent spoken reply on a nonessential source.
args.cost_estimate: Usually <$0.01 per reconciliation using a small model over compact typed claims; occasional realtime speech dominates interactive cost. Storage is a few KB per snapshot/claim, with short retention for sensitive browser facts.
args.security_concerns: Authenticated page contents, mail/calendar metadata, and device telemetry must stay in the existing private surfaces; send only hashes/typed claims to the reconciliation layer where possible. Never expose secrets or infer that a queued command ran. Require confirmation before repair actions, browser submissions, mail, deletion, or replaying pending commands.
missing: A durable, provenance-aware claim ledger with source timestamps, TTLs, and status values (current, stale, contradicted, unreachable).
A reconciliation pass that compares /ops/status permissions against generated briefings and compares pipeline state against relay/device acknowledgements.
A spoken-safe formatter that suppresses contradicted claims and emits evidence plus a reversible repair proposal.
A repair workflow that rechecks preconditions immediately before action and records the resulting receipt.

args.change: Add a cross-surface Truth Ledger and gate every spoken brief/action plan on it. Each observation becomes a typed claim {subject,predicate,value,source,observedAt,expiresAt,confidence,sensitivity}; reconciliation marks claims current, stale, contradicted, or unreachable. For contradictions, retain both evidence records, prefer direct live probes over cached/generated artifacts, and require a fresh probe before any dependent action. The formatter must say 'I have conflicting reports' rather than selecting a plausible value. Add a repair transaction that refreshes the relevant source, re-evaluates preconditions, and records a receipt without replaying queued browser commands.
args.why_useful_to_owner: The pendant would stop telling you that Mail needs a grant when the live Mac snapshot says it has one, stop calling a dead browser online, and stop treating a half-open pipeline as completed. You get a short, honest answer and a safe recovery path instead of discovering later that the system acted on stale state.
args.effort: Medium: typed claim schema, a small D1/local JSON ledger, reconciliation rules, and adapters for existing status/briefing/pipeline/browser routes; then add a pre-speech and pre-action hook.
args.risk: Incorrect TTLs could make the assistant over-cautious or hide a real update. Recover by preserving raw evidence, allowing an explicit 'refresh and decide' command, and failing closed only for irreversible actions. Avoid deleting existing records.
args.cost_impact: Negligible storage and small-model classification cost; compact claims reduce repeated context tokens. Live refreshes add API calls only when a claim is stale or action-critical.
args.latency_impact: No noticeable delay from cached reconciliation; 1–10 seconds for source refresh, with immediate provisional wording if the owner is waiting.
args.security_impact: Improves security by preventing stale/private browser evidence from being presented as current and by keeping page contents on their owning surface. Claim sensitivity labels must prevent secrets from entering shared prompts or audio.
depends_on: A durable cross-surface event/receipt identity shared by relay, Mac, browser, and pendant
A freshness policy for each source and explicit precedence rules
Existing /ops/status, /briefing/latest, /browser/status, /pipeline, and job receipt adapters

transcript.text:
I still need one foundational layer: a **cross-surface truth ledger**.

The live system currently has contradictory reports:

- `/ops/status`: Calendar and Mail automation are granted.
- `/briefing/latest`: says both need an Automation grant.
- `/browser/status`: Chrome is offline with 12 queued commands.
- `/pipeline`: contains completed runs alongside runs still marked `processing`.

I proposed:

1. **Truth Ledger and freshness gate** — claims carry source, timestamp, expiry, confidence, and sensitivity; contradictions are spoken as contradictions rather than silently resolved.
2. **Incident timeline and safe retry** — correlate pendant → relay → Mac → browser → audio receipts, explain where a request stalled, and preview retries without replaying potentially destructive actions.

What I still need is not another owner permission. I need the implementation to connect the existing routes—status, briefing, pipeline, browser, journal, jobs, and receipts—with:

- Stable correlation IDs across every surface.
- Explicit freshness and source-precedence rules.
- A pre-speech/pre-action contradiction check.
- Duplicate-risk detection before retries.
- Redacted, short spoken explanations for failures.

Until that exists, the system should conservatively say **“I have conflicting reports”** rather than claim that a task, permission, or delivery is complete.

args.user_asks: Before I commit to something, let me rehearse the consequences: check my calendar, current commitments, private messages, travel or account details, and active browser work; show what this choice would collide with, what it would make harder, and a few safe alternatives—without changing anything.
args.why_useful: The owner can ask the system to execute isolated tasks, but cannot yet ask it to reason about a life decision across all of the places where consequences are distributed. A rehearsal would prevent accidental overbooking, missed obligations, contradictory replies, and commitments made without seeing the relevant private context. It is advice and simulation, not autonomous action.
args.model_tier: Use a cheaper background reasoning model to gather and normalize facts and generate multiple scenarios; use the realtime tier only for the short spoken result and follow-up questions. Escalate to the expensive tier only when evidence conflicts or the decision has high stakes.
args.latency_budget: A quick rehearsal in 5 seconds from cached context; a thorough one in 20 seconds with fresh private-page checks. The pendant should give an immediate acknowledgement while the deeper analysis runs.
args.cost_estimate: Roughly $0.01–$0.05 per rehearsal, dominated by authenticated browser reads and synthesis rather than speech. Cache stable obligations and only refresh volatile sources.
args.security_concerns: Keep mail, calendar, account, and page contents on their owning surfaces; pass typed facts and redacted excerpts to the judge where possible. Clearly label inference versus evidence. No messages, bookings, edits, or submissions occur in rehearsal mode; any conversion to action requires a new confirmation and a fresh precondition check.
missing: A read-only scenario/rehearsal contract that takes a proposed commitment plus constraints and returns impacts, uncertainties, and alternatives.
A cross-surface obligation model that links calendar events, reminders, messages, browser transactions, travel details, and active work without copying sensitive payloads unnecessarily.
A temporal consequence engine for detecting collisions, deadlines, dependencies, and opportunity costs.
An explicit boundary in the action layer preventing rehearsal outputs from becoming queued mutations, plus provenance for every cited consequence.

args.change: Introduce a visibly separate `REHEARSE` conversation state spanning pendant, relay, Mac, and browser. In this state, all retrieved facts are assembled into an immutable scenario snapshot; the judge may branch alternatives and calculate consequences, but the action router is structurally unable to enqueue mutations. The owner can say `make this real` only after reviewing a compact delta that lists every proposed change, affected surface, evidence age, uncertainty, and duplicate risk; that phrase creates a new action plan rather than upgrading the rehearsal in place.
args.why_useful_to_owner: They can explore consequential choices while walking or away from the Mac without fear that asking 'what if?' will send a message, alter a calendar, replay a browser command, or spend a scarce approval. The owner gets understandable alternatives first and deliberate execution second.
args.effort: Medium-to-large: add a scenario snapshot and branch format to the relay protocol, propagate mode through planner and browser requests, enforce a deny-by-construction mutation guard, then add a review-to-action transition with fresh preconditions.
args.risk: A stale snapshot could produce an attractive but wrong rehearsal. Show observation times, mark unknowns, refresh volatile facts before conversion to action, and expire snapshots quickly. If mode metadata is lost, fail closed as read-only.
args.cost_impact: Small persistent metadata and one additional synthesis call when branching alternatives; no mutation or browser-action cost during rehearsal. Realtime speech remains limited to acknowledgement and summary.
args.latency_impact: Immediate local acknowledgement; 5–20 seconds for scenario assembly depending on private-source refreshes. Conversion adds a final precondition check.
args.security_impact: Strongly reduces accidental side effects and prevents scenario text from being mistaken for executable intent. Sensitive evidence remains source-local and only redacted claims enter the scenario snapshot.
depends_on: A cross-surface typed fact/obligation projection
Stable provenance and freshness metadata
A mutation-deny guard enforced below the planner, not merely in prompts
Existing job, browser, pipeline, and receipt identifiers

args.user_asks: Keep my pendant’s speech clear automatically as I move between a quiet room, a noisy street, and a Mac/browser call—without making me run a calibration each time.
args.why_useful: The owner gets consistent intelligibility during the moments they actually rely on the pendant. A tiny device can sense acoustic conditions, the relay can choose a safe low-latency profile, and the Mac/browser can apply the matching input/output route; each change is reversible and reported in one short receipt.
args.model_tier: Use a deterministic/on-device classifier and cheap relay DSP scorer for routine environment changes; reserve realtime model only for ambiguous transitions or when the owner asks why audio changed. No background LLM call is needed for ordinary profile switches.
args.latency_budget: Classify locally in under 100 ms; relay decision and profile push under 300 ms; Mac/browser application under 1 s. Never interrupt speech for a profile change; queue it until an utterance boundary.
args.cost_estimate: Usually <$0.001 per transition (telemetry plus deterministic DSP); occasional explanation costs one realtime turn. Storage is a few hundred bytes per transition plus profile definitions.
args.security_concerns: Transmit features/levels, not raw room audio, by default; discard any calibration snippets immediately after scoring. Call apps and browser tab identity are sensitive, so expose only the selected route/profile in receipts. Require confirmation before changing a call’s active microphone or camera; volume/EQ and reversible device selection may follow the owner’s existing automation policy.
missing: A versioned audio-profile schema shared by firmware, relay, Mac, and browser (input gain, AGC, noise suppression, codec mode, output EQ, route);
a firmware acoustic-feature sampler that fits the 211,608 B application-RAM budget and emits no raw audio;
a relay profile state machine with hysteresis, utterance-boundary application, rollback, and durable receipts;
Mac/browser adapters that can apply and verify profiles through the existing granted AppleScript/high-level actions, plus a dashboard timeline of profile changes;
acceptance tests for 24 kHz speech intelligibility, transition latency, clipping, and privacy deletion.

args.change: Add an event-boundary audio adaptation service: compute 10 Hz bands/level/noise-floor/clipping features locally, classify quiet/voice-noise/music/wind with hysteresis, and publish only a signed profile recommendation (not raw audio) over the existing audio/events path. args.why_useful_to_owner: Speech remains understandable without the owner fiddling with settings, while a long press gives them an immediate, dependable way to stop automation in a sensitive environment.
args.effort: Medium firmware work plus relay contract and Mac/browser adapters; 2–3 weeks including acoustic acceptance tests.
args.risk: A wrong classifier could make audio worse or change during a call. Hysteresis, confidence thresholds, utterance-boundary application, profile rollback, and a freeze gesture recover safely; default profile remains unchanged on link loss.
args.cost_impact: No meaningful API cost; roughly 8–16 KB code, under 6 KB RAM, and negligible flash writes if recommendations are rate-limited. Hardware cost $0 on prototype.
args.latency_impact: Feature windows add 100 ms; profile changes take effect within 1 s but never mid-utterance.
args.security_impact: Only coarse acoustic features and signed recommendations leave the pendant; no raw room audio is retained. Freeze gesture is local and works offline.

A 24 kHz intelligibility/clipping acceptance scorer

args.user_asks: If the pendant or relay is unsure what I said, catch the bad phrase before anything happens, ask me for only that phrase, and then continue the original request without making me start over.
args.why_useful: Today a noisy or clipped word can turn a perfectly good spoken request into a failed action or, worse, the wrong action. The owner should experience a two-second, targeted repair instead of repeating an entire multi-step thought or discovering the mistake afterward.
args.model_tier: Use streaming ASR confidence, acoustic clipping features, and deterministic entity/action validation first. Invoke the realtime model only to formulate the shortest repair question and reconcile the corrected span; use a cheaper background model for post-action quality analytics.
args.latency_budget: Detect a suspect span within 250 ms of the utterance end and ask within 700 ms. Preserve the original intent for up to 30 seconds while waiting; never block unrelated audio or silently guess after the repair window expires.
args.cost_estimate: Routine turns add negligible DSP/metadata cost; roughly one extra realtime turn only when a repair is needed, typically <$0.01 per repair. Keep only the original and corrected transcript spans plus hashes, not raw audio.
args.security_concerns: The system must not execute an irreversible action while any required slot is uncertain. Show the owner the exact disputed word/field on the Mac when available, speak no sensitive surrounding transcript aloud in public, and expire the pending intent locally and server-side after 30 seconds. Confirmation remains mandatory for sending, deleting, purchasing, or other destructive actions.
missing: A typed utterance-repair protocol carrying span offsets, confidence, acoustic-failure reason, preserved intent, expiry, and corrected value across pendant and relay
A deterministic pre-action validator that marks which slots are safety-critical and refuses to fill them by best guess
A low-memory pendant clipping/noise feature stream and a local retry tone/button path that works through a dropped link
A faculty-action transaction hold that can resume the same plan after one corrected span, with a receipt showing original, repair, and final values
Mac/browser UI support for highlighting the disputed field without replaying the entire request

args.change: Introduce a first-class 'uncertain span' transaction state between perception and action. The planner must carry the original intent and all resolved slots, mark only low-confidence spans, ask one targeted spoken repair, then re-run validation and produce a diff before releasing the action. If the link drops, the pendant stores a compact repair token and gives a local retry tone; it never guesses or expires into execution.
args.why_useful_to_owner: A clipped name, number, or date no longer forces the owner to repeat an entire request or risk the wrong real-world action. They get a fast, understandable repair and continuity across the pendant, relay, Mac, and browser.
args.effort: Medium protocol and UX work across perception/action/relay plus a small firmware queue; extensive adversarial tests for stale repairs, duplicate delivery, and destructive actions.
args.risk: A stale correction could be attached to the wrong request, or repeated prompts could annoy the owner. Bind every repair to an intent hash, tab/job/session ID, and short expiry; cap retries at one and fall back to a clear failure receipt.
args.cost_impact: Minimal persistent storage (under 1 KB per pending repair); one additional realtime turn only on uncertain speech; no new hardware required.
args.latency_impact: Adds under 700 ms when repair is needed; zero added latency to high-confidence utterances.
args.security_impact: This is a safety barrier: uncertain destructive fields cannot pass. Sensitive transcript spans remain encrypted and expire; only the disputed span is spoken or displayed.

args.user_asks: Give me my briefing on the pendant, and keep it understandable and resumable even if the pendant is low on battery, the connection drops, or I get interrupted.
args.why_useful: A spoken brief should survive the conditions of real life rather than silently fail. The pendant can detect local battery/audio health, the relay can choose a frame/codec profile and retain a short encrypted queue, and the Mac/browser can supply cited text and regenerate only the missing segment. A button press resumes at the last acknowledged item instead of replaying everything.
args.model_tier: Use a cheap background model for summarization and segmentation; use realtime only for the owner's interruption/resume conversation. Codec negotiation, acknowledgements, retries, and resume offsets are deterministic.
args.latency_budget: Start playback within 2 seconds when a prepared brief exists; resume within 500 ms after a button press. Reconnect recovery may take up to 10 seconds and should be announced honestly.
args.cost_estimate: Usually <$0.01 per prepared brief beyond existing TTS/transcoding; retry cost is dominated by regenerated audio only for lost segments. Device telemetry and acknowledgements are negligible.
args.security_concerns: Brief text/audio can contain private mail, calendar, and authenticated-page data. Encrypt queued segments, keep only a short TTL, bind resume tokens to the owner's device/session, and require confirmation before any browser or mail mutation. Do not upload raw microphone audio beyond the existing voice interaction.
missing: End-to-end 24 kHz capability negotiation and a verified loopback test (current pendant capture is 15,625 Hz while decode is 24 kHz).
Durable per-item audio segment queue with delivery acknowledgements, bookmark/resume offsets, and idempotent replay protection.
A local battery/thermal/link-health event from the pendant and a relay policy that selects a lower-cost fallback without pretending quality is unchanged.
A Mac/browser text fallback that can regenerate one cited item when an audio segment is unavailable.

args.change: Replace the prototype's implicit audio assumptions with an explicit negotiated profile and loopback contract: pendant advertises capture/playback rates, frame duration, Opus mode, battery/thermal headroom, and firmware version; relay selects a profile, stamps every segment with profile+sequence+CRC, and runs a nightly fixture test that compares a 24 kHz source through uplink/transcode/decode/I2S output. Fail closed to a clearly labeled narrowband profile when the 15,625 Hz microphone path cannot satisfy superwideband, rather than upsampling and calling it 24 kHz.
args.why_useful_to_owner: The owner gets audio that is genuinely 24 kHz when promised, and an honest fallback when this development kit cannot provide it. Regressions become visible before they turn into a day of muffled or missing pendant speech.
args.effort: Medium-high: firmware capability packet and sequence metadata, relay negotiation/transcode changes, deterministic test fixture, and one hardware measurement pass. Product hardware may need a microphone/clock path capable of 24 kHz capture; software alone cannot recover information absent from 15,625 Hz capture.
args.risk: A negotiation bug could strand older firmware or cause silence. Keep a backward-compatible profile, require an explicit ACK before switching, and retain a server-side narrowband fallback. Test with packet loss and reconnects.
args.cost_impact: No meaningful per-request model cost; modest relay CPU/storage for loopback tests. Hardware prototype cost roughly $10–$30 for a suitable codec/mic/clock change, with power impact to be measured; current Opus encode+decode already consumes about 87% of one core when simultaneous.
args.latency_impact: Capability exchange adds <100 ms. 24 kHz encode/decode remains bounded by existing 60 ms framing; fixture tests run off-path.
args.security_impact: Telemetry contains device/firmware/profile and sequence metadata, not message content. Encrypt any diagnostic audio fixtures and expire them quickly; never retain owner speech for QA by default.
depends_on: A durable audio delivery acknowledgement/bookmark layer
An end-to-end audio acceptance test and the owner's decision on whether this development kit may be called superwideband
Physical microphone/clock redesign if true 24 kHz capture is required

args.user_asks: Keep me aware of genuinely urgent changes without making me pull out my phone or broadcasting private information in public; use a private signal now and explain it later.
args.why_useful: Today the system can speak, queue jobs, and inspect surfaces, but it cannot reliably arbitrate urgency across calendar/mail/browser/Mac signals and deliver a discreet, offline-tolerant signal on the wearable. This would let the owner stay reachable during a commute, meeting, or hands-busy moment without turning every notification into an interruption.
args.model_tier: Use deterministic rules and a cheap background model to classify urgency and deduplicate events; reserve realtime for the owner's follow-up question. Never spend the expensive conversational tier merely to decide that an unchanged notification is nonurgent.
args.latency_budget: Urgent events should reach the relay within 5 seconds and the pendant within 2 seconds of connectivity. If disconnected, latch the signal locally and deliver the explanation when the link returns; nonurgent items can wait for the next briefing.
args.cost_estimate: Usually <$0.005 per event batch; the dominant cost is occasional model classification of ambiguous messages. Haptic delivery and event metadata are negligible.
args.security_concerns: Urgency classification must minimize content exposure: prefer sender, deadline, and user-defined domains before message bodies. Keep private signals content-free, encrypt event metadata, expire raw excerpts, and require confirmation for any resulting external action. The owner must be able to define people, topics, and quiet hours, with an unmistakable physical all-clear/stop control.
missing: A pendant actuator and firmware protocol for at least three private urgency patterns plus a local latch that survives a dropped link and reboot.
A shared event-ingestion and deduplication stream from Mac notifications, Calendar, Mail, and authenticated browser watches, with source, deadline, confidence, and expiry.
A policy engine that combines urgency, quiet hours, current activity, and repetition history without silently escalating low-confidence events.
A delivery receipt and later explanation view that proves why the signal fired, what evidence supported it, and whether it was acknowledged.

args.change: Add a low-power haptic actuator with a dedicated interrupt-capable driver and a small nonvolatile attention latch (plus a physical acknowledge/stop input) to the wearable. Define three patterns—urgent, time-sensitive, and informational—whose waveform carries no message content; the relay sends only a signed event class and expiry, while the pendant can signal urgent events during a link outage and report acknowledgement after reconnect.
args.why_useful_to_owner: The owner can receive a private, glance-free warning in public or while hands are occupied, without a speaker announcing sensitive content and without losing an important event just because Wi-Fi or the Mac went to sleep.
args.effort: Hardware revision plus firmware driver, battery characterization, enclosure/acoustic isolation tests, relay event signing, and a small user calibration flow. This deliberately adds a capability rather than pretending the current single-LED/button prototype can provide reliable private urgency levels.
args.risk: False alarms could erode trust; missed alarms could be serious. Start with advisory notifications, require explicit owner-selected sources, expose a physical universal stop, expire stale latches, and log every trigger/acknowledgement for review. Haptic vibration can affect battery life and comfort.
args.cost_impact: Rough prototype addition: approximately $2–$8 for actuator, driver, and passives, plus PCB/enclosure changes; brief pulses likely add tens of milliwatts while active, with negligible average draw at low event rates. No model cost for delivery.
args.latency_impact: Local haptic onset can be under 100 ms after a signed event arrives; event arbitration and Mac/browser ingestion remain network-bound.
args.security_impact: The pendant receives only an authenticated class, expiry, and event identifier—not message text. Protect the latch against spoofing and ensure a stolen pendant cannot reveal private content through pattern semantics beyond the owner-configured vocabulary.
depends_on: A cross-surface urgency/deduplication policy and event stream
Owner-configured quiet hours, source allowlist, and confidence threshold
Delivery receipt and explanation records for every haptic event

transcript.text:
Recorded:

- A cross-surface **private urgency channel** that filters calendar, mail, browser, and Mac events, then discreetly signals only genuinely urgent items on the wearable and explains them later.
- A hardware/firmware change adding a **low-power haptic actuator**, signed urgency patterns, offline latching, acknowledgement, expiry, and a physical stop control.

These require a shared event stream, urgency/deduplication policy, owner-configured quiet hours and source allowlists, delivery receipts, and a pendant hardware revision.

args.user_asks: “Make spoken replies and my queued briefings sound clear, but never let them stutter: use 24 kHz when the link and pendant can sustain it, fall back smoothly when they cannot, and resume at the exact sentence if I walk out of coverage.”
args.why_useful: The current pendant path can decode 24 kHz playback but capture/uplink is 16 kHz, and simultaneous Opus encode/decode consumes roughly 87% of one Cortex-M33 core. A fixed mode will either waste quality or cause glitches. A hive-level adaptive session would let the owner hear consistently intelligible speech, preserve queued work through connectivity loss, and avoid replaying a briefing from the beginning.
args.model_tier: Use the realtime tier only for the live conversational turn and codec-mode negotiation; use a cheaper background worker for transcoding, queue preparation, and sentence-boundary indexing.
args.latency_budget: Mode negotiation under 300 ms at session start; fallback within 1–2 lost frames (120 ms) with a short crossfade; queued-briefing recovery can take seconds and must not block live speech.
args.cost_estimate: Small incremental API cost: mostly background Opus transcode/storage already paid for; roughly one extra cheap worker invocation per queued item, with bandwidth/storage dominating. Realtime token cost is unchanged if negotiation is structured metadata rather than prose.
args.security_concerns: Audio remains private and should stay in the existing authenticated relay storage. Telemetry should contain only codec mode, packet loss, battery/thermal buckets, and sentence IDs—not transcript text. Switching mode is reversible and needs no confirmation; deleting or pinning recordings still follows the owner's retention policy.
missing: A firmware capability/telemetry handshake exposing supported playback modes, decoder CPU headroom, queue cursor, and a local sentence-boundary resume marker.
Relay-side adaptive jitter buffer and Opus profile switch with sequence continuity and crossfade, rather than starting a new unrelated stream.
A background audio compiler that emits sentence/word boundary indexes and low/high-fidelity variants, plus garbage-collectable retention metadata.
Mac-side preflight and fallback notification so a briefing can be prepared or surfaced locally when the pendant is offline.
An end-to-end fault-injection test covering loss, reconnect, duplicate packets, SD failure buffer, and resume without duplicate speech.

args.change: Add an audio-session capability handshake and resumable playback cursor to the pendant protocol: advertise supported Opus rates/frame sizes, report coarse CPU/battery/link buckets, accept a mode switch only at a packet boundary, persist the current sentence ID plus sequence number in a tiny journal, and expose an explicit reconnect/resume event. Pair this with relay-side mode arbitration and a Mac preflight that selects 24 kHz, 16 kHz, or a pre-rendered fallback before delivery.
args.why_useful_to_owner: Briefings and replies would remain understandable instead of glitching or restarting when the owner moves between coverage or the pendant is busy. The owner gets one continuous conversation and can resume a long briefing where they stopped.
args.effort: Medium-high: protocol versioning, nRF9160 Opus scheduling, relay jitter/transcode state, Mac preflight, and network fault-injection tests across the four surfaces.
args.risk: A bad mode switch could produce silence, duplicated speech, or an unrecoverable cursor. Mitigate with capability-version negotiation, boundary-only switches, a watchdog fallback to the known 16 kHz path, journal checksum, and server-side duplicate suppression. Roll back by disabling negotiation and using the current fixed profile.
args.cost_impact: Negligible model cost; modest relay CPU for dual-variant transcode and temporary boundary metadata. Firmware flash/RAM impact should stay small (roughly 8–16 kB flash and under 4 kB RAM if the journal is compact).
args.latency_impact: Adds under 300 ms at session setup; recovery adds at most one short buffered segment. Normal speech should not gain a model round trip.
args.security_impact: Only coarse device telemetry and opaque sentence/sequence IDs leave the pendant; no transcript is added. Resume journals on SD must obey the existing rule that SD is a failure buffer, with bounded expiry and encryption if it contains audio references.
depends_on: A versioned audio control message path between pendant, ESP32 bridge, and relay
Relay adaptive jitter/transcode state and sentence-boundary indexing
A Mac offline/preflight hook
End-to-end audio loss/reconnect tests

args.user_asks: “Erase everything this hive knows about [topic/person/project] everywhere, prove what was erased, and stop any queued or offline action that depends on it.”
args.why_useful: Today a private fact or sensitive project can be distributed across relay job records, generated audio, Mac workspace files, browser-session state, pending commands, receipts, and the pendant’s failure buffer. The owner has no single, verifiable way to revoke that knowledge across all bodies. A topic-scoped cryptographic erasure and revocation operation would provide a real safety boundary, not merely a promise that future prompts will omit it.
args.model_tier: Use a deterministic background control-plane worker for indexing, revocation, deletion, and verification; use the realtime tier only to clarify the topic scope and speak the final receipt.
args.latency_budget: Acknowledge the request immediately; revoke queued work within 2 seconds; complete online erasure and produce a receipt within 30 seconds. Offline pendant and Mac components must apply the tombstone on reconnect before accepting work.
args.cost_estimate: Low model cost and modest control-plane/API cost. The dominant cost is enumerating and verifying distributed stores; no transcript generation is needed.
args.security_concerns: The erase request itself must not echo the secret in logs or spoken output. Use a keyed topic fingerprint, per-surface deletion capability, authenticated tombstones, and append-only proof metadata that records locations and outcomes without retaining content. Destructive erasure requires explicit confirmation, except for a separately configured physical panic gesture. The system must distinguish successful deletion, inaccessible storage, and cryptographic invalidation, never claim complete erasure when a surface is offline.
missing: A hive-wide data inventory that maps each artifact, pending action, browser session value, audio object, file, and device journal to privacy-scope fingerprints without copying sensitive content.
A signed, monotonic revocation/tombstone protocol consumed by relay, Mac, browser bridge, and pendant offline queue before execution or replay.
Per-surface secure deletion adapters: R2/D1 and logs on relay; workspace/receipt/job artifacts on Mac; browser extension/session caches; pendant SD failure-buffer records and local journals.
A verification sweep that returns a surface-by-surface receipt and retries or escalates offline failures, with an owner-visible distinction between erased and merely revoked.
A policy preventing model context, scheduled routines, and queued jobs from rehydrating a revoked scope.

args.change: Replace the prototype pendant’s single momentary button with a dedicated, latching privacy control that electrically disconnects the I2S microphone and signals the state with a hard-to-misread physical indicator. Add a small secure element or protected flash region for a device identity and an erase/revocation counter, so the pendant can reject stale queued commands after a privacy event even while offline. Firmware must treat the switch as authoritative, zeroize volatile audio buffers, stop capture, and emit only a minimal privacy-state event on reconnect.
args.why_useful_to_owner: The owner could put the pendant on a table in a confidential meeting and know—without trusting software, network state, or a model—that it cannot hear them. After privacy is lifted, old offline work cannot silently replay against the new context.
args.effort: High hardware revision plus firmware and relay protocol changes: microphone power/clock gating, debounce and boot-state handling, secure-counter integration, enclosure redesign, and certification/regression testing.
args.risk: A stuck or bounced switch could disable conversations or create a false sense of privacy. Use a mechanically stable two-position control, visible state, boot self-test, and an explicit spoken/LED confirmation when capture resumes. Treat any hardware fault as privacy-on. Secure-counter failure must fail closed and allow recovery only through a local owner procedure.
args.cost_impact: Prototype BOM increase roughly $2–6 for a latching switch, mic power gate, indicator, and secure element, plus board/enclosure NRE; negligible ongoing API cost and sub-milliwatt standby impact.
args.latency_impact: Privacy engagement is immediate; resume adds under 500 ms for hardware settle and session renegotiation.
args.security_impact: Strongly improves the trust boundary by making microphone disablement independent of the application and relay. The device identity/counter prevents replay of pre-privacy commands, but it introduces key provisioning and replacement/recovery obligations.

args.user_asks: “Keep the pendant useful all day: spend battery and bandwidth on urgent things, defer or compress everything else, and tell me what was deferred before it becomes stale.”
args.why_useful: Today the hive has no owner-facing energy contract. A long briefing, live conversation, queued browser job, and urgent interruption compete blindly for the same pendant radio, CPU, and failure-buffer space. The owner should get graceful degradation rather than a dead device or silently lost work: urgent contact remains available, routine work is deferred with an expiry, and the Mac/relay can carry on when the pendant cannot.
args.model_tier: Use deterministic policy and a cheap background worker for energy prediction, queue reprioritization, and transcoding. Invoke the realtime tier only for an active conversation or a truly urgent spoken alert.
args.latency_budget: Urgency classification and budget update under 1 second; routine deferral is immediate. The Mac or relay may continue background work without pendant availability, while urgent delivery retries within 2 seconds.
args.cost_estimate: Low model/API cost because the decision is policy over device telemetry; occasional background summarization/transcoding dominates. It can reduce cost by avoiding unnecessary high-fidelity streaming and repeated retries.
args.security_concerns: Battery, link, and queue telemetry should be coarse and authenticated. Never silently discard owner work: every deferral needs an expiry and receipt. Urgency rules must be owner-configurable, with conservative defaults and an emergency override that may require confirmation for noisy alerts.
missing: A signed low-rate device telemetry stream for battery, radio quality, thermal/CPU headroom, SD capacity, and charging state.
A shared resource ledger that assigns budgets to live audio, queued briefings, browser/Mac jobs, and retry buffers with explicit expiry semantics.
Relay/Mac ability to continue and later reconcile work while the pendant is unavailable, without duplicating spoken output.
A policy evaluator that can distinguish urgent owner-defined events from routine work and explain each defer/compress decision.
A compact pendant status interaction so the owner can inspect or override the current budget without opening a screen.

transcript.text:
Recorded two proposals:

1. **Hive-wide topic erasure and revocation** — erase or cryptographically invalidate sensitive information across relay, Mac, browser, pendant buffers, queued jobs, and model context, with an honest surface-by-surface receipt.

2. **Energy-aware continuity** — keep urgent communication available while battery, bandwidth, CPU, or storage are constrained; defer, compress, or reroute routine work with expiry and an explanation rather than silently losing it.

Both require new cross-surface control-plane, telemetry, policy, and verification work rather than another isolated feature.

args.model_tier: Use the slower background model for planning and receipt summarization; use realtime only if the owner presses the pendant after an approval-needed haptic or asks a follow-up.

args.risk: Extra current draw and mechanical buzz could annoy the wearer; a bad pattern could be mistaken for an approval. Default to conservative patterns, allow disabling, require an explicit button press for approval, and fall back to LED/audio when the haptic self-test fails.
args.cost_impact: Approximately $4–$12 BOM increase (motor, driver, gauge, passives, sensor) and a few mA during pulses; no per-call API cost. Fuel gauge reduces uncertainty but adds always-on quiescent current.
args.latency_impact: Local acknowledgment is sub-100 ms once an event reaches the pendant; no model latency. Haptic queue must survive LTE reconnects without replaying expired events.
args.security_impact: Improves privacy by removing sensitive audio from routine status. Do not encode semantic content in patterns beyond urgency/state; encrypt and authenticate event IDs, and expire approval challenges.

This round I found the bridge is online, but there is still one pending browser command. Accessibility and Screen Recording remain unavailable; AppleScript automation is available, so quiet execution must avoid vision and never replay stale commands.

I proposed:

- **“Handle it quietly, and only get my attention if you need me.”**  
  A cross-surface privacy mode where Mac/browser work continues silently, the relay aggregates redacted receipts, and the pendant signals only completion, approval-needed, or failure.
- **Quiet-Intent integration.**  
  A signed, expiring mode lease flows from unified → relay → Mac/browser, with exactly-once event delivery, no replay after reconnect, and full details withheld until the owner intentionally engages.
- **Pendant hardware support.**  
  Add an I²C haptic actuator and battery gauge so private status does not require spoken audio. The current pendant has a free I²C bus but only one LED and one button.

What is still needed:

1. A typed relay-to-pendant notification and acknowledgement protocol.
2. Durable cross-surface job events tied to the transaction coordinator and approval nonces.
3. Quiet-mode leases with expiry, cancellation, and reconnect reconciliation.
4. Pending-browser-command reconciliation so stale commands are explicitly expired rather than replayed.
5. Haptic hardware and firmware support; this cannot be implemented reliably with the current LED alone.
6. A dashboard indicator showing whether quiet mode is active and when it will expire.

No additional permission request is needed this round.

args.user_asks: “Before I commit to this, show me what it will cost me and what it will displace.”
args.why_useful: The owner gets a consequence preview before accepting a meeting, booking travel, agreeing to a deadline, or sending a significant message. The system compares the proposed commitment with calendar load, existing tasks, travel time, active browser work, and known obligations, then presents the smallest set of real trade-offs without changing anything.
args.model_tier: Use a cheaper background model for source collection and normalization; reserve realtime for the owner's short spoken decision and one clarifying question when a key assumption is missing.
args.latency_budget: Return a concise first risk preview within 10 seconds; deeper source reconciliation may continue in the background for up to 60 seconds. No external action occurs during preview.
args.cost_estimate: Approximately $0.02–$0.10 per preview, dominated by multi-source extraction and synthesis; repeated unchanged source facts should be cached with freshness limits.
args.security_concerns: Treat calendar, mail, account pages, travel data, and task details as private. Keep raw content on the Mac/browser where possible and send the relay only normalized claims with provenance. Clearly label estimates versus facts; never silently infer consent or make changes.
missing: A first-class consequence-preview schema containing proposal, assumptions, affected commitments, displacement costs, confidence, and source evidence
A shared obligation/time model that can normalize Calendar, Reminders, Mail, browser account pages, and active Mac jobs without collapsing uncertainty
A read-only multi-surface gather operation with bounded parallelism and source freshness checks
A spoken comparison format that fits in one short turn and supports 'show me the worst case' or 'use the least disruptive option' follow-ups

args.change: Add a read-only consequence projection engine that accepts a proposed commitment as an untrusted hypothetical, resolves affected time windows and obligations across local Calendar/Reminders/Mail metadata, browser sessions, and active jobs, and returns a provenance-linked displacement graph. It must preserve competing interpretations instead of forcing one identity or deadline, assign confidence/expiry to every edge, and expose a compact spoken rendering plus an audit payload.
args.why_useful_to_owner: They can ask about a decision before making it and receive an honest answer such as 'this fits only if you give up lunch and delays the current browser task by two hours,' rather than discovering the conflict after committing.
args.effort: Medium-to-high: schema and graph algorithms, local AppleScript readers, browser extraction adapters, hypothetical simulation tests, and a voice renderer. Start read-only with synthetic fixtures, then add live sources one at a time.
args.risk: False conflicts could make the owner avoid worthwhile commitments; missed obligations are more dangerous. Show evidence and confidence, distinguish hard calendar conflicts from soft estimates, allow source-by-source inspection, and never write to external systems.
args.cost_impact: Low recurring storage; roughly $0.01–$0.08 per preview after cached extraction. The main cost is model synthesis over several normalized claims, not raw source reads.
args.latency_impact: Local extraction can begin immediately; a first estimate in seconds, full reconciliation under a minute. It must degrade to a partial answer when a source is unavailable rather than blocking.
args.security_impact: Read-only by design. Keep source text and account identifiers on the Mac/browser; relay receives redacted claim IDs, timestamps, confidence, and hashes. Hypothetical proposals must not be persisted as commitments unless the owner explicitly confirms.
depends_on: Typed task-relevant context projection with provenance and TTL
A normalized local obligation/time representation
Authenticated browser read/extract adapters
A read-only planning endpoint that accepts hypothetical inputs
