args.user_asks: “Quarantine everything you know about this person/project for now—don’t use it in answers, briefs, or actions, but keep an auditable record so I can release the quarantine later.”
args.why_useful: The owner needs a reversible boundary between forgetting and unrestricted use. Today a fact can survive in facts.json, the context graph, browser-derived memory, evidence, an inherited prompt projection, or a queued job, and there is no single way to stop all of those copies influencing a decision. Quarantine would let the owner handle a sensitive dispute, client matter, or family situation immediately without destructive deletion or pretending revocation propagated.
args.model_tier: Use deterministic policy enforcement for matching, blocking, and expiry. Use a background model only to help map the owner’s natural-language subject to candidate entities/facts, with the owner reviewing ambiguous matches; realtime is only for the spoken command and confirmation.
args.latency_budget: A confirmed quarantine should block new prompt projections and external-action planning within 1 s across relay and Mac. Existing queued work must be marked blocked before execution; listing affected records can finish in the background.
args.cost_estimate: Low ongoing model cost; one small model call for ambiguous entity matching, then local indexed lookups. Storage grows by compact quarantine rules and tombstone references, not copied content.
args.security_concerns: Fail closed: an uncertain subject match blocks rather than leaks. The pendant confirmation must not repeat the sensitive subject aloud. Quarantine metadata should contain opaque IDs and hashed selectors where possible. It must cover prompt projection, brief narration, browser extraction, memory retrieval, queued jobs, and action planning, while preserving only the minimum audit evidence needed to explain a block. Release, expiry, and exceptions require deliberate owner confirmation.
missing: A shared quarantine policy and matcher consumed by relay memory projection, Mac memory/context-graph retrieval, browser provenance, briefing/audio rendering, and job/action planners

Stable provenance links from derived facts and graph entities to their source capsules, browser records, jobs, and fleet-memory events; current facts and graph copies cannot be reached by evidence revocation
A durable cross-surface propagation protocol with version/epoch so an offline Mac, browser, or queued relay job cannot continue using a stale policy
A dashboard view showing blocked surfaces, affected pending work, expiry, and an explicit release operation

args.subject: Distinct proposals this round
args.body: I’m considering a correction-learning loop (owner stop/undo/approve feedback updates policy), a cross-surface reliability report based on delivery ACKs/receipts, and an intent-to-artifact continuity check. Any gap you see that avoids reconciler/provenance duplicates?

result.note: They will see this on their next round.

args.user_asks: If I tell you an action was wrong—or stop it halfway—learn exactly what failed, show me the evidence, and avoid making the same class of mistake again without silently changing your rules.
args.why_useful: Today stop/undo, delivery ACKs, receipts, and provenance are separate. The owner has to reconstruct failures and the system cannot distinguish a wrong target from stale evidence or an audio delivery problem. A reviewable correction loop turns the pendant’s physical interruption and Mac/browser outcomes into safer future decisions, while keeping policy changes explicit and owner-approved.
args.model_tier: background for classification and weekly pattern summaries; realtime only to acknowledge the correction and state the immediate safe action
args.latency_budget: Immediate acknowledgement under 1 second; classification within 10 seconds; no blocking of the owner’s next request
args.cost_estimate: About $0.002–$0.02 per correction depending on whether a model is needed; most cases are deterministic labels from receipts, ACKs, and policy verdicts
args.security_concerns: The correction record must contain IDs and structured failure labels by default, not transcript or page contents. Provenance is shown through explain_action_provenance. Never auto-promote a learned rule; stage a policy patch and require explicit approval. A malicious or accidental stop must not rewrite autonomy policy.
missing: A typed correction event API linking a pendant stop/undo/approval to one action or briefing item
A durable cross-surface action identity joining relay, Mac, browser, and artifact IDs
A review route that proposes policy changes without applying them
A background evaluator that clusters repeated corrections with source-linked evidence

args.user_asks: When I come back, tell me what actually happened while I was away: what finished, what reached the pendant, what is still stuck, and what needs me—without making me ask every surface separately.
args.why_useful: Catch-up today is assembled from partial sources and cannot prove pendant playback, does not reliably identify orphaned Mac jobs, and has no single owner-facing continuity report. A delivery-aware return brief would prevent duplicate work and expose silent failures such as audio downloaded but never heard or a job left processing after a Mac crash.
args.model_tier: background model to summarize structured events; deterministic rules first for completion, expiry, and duplicate suppression
args.latency_budget: Generate in under 5 seconds on request; optional scheduled preparation under 30 seconds
args.cost_estimate: Roughly $0.005–$0.03 per report; token cost dominates only when many heterogeneous receipts need summarization
args.security_concerns: Speak only item titles/statuses unless the owner explicitly requests detail; do not include raw mail, page text, or private audio in a default report. Every line must carry an evidence reference and freshness timestamp. Stale or missing ACKs must be reported as unknown, never as completed.
missing: A relay-to-local durable job identity and lease/requeue semantics for orphaned processing jobs
A report aggregator joining relay job receipts, Mac/browser receipts, context handoffs, and authenticated pendant delivery ACKs
A durable last-seen cursor so reconnect/replay does not duplicate items
An owner-facing route and compact audio rendering for finished/stuck/needs-you sections

args.user_asks: Do this once, even if the Mac, browser, or relay reconnects halfway through—and if you already did it, prove that before trying again.
args.why_useful: The system currently has five unrelated ID namespaces and only Mac-local idempotency. A single owner-visible action identity would prevent duplicate reminders, duplicate browser submissions, repeated drafts, and confusing handoffs after reconnects. This is the difference between a hive mind and several agents independently repeating the same request.
args.model_tier: Deterministic routing and idempotency checks; use the realtime model only for ambiguous natural-language matching to an existing action
args.latency_budget: Under 300 ms for known IDs; under 2 seconds for ambiguous matching; no external mutation until identity and current-state checks pass
args.cost_estimate: Near-zero for deterministic hashes and store lookups; up to $0.01 for ambiguous matching
args.security_concerns: The identity must bind intent, target, and allowed effect—not secrets or page contents. Never treat a textual similarity match as proof for destructive actions. Expired or state-changed identities become ASK/PREPARE, not retries. Owner can inspect and revoke the chain.
missing: A relay-issued correlation ID carried unchanged through Mac jobs, browser commands, action receipts, pipeline artifacts, and pendant ACKs
A durable idempotency ledger shared or reconciled across relay and Mac
Adapters that map browser command IDs and Mac action IDs into the shared record
A fail-closed duplicate decision integrated before POST /execute and browser mutation

args.change: Add a lease_until/attempt counter and requeue sweep to relay_jobs, then preserve one relay correlation ID through bridge handoff and local/browser receipts. On reconnect, the relay must classify each job as completed, safely retryable, or owner-attention-required using idempotency evidence; never blindly replay a mutation.
args.why_useful_to_owner: A sleeping or crashed Mac will no longer make a request vanish for 24 hours or cause a duplicate when it comes back. The owner gets one truthful status and one safe continuation instead of repeating themselves across surfaces.
args.effort: Medium: D1/memory-store schema and sweeper, bridge propagation, receipt joins, and tests for crash/reconnect races.
args.risk: A lease that is too short can duplicate a slow action; too long delays recovery. Fail closed for external or destructive actions, and require current-state revalidation before retry. Roll back by leaving old processing semantics behind a feature flag while migrating rows.
args.cost_impact: Negligible storage and CPU; no model cost for deterministic lease decisions.
args.latency_impact: Adds one lookup/update before retry; normal first execution unchanged.
args.security_impact: Improves auditability. Correlation records must carry opaque IDs only, not page contents, credentials, or audio.
depends_on: A durable relay↔Mac↔browser correlation mapping
revalidate_pending_plan for stale prepared actions
autonomy_policy_evaluate before any replay
record_pendant_delivery_event for audio completion evidence

transcript.text:
This round produced three owner-facing capabilities:

1. **Correction learning without silent policy drift**  
   When you stop, undo, or reject an action, the system records the failure class, shows the evidence, and proposes—but does not silently apply—a policy improvement.

2. **A delivery-aware “what happened while I was away?” brief**  
   One report joins relay jobs, Mac/browser receipts, handoffs, and authenticated pendant playback ACKs. It distinguishes *finished*, *delivered but unheard*, *stuck*, and *needs you*.

3. **Exactly-once execution across the hive**  
   A single correlation identity follows an intent through relay, Mac, browser, artifacts, and pendant. Reconnects check whether the action already happened before retrying, preventing duplicate reminders, drafts, submissions, or speech.

I also proposed the relay change underpinning these: leases and requeue for orphaned jobs, plus durable cross-surface correlation. This is the most important missing reliability behavior: a crashed Mac must not make work disappear or replay it blindly.

What I still need is not another broad capability request. The remaining implementation gaps are concrete:

- A durable relay ↔ Mac ↔ browser ↔ pendant correlation record.
- Relay job leases, expiry, and safe requeue.
- A typed correction/feedback event linked to action provenance.
- A continuity-report aggregator and owner-facing route.
- Integration of replay decisions with `revalidate_pending_plan` and `autonomy_policy_evaluate`.
- A durable, review-only store for proposed policy changes.

The biggest unknown is the owner’s desired policy for learning from corrections: whether repeated corrections should merely be suggested as rules, or whether some narrowly scoped reversible preferences may eventually be auto-applied.

args.user_asks: Give me a portable, complete account of what this system knows about me, where each claim came from, what it caused, what I revoked, and what is still retained—so I can inspect it or leave without trusting the system’s own dashboard.
args.why_useful: Today provenance is queried per action or evidence item, while facts, graph records, browser captures, relay memory, audio artifacts, and revocations are split across stores with no owner-controlled export or completeness proof. The owner cannot independently audit the system’s memory, detect orphaned copies, or migrate away. A signed, resumable export with omission proofs makes trust inspectable rather than assumed.
args.model_tier: Deterministic extraction, joins, redaction, and hashing; background model only to produce an optional human-readable summary after the exact manifest is generated
args.latency_budget: Start streaming within 2 seconds; export incrementally in the background; summary under 30 seconds for a typical month
args.cost_estimate: Near-zero for manifests, hashes, and structured records; up to $0.02 for an optional natural-language summary
args.security_concerns: Exports are highly sensitive and must be local-first, encrypted, expiring, and explicitly downloaded. Default output contains metadata and source references, not raw secrets or audio. The owner must choose whether to include sensitive bodies. Every omitted record needs a reason (expired, revoked, inaccessible, or unsupported), never silent omission. No third-party model receives the export unless explicitly requested.
missing: A cross-store export protocol joining Mac facts/graph/captures/evidence, browser provenance, relay jobs/memory, pipeline artifacts, and pendant delivery events
Stable source and deletion identifiers so revocations and derived copies can be proven to propagate or be reported as orphaned
A signed manifest with per-store watermarks, record hashes, omission reasons, and export encryption
An owner-controlled import/delete verification path rather than a dashboard-only rendering

args.user_asks: Watch yourself for violations of your own promises and tell me before I rely on you: for example, if private content was spoken, an action bypassed consent, a stale source drove a decision, or an artifact was delivered without a valid receipt.
args.why_useful: The current system records many events but does not continuously compare them against safety invariants. Failures can remain invisible unless the owner already knows which route to inspect. An independent watchdog gives the owner an honest trust signal and a reviewable incident report, rather than assuming successful HTTP responses mean safe behavior.
args.model_tier: Deterministic invariant checks and signed event joins; background model only for grouping incidents and drafting a plain-language explanation
args.latency_budget: Critical violations surfaced within seconds; routine audit every 15 minutes; report generation under 10 seconds
args.cost_estimate: Near-zero for structured checks; under $0.01 per incident summary when a model is used
args.security_concerns: The watchdog must be isolated from the component it audits and append-only for incident evidence. It must not replay, repair, or conceal a violation. Spoken alerts must reveal only a safe category by default. False positives should create review items, never automatically cancel unrelated work. Retention and export of incident records need explicit owner controls.
missing: A typed invariant registry covering consent, freshness, sensitivity, delivery, and revocation rules
An append-only cross-surface event stream with authenticated timestamps and correlation IDs
A verifier independent of the normal planner and speech path
A critical-alert route that can reach the existing pendant inbox without exposing sensitive payloads
A dashboard showing invariant, evidence, impact, and remediation state

transcript.text:
Recorded two capabilities:

- **Portable personal-AI audit export**: a complete, signed, resumable account of memories, evidence, derived claims, actions, revocations, retained copies, and omissions—so the owner can independently inspect or leave the system.
- **Independent trust watchdog**: continuously checks whether the system violated its own consent, freshness, privacy, revocation, or delivery guarantees, and surfaces a safe incident report before the owner relies on the result.

They require cross-store identifiers, authenticated event joins, append-only audit records, explicit omission proofs, and a verifier independent of the normal planner and speech path.

args.user_asks: When I delegate something, make sure it either finishes or comes back honestly for recovery—even if the Mac, browser, or relay dies halfway through.
args.why_useful: Today a job can remain permanently 'processing' after a crash, so the owner cannot tell whether to wait, retry, or start over. A leased, resumable delegation would recover orphaned work without duplicate external actions and would surface a precise recovery choice.
args.model_tier: background for lease/recovery decisions; realtime only for the owner's spoken status
args.latency_budget: Normal completion unchanged; crash recovery detected within 1–5 minutes, with an immediate dashboard/pendant status when the owner asks.
args.cost_estimate: Negligible model cost; dominant cost is a few D1 reads/writes per lease sweep and one compact recovery summary when needed.
args.security_concerns: Requeue only idempotent or explicitly reversible steps. Never replay a send, purchase, deletion, or other external side effect without a fresh autonomy-policy verdict and physical approval where required. Store only IDs, step hashes, and receipts in the recovery record.
missing: relay_jobs lease_until and an atomic requeue sweep
a durable relay-job-id to Mac-job-id mapping rather than telemetry-only localJobId

args.user_asks: Give me a morning brief that knows what I actually heard: continue after an interruption, skip what I acknowledged, and never claim delivery just because audio was generated.
args.why_useful: A generated artifact is not the same as a heard briefing. This would make the pendant a trustworthy conversational surface: playback position and item acknowledgements survive link loss, duplicates collapse, and unfinished items fall back to a reviewable Mac/dashboard queue rather than silently disappearing.
args.model_tier: background for compiling/ranking the brief; realtime only for barge-in and the owner's short follow-up
args.latency_budget: Brief compilation under 10 seconds; item state updates under 1 second when connected and reconciled on reconnect.
args.cost_estimate: Low model cost after compilation; dominant operational cost is artifact metadata and a few authenticated ACK writes, not repeated synthesis.
args.security_concerns: ACKs must be authenticated, monotonic, and deduplicated. The pendant receives opaque item IDs and bounded spoken text only; private content must still pass the existing delivery redaction gate. Never infer that downloaded means heard.
missing: a single durable briefing manifest joining source item, audio artifact, cursor, and owner acknowledgement
relay ingestion of the existing pendant delivery ACK queue with offline replay and duplicate suppression
scheduler wiring that creates item IDs before synthesis and advances only on playback state
a dashboard review state for generated-but-unheard items

args.user_asks: If a task gets stuck because a website needs me to log in or approve something, pause it safely, tell me exactly what is needed, and finish automatically once I have cleared the block.
args.why_useful: Authenticated browser sessions are physically reachable only through the extension, while planning and follow-up live on the Mac/relay. Today a blocked browser task either fails ambiguously or leaves the owner to remember it. This would turn a login wall into a durable, bounded handoff instead of a lost task or unsafe credential request.
args.model_tier: background for classifying the block and preparing the next read-only step; realtime only to explain the block or receive the owner's approval
args.latency_budget: Detect a block during the current browser poll; notify within one attention-arbitrated cycle. Resume within one poll after the owner clears it.
args.cost_estimate: Low: mostly browser snapshots and state polling; model calls only when the page state is ambiguous. No credential extraction or upload.
args.security_concerns: The browser must return only a typed block reason (login, MFA, owner approval, unavailable page), never passwords, OTPs, cookies, or secret form values. Resume plans expire and are revalidated against current page/session state. Any send, purchase, deletion, or other external side effect remains a separate owner-confirmed action.

args.user_asks: “Can you keep this thread alive until it is actually done?” Turn a spoken intention into a small, observable outcome with a deadline, check progress across the right surfaces, and tell me only when it is done, blocked, or needs me.

This is the missing life-level behavior: the pendant remembers what ‘done’ means, the relay coordinates, the Mac/browser verify reality, and the owner is not nagged by intermediate noise.

args.latency_budget: Initial capture under 2 seconds; checks run on schedules or source events; completion notification under 5 seconds of verified evidence.
args.cost_estimate: Moderate initial extraction, then low background cost. Source polling and browser reads dominate, not generation.

A blocked state must be honest about missing permissions, stale browser sessions, or contradictory evidence; never infer completion from a queued job.

args.risk: Existing callers may break when they must handle unknown/stale instead of empty. Recover by dual-writing contracts, logging violations, and failing closed only for high-impact decisions before expanding enforcement.
args.cost_impact: Negligible storage and token overhead; avoids expensive realtime explanations by carrying compact evidence references.
args.latency_impact: Milliseconds for deterministic checks; at most one extra source read when a contract is expired.
args.security_impact: Improves least-privilege and disclosure: spoken content can be blocked based on both sensitivity and recipient freshness/provenance. Contracts contain IDs and timestamps, not raw secrets.

Add relay-job to Mac/browser job correlation (currently only unindexed telemetry)
Use the existing briefingTriage empty-pair corroboration for EventKit and preserve unreadable as a first-class state

transcript.text:
Round 259 produced four proposals:

1. **“What changed since I last checked?”** — a source-linked delta across mail, calendar/reminders, browser, Mac jobs, and pendant delivery, with explicit stale/unreadable states.
2. **Attention-leak diagnosis** — identify repeated failures, abandoned jobs, browser disconnects, routine errors, and audio interruptions, then recommend one reversible fix.
3. **Outcome tracking** — let the owner say “keep this thread alive until it’s done,” define observable completion criteria, monitor the relevant surfaces, and report only completion, blockage, or a request for help.
4. **Freshness contracts** — every observation and judgement carries source, timestamp, expiry, permission state, redaction state, and evidence references, preventing “calendar is clear” or “done” claims based on unreadable or stale data.

The first proposal was flagged as close to an existing backlog item, so it should not be repeated. The valuable new part is the **freshness contract**, which should underpin any future delta or outcome feature.

What I still need is not another tool grant. The unresolved owner decisions are:

- Which notification content may be spoken aloud, versus only summarized or queued.
- Quiet hours and what qualifies as genuinely urgent.
- Which destinations and data classes are trusted to leave the Mac.
- Whether the owner wants outcome tracking to create reminders automatically or only report status.

The biggest technical unknown is whether every relevant source can be given a durable freshness and provenance contract without introducing false certainty—especially EventKit calendar/reminder reads and browser connectivity.

args.user_asks: “Before I say yes, show me the likely cost to future-me.” For a proposed commitment, simulate its effects on time, existing obligations, privacy, and attention, then present the smallest safe version or a clear tradeoff.
args.why_useful: The owner currently gets execution and reminders, but not a judgment that connects a new promise to the life it will displace. This is a decision aid, not an automatic planner: it makes hidden opportunity costs visible before they become obligations.
args.model_tier: A background model builds a few bounded scenarios from structured state; realtime is used only to discuss the selected tradeoff. Deterministic checks enforce deadlines, conflicts, permissions, and spending limits.
args.latency_budget: Initial answer within 5 seconds; deeper alternatives can arrive as a queued briefing. No interruption unless the owner explicitly asks.
args.cost_estimate: Moderate per explicit invocation; the expensive part is scenario synthesis, while calendar/job/reminder reads remain local and cheap.
args.security_concerns: Use abstract facts and time blocks by default, not raw message contents. Never contact anyone or create an obligation during simulation. External actions require the existing policy and physical approval path. Every forecast must distinguish observed facts from assumptions.

A bounded scenario evaluator with explicit assumptions and confidence intervals
A provenance-backed comparison view showing which facts drove each predicted cost

args.user_asks: “Give me a private weekly mirror of how I actually lived.” Summarize patterns in attention, unfinished intentions, interruptions, and recovery—using local aggregates—then let me correct the story or erase a pattern.
args.why_useful: The system reacts to individual events but cannot help the owner notice recurring causes: which commitments repeatedly slip, when interruptions cluster, or whether the pendant is being used as intended. A private mirror supports better choices without turning behavior into a score or surveillance feed.
args.model_tier: Cheap background aggregation over typed local events, followed by a small synthesis model. Realtime is unnecessary except for an owner follow-up such as “why do you think that?”
args.latency_budget: Weekly generation under 20 seconds; spoken summary under 90 words. Detail is dashboard-only and on demand.
args.cost_estimate: Low: local aggregation dominates, with one small background synthesis call per reporting period.
args.security_concerns: Keep raw audio, page text, mail bodies, and credentials out of the mirror. Store only owner-approved aggregate dimensions with a short retention period. Every statement needs an evidence range and an easy correction/erase action; never infer health, personality, or protected traits.

args.user_asks: “When I am unavailable, leave the right kind of explanation—not just a failure.” For a blocked task or missed commitment, produce a compact handoff stating what was attempted, what is known, what is uncertain, and the safest next owner action.
args.why_useful: Today a failed job, stale browser session, or missing permission leaves the owner to reconstruct the situation from logs. A truthful handoff preserves agency across sleep, travel, crashes, and changing attention without pretending that queued work succeeded.
args.model_tier: Deterministic receipt assembly first; a cheap background model compresses it into owner language. Realtime only answers follow-up questions.
args.latency_budget: Available immediately when a task becomes blocked; spoken form under 2 seconds and one sentence, with detail queued.
args.cost_estimate: Low: receipt assembly is local; generation is a small background call only for non-template explanations.
args.security_concerns: Handoffs must carry sensitivity labels and avoid raw page/mail content by default. Never disclose a third party's private data to another recipient. Do not retry or mutate while composing the handoff. Include provenance and an expiry so an old explanation cannot be mistaken for current state.

args.user_asks: “Undo the last thing you did, wherever it happened.”
args.why_useful: Today undo exists as separate Mac/job/plan endpoints, but the owner cannot safely invoke one semantic undo across a browser action, Mac action, or queued job. This would turn the hive's receipts into a trustworthy escape hatch after a mistaken action.
args.model_tier: gpt-5.6-luna for selecting and explaining the target; deterministic receipt/reversibility checks for execution, with realtime only for the spoken request
args.latency_budget: Under 2 seconds to identify and speak the candidate; under 5 seconds to execute a reversible undo. Ask for confirmation if more than one candidate or if any step is not provably reversible.
args.cost_estimate: About $0.01–$0.04 per invocation when model selection is needed; receipt lookup and policy checks dominate latency, not tokens.
args.security_concerns: Never guess across multiple recent actions. Require a receipt-backed inverse, run autonomy_policy_evaluate and cross_surface_preflight, and fail closed when the inverse is absent. Do not undo destructive or externally committed actions; explain why. No new data leaves the Mac beyond existing receipt metadata.
missing: A durable cross-surface join between relay job IDs, Mac action IDs, and browser command IDs
A typed inverse-operation registry that maps receipts to existing undo endpoints
A single owner-facing endpoint that selects the latest eligible action

args.user_asks: “I lost the connection—continue from exactly where I stopped, and don't repeat what I already heard.”
args.why_useful: A dropped LTE session currently risks repeating an entire response or silently losing it. Combining the durable context handoff, semantic audio cursor, and authenticated pendant delivery ACKs would make the pendant feel continuous rather than like a radio that forgets.
args.model_tier: Deterministic cursor reconciliation first; gpt-5.6-luna only to regenerate a compact replacement when the original artifact is unavailable. Realtime is used only for the reconnect utterance.
args.latency_budget: On reconnect, return a resume decision in under 500 ms; begin playback within 2 seconds. Regeneration may take up to 8 seconds but must be explicitly labeled as a replacement.
args.cost_estimate: Near-zero for cursor/ACK reconciliation; $0.01–$0.06 only when audio must be regenerated.
args.security_concerns: Use opaque artifact IDs and authenticated device sessions; never infer completion from download alone. Deduplicate offline ACK replay, honor universal_stop_latch, and do not replay secret text merely because it was partially downloaded. Preserve provenance to the original item and mark replacement audio distinctly.
missing: A relay-side durable delivery ledger joining artifact IDs to briefing items and context handles
A reconnect route that computes the first unplayed cursor from record_pendant_delivery_event events

args.user_asks: “Learn how much interruption I can actually tolerate, and only interrupt me when it is worth breaking my attention.”
args.why_useful: The current arbiter can rank events but has no outcome loop: it cannot distinguish an urgent interruption the owner acted on from one they repeatedly deferred. A bounded, explainable calibration loop would reduce nuisance speech without hiding deadlines.
args.model_tier: Cheap deterministic policy update from explicit outcomes (acknowledge, defer, replay, dismiss) and observed attention state; use gpt-5.6-luna only for weekly plain-language summaries of what changed.
args.latency_budget: No added latency to event arbitration; update policy in under 100 ms after an outcome. Weekly summary can be generated in the background.
args.cost_estimate: Usually under $0.005 per update; weekly summary roughly $0.01–$0.03.
args.security_concerns: Never silently learn a rule that suppresses safety-critical or deadline-bound events. Keep learned weights bounded, time-decayed, and visible by policy field; separate content sensitivity from urgency. Store only event class/outcome, not raw mail or page text, and allow reset of learned state.

transcript.text:
Round 260 produced four proposals:

1. **Cross-surface “undo the last thing”** — identify the latest receipt-backed reversible action across Mac, browser, or relay, then safely invoke its inverse.
2. **Exact playback continuation after reconnect** — use pendant delivery ACKs and audio cursors to resume at the first unheard item without replaying completed audio.
3. **Outcome-based interruption calibration** — learn from defer/replay/ack outcomes while preserving hard floors for deadlines and safety-critical alerts.
4. **Conflict-to-question resolution** — when sources disagree, ask one focused owner question, store the explicit scoped answer, and retain provenance.

I also proposed a relay change for lease-based stalled-job recovery. It was recorded, but the recorder flagged it as close to an existing backlog item; the underlying need remains: expired jobs must not sit invisibly in `processing` for 24 hours.

What I still need:

- **Implementation work, not another concept:** durable relay↔Mac↔browser correlation IDs, lease/requeue semantics, a delivery ledger, and conflict-decision persistence.
- **Owner policy values:** quiet hours, what qualifies as emergency, what notification classes may be spoken aloud, and trusted disclosure destinations. These must remain configurable rather than guessed.
- **Shipping validation:** LTE-M registration and reconnect testing. USB is useful for bench work but is not a product transport.
- **A decision on the current timezone conflict:** Mac routine time is authoritative for local execution, while the owner projection says America/Chicago; the owner’s actual location timezone remains unresolved.

Every claim must show its source and date, respect revocations, and distinguish contemporaneous evidence from later interpretation. Never let historical context silently influence a current external action.

Every claim needs a source link and date; participant names and quoted content should not be spoken in public mode.
missing: A conversation bundle that joins mail threads, browser pages, local notes/files, and calendar events without copying raw bodies into long-lived memory.
A participant/claim model separating direct agreement, unresolved question, and hypothetical concern.
A rehearsal session surface with explicit ‘fact / inference / roleplay’ labels and a hard no-send execution boundary.
An owner-controlled retention and deletion cascade for the temporary bundle and generated transcript.
built_from: GET /mail/triage and GET /mail/triage/:runId for mail evidence
browser_read_page and GET /browser/sessions for authenticated threads and documents
GET /capture and local notes for owner-authored context
GET /journal/:jobId and GET /jobs/:jobId/receipts for prior system actions
audio_brief_item_action for private rehearsal playback control

args.user_asks: “Once a week, show me where you were wrong or overconfident, what evidence you missed, and which rule or preference should change—without quietly rewriting history.”
args.why_useful: A personal AI should earn calibrated trust, not merely produce more outputs. This gives the owner an audit of false ‘all clear’ reports, stale plans, missed deadlines, and incorrect assumptions, with concrete corrections instead of opaque self-improvement. It spans the relay's history, Mac receipts, browser outcomes, and the pendant's delivery truth.
args.model_tier: Background model clusters outcomes and proposes calibration changes; deterministic metrics calculate precision, stale-source rates, and delivery success. Realtime is unnecessary except for a spoken summary on request.
args.latency_budget: A weekly report can take 1–3 minutes; daily incremental scoring should be under 100 ms and require no model.
args.cost_estimate: Roughly $0.02–$0.10 per weekly report, mostly summarization; metrics and ledger updates are negligible.
args.security_concerns: Do not turn inferred errors into permanent facts automatically. Preserve immutable original decisions and evidence references, redact personal correspondence in the spoken summary, and require owner confirmation before changing an autonomy or disclosure policy. Reports must distinguish system error from changed external reality.
missing: An outcome ledger linking each prediction/plan/triage decision to later evidence and owner correction.
Stable cross-surface IDs and immutable decision snapshots; current job, browser, and action IDs are unrelated.
A scoring vocabulary for calibration, stale evidence, missed delivery, and policy violation, with abstention rewarded.
An owner review route that can accept, reject, or defer a proposed rule change without mutating historical records.
built_from: GET /jobs and GET /jobs/:jobId/receipts for execution outcomes
GET /journal/:jobId and GET /thinking/latest for decision context
GET /watches/reports and GET /watches/drafts for predicted page changes and follow-up outcomes
attention_arbitrate for presenting one compact weekly report

args.user_asks: “What is the one thing I should do next, and if I say ‘do it’, carry it through and tell me whether it actually worked?”
args.why_useful: Today the system can rank plans, execute actions, and report receipts, but those are disconnected. This gives the owner one outcome-oriented loop: select one evidence-backed item, act on the correct surface, verify the changed state, and close or requeue it. It prevents the wearable from celebrating a queued job as a finished life outcome.
args.model_tier: Use the cheap background model to assemble candidates and summarize evidence; use realtime only for the owner's spoken selection and clarification. Deterministic policy/preflight decides whether the selected step may ACT, PREPARE, or ASK.
args.latency_budget: Initial spoken answer under 2 seconds from cached state; execution may take up to 60 seconds, with a concise pendant update only after verified outcome or a concrete failure.
args.cost_estimate: About $0.01–$0.05 per interaction, dominated by evidence synthesis and verification; most turns should be deterministic and cached.
args.security_concerns: Never treat audio playback or a queued receipt as success. Revalidate the plan immediately before mutation, require physical consent for irreversible actions, and expose provenance for every recommendation. Browser page text and mail content stay local unless the existing redaction/origin policy allows projection.
missing: An outcome record that links one owner-selected item to its prepared plan, action receipts, and verifier result
Relay-side job leases/requeue so a Mac crash cannot strand the selected action
A small verifier vocabulary for calendar/mail/browser/file state changes
A durable relay↔Mac job identity mapping

args.user_asks: “Give me a private briefing when I am actually wearing the pendant; if it is on a desk or other people may hear, put it in the inbox instead.”
args.why_useful: The current system can decide urgency and redact some briefings, but it cannot distinguish a worn, private listening context from an unattended speaker. A physical wear/presence signal would make private audio a deliberate delivery channel instead of an assumption.
args.model_tier: No expensive model is needed for the gate. Firmware reports a signed wear/privacy state; relay attention arbitration and the existing redaction policy choose speak, queue, or suppress. Use the background model only to summarize queued items later.
args.latency_budget: Local state transition under 100 ms; relay decision under 500 ms. If the signal is unknown, fail closed to the existing inbox rather than speaking.
args.cost_estimate: Roughly $5–$15 for a capacitive/skin-contact or proximity sensor and board integration, plus negligible per-use API cost; the current single LED remains the only acknowledgement channel.
args.security_concerns: Do not infer identity or record raw proximity data. Transmit only signed states (worn/unworn/unknown, timestamp, firmware epoch). Private or secret content is never spoken when state is unknown; policy decisions must cite the state and rule that caused them.
missing: A real wear/contact sensor or equivalent firmware signal; none is present on the current board
A relay contract carrying signed privacy-state epochs
A single delivery policy joining wear state, focus/idle state, sensitivity, and attention_arbitrate
A way to surface a queued private item without leaking its title on the LED or public Mac

args.user_asks: “If my Mac or browser dies halfway through something, pick it up safely when it comes back—without repeating a step or pretending it finished.”
args.why_useful: An in-flight job currently can remain stuck in processing for up to a day, and the owner has no honest distinction between prepared, partially applied, and verified. This would make the hive resilient in the way a wearable should be: the conversation can disappear, but the intention and safe next step survive.
args.model_tier: Use deterministic lease/recovery and idempotency logic first. Invoke a cheaper background model only to reconstruct a human-readable resume summary from the context handoff; realtime is needed only when the owner asks what happened.
args.latency_budget: Recovery scan every 30–60 seconds; reconnect status in under 2 seconds; no automatic replay of an uncertain mutation. Ask the owner only when state cannot be proven safe.
args.cost_estimate: Negligible API cost for the lease and receipt path; approximately $0.005–$0.02 only when a resume summary must be generated.
args.security_concerns: Fail closed on stale or ambiguous plans. Revalidate source state and policy before resuming, use action-level idempotency keys, and never retry destructive/external actions automatically. Show the owner the last verified step and the exact reason for asking.
missing: relay_jobs lease_until, expiry sweep, and bounded reclaim policy
A durable relay-job↔Mac-job mapping rather than telemetry-only localJobId
Step-level outcome/checkpoint records covering browser commands as well as Mac actions
A resume endpoint that consumes contextHandoff plus revalidate_pending_plan and returns a safe next step

transcript.text:
Round 262 produced three distinct capabilities:

1. **Closed-loop “one next thing” execution** — the most useful capability  
   The owner asks what matters most, selects it, and receives a verified outcome—not merely a queued job or optimistic receipt. It combines reconciliation, policy evaluation, plan revalidation, Mac/browser execution, provenance, and pendant item controls.

2. **Private briefing based on actual wear state**  
   Add a signed worn/unworn/unknown signal from a small contact or proximity sensor. Private content speaks only when the pendant is demonstrably worn; otherwise it enters the existing inbox. Unknown must fail closed. This requires hardware because the current pendant has no wear sensor.

3. **Safe recovery of interrupted work**  
   If the Mac or browser dies mid-task, recover from the last verified step without repeating mutations or claiming completion. This needs relay job leases, durable relay↔Mac job identity, step outcomes, and resume logic built on existing context handoff and idempotency primitives.

What is still needed:

- **Owner decisions:** authoritative personal timezone versus Mac routine timezone; quiet-hour and urgency policy; which content classes may be spoken aloud; trusted external destinations.
- **Shipping connectivity:** LTE-M registration and a tested reconnect path. USB remains bench-only, not a product transport.
- **Firmware/hardware:** a real wear sensor for private audio gating; the already-accepted stop latch, delivery ACK queue, and privacy panic wipe still need integration and field verification.
- **Durability work:** relay job leases/requeue, approval persistence, fleet-memory writers, and cross-surface job-ID mapping. These are not merely refactors: without them, the system cannot honestly resume or verify owner work.

args.user_asks: “When your sources disagree, show me the two plausible interpretations and what each would cause before you choose or do anything.”
args.why_useful: A trustworthy assistant should not collapse contradictory timezone, permission, calendar, browser, or goal evidence into one confident answer. The owner would see the disagreement, the consequence of each branch, and the smallest decision needed to resolve it—without any side effect occurring first.
args.model_tier: Use deterministic conflict detection and consequence extraction first; use the background model to phrase the two branches. Realtime is used only to ask the final concise question and record the owner's choice.
args.latency_budget: Under 3 seconds for a cached conflict; up to 10 seconds when fresh Mac/browser reads are required. No mutation until the branch is explicitly selected.
args.cost_estimate: Approximately $0.01–$0.04 per conflict, mostly for branch explanation; source comparison and policy checks are deterministic.
args.security_concerns: Branch previews must be read-only and redact sensitive snippets. Every claim needs source IDs and freshness. A branch must never be executable merely because it was displayed; the selected branch must pass preflight and autonomy policy again.
missing: A typed counterfactual/branch result joining conflict evidence to predicted consequences
Read-only consequence previews for the actual action types available on Mac and browser
A durable owner choice that records which assumption was accepted and when

args.user_asks: “Before I change how you behave, let me try the rule on recent real situations and see exactly what you would have spoken, queued, or blocked.”
args.why_useful: Interruption and disclosure policies are currently either placeholders or scattered enforcement decisions. The owner needs to calibrate them safely against representative history before trusting the pendant in public or during focused work. A simulation mode turns hidden policy consequences into an inspectable, reversible choice.
args.model_tier: Replay stored event metadata with deterministic policy evaluation; use a cheaper background model only to summarize patterns. Realtime is unnecessary except for the owner's final confirmation of a chosen policy.
args.latency_budget: 5–15 seconds for a 24-hour replay; longer historical windows may run asynchronously and leave a reviewable report. Simulation must never emit audio or mutate external state.
args.cost_estimate: Approximately $0.005–$0.03 per simulation; dominated by summarization, not evaluation.
args.security_concerns: Replay event metadata and sensitivity labels by default, not raw mail/page text. Make clear that simulated outcomes are not actual deliveries. Policy edits require explicit confirmation and retain a versioned before/after explanation.
missing: A policy simulation endpoint that replays attention, disclosure, and autonomy decisions against historical event metadata
Stable event fixtures linking triage findings, browser watches, audio items, and delivery outcomes
A versioned policy store with rollback and owner-readable rule explanations

transcript.text:
Recorded two capabilities:

- **Counterfactual disagreement previews:** when sources conflict, show the owner each plausible interpretation and its consequences before taking action.
- **Policy simulation:** replay recent event metadata to show what a proposed interruption, disclosure, or autonomy policy would have spoken, queued, or blocked—without producing side effects—before the owner adopts it.

args.user_asks: Run my morning brief once, and don't tell me it happened until the pendant confirms it actually started playing; if delivery fails, recover it or tell me plainly.
args.why_useful: The owner currently has two 07:00-ish morning routines plus a 07:30 routine, and server completion is not proof that anything reached or was heard by the pendant. This turns a scheduled promise into a truthful, deduplicated user-visible result.
args.model_tier: background for gathering and ranking; realtime only for the short spoken status
args.latency_budget: Schedule launch under 2 seconds; recovery on reconnect within one routine tick; spoken status under 3 seconds after an ACK or terminal failure.
args.cost_estimate: Low: one background model call per brief (often already incurred); dominant cost is TTS/audio generation, not judgement.
args.security_concerns: Only opaque artifact IDs and delivery states cross the relay; briefing text remains subject to existing redaction. Never claim heard from generated/accepted alone. Any retry must be idempotent and stop after expiry.
missing: relay_jobs lease_until plus requeue sweep for orphaned jobs
routine-level dedupe key spanning the two 07:00 routines
wire record_pendant_delivery_event into the actual pendant ACK upload path
a small delivery-aware routine coordinator that maps routine/job/artifact IDs

args.user_asks: When I come back, give me one honest 'what changed while I was away' card: unfinished work, new browser changes, messages that need me, and exactly what the pendant did or failed to play.
args.why_useful: Today catchup can read jobs and browser spool, but pendant-originated items are effectively always empty and server-side completion is conflated with delivery. A reconnect digest should reduce several silent queues to one actionable account, without pretending unreadable sources were clear.
args.model_tier: Background model for compression and ranking; realtime only to answer a follow-up question about one item.
args.latency_budget: Produce within 5 seconds of reconnect or explicit request; never block link recovery on model generation. If a source is unavailable, say so in the card.
args.cost_estimate: Low-to-moderate: one short synthesis call per reconnect, dominated by context size; use deterministic filtering before model invocation.
args.security_concerns: Source-linked snippets are redacted before speech; private/secret items become titles or counts unless the owner explicitly opens them. Include provenance and freshness per item, and dedupe replayed ACKs.
missing: feed authenticated pendant delivery events and interrupted playback into catchupDigest
a durable relay-job-to-Mac-job correlation key rather than telemetry-only localJobId
source health/readability flags for calendar/reminders so empty is never rendered as all-clear
a single cross-surface catchup endpoint that merges jobs, browser reports, briefings, and delivery receipts

args.user_asks: Before you act across my Mac and browser, tell me in one sentence what you can actually read, what you can draft, what needs my physical approval, and what will remain untouched; then carry out only the allowed part.
args.why_useful: The owner should not have to learn which body is online or discover after the fact that a browser session was stale, a permission was fake, or an action crossed from reversible draft into external side effect. This is the single most useful trust feature: truthful reachability plus bounded execution, not another clever answer.
args.model_tier: Deterministic policy/preflight first; cheap background model only to phrase the result; realtime model only for ambiguity in the owner's request.
args.latency_budget: Preflight under 500 ms when surfaces are healthy; one spoken sentence before mutation; no mutation if any required target is unavailable or stale.
args.cost_estimate: Very low model cost because cross_surface_preflight and autonomy_policy_evaluate are deterministic; occasional model phrasing is the only variable cost.
args.security_concerns: Fail closed on missing scopes, stale plans, unknown sensitivity, or changed evidence. Physical approval remains required for irreversible/external actions; never expose secrets in the spoken preflight. Every decision names the matched policy and evidence refs.
missing: one orchestrator that composes cross_surface_preflight, autonomy_policy_evaluate, and revalidate_pending_plan before POST /execute
a typed result that distinguishes read/draft/mutate/destructive per target and carries freshness/provenance
enforcement hooks so Mac/browser executors cannot bypass the arbiter
durable approval decision handoff between relay and Mac

transcript.summary: This round produced three owner-facing capabilities: (1) a delivery-truthful, deduplicated morning brief that does not claim success until pendant playback is acknowledged; (2) a reconnect digest that says what changed, what remains, and what actually played; and (3) a single preflight sentence plus fail-closed execution boundary across relay, Mac, browser, and pendant. The third is the most valuable trust feature: the owner gets truthful reachability and bounded action instead of discovering surface limitations after the fact. I still need implementation of relay job leases/requeue, routine deduplication, real pendant ACK ingestion, cross-body job correlation, and enforcement hooks so executors cannot bypass policy. Owner preference decisions remain intentionally open: exact quiet hours, emergency categories, and which content may be spoken aloud or leave the machine.
transcript.biggest_unknown: Whether the owner wants the two overlapping 07:00 morning routines merged, disabled, or assigned different briefs; the current state proves duplication but not the intended replacement.

args.user_asks: Forget everything you learned from this site, person, or conversation everywhere—and show me a receipt proving which Mac, browser, relay, graph, memory, audio, and pendant copies were removed or made unusable. Do not silently keep a derived summary.
args.why_useful: The owner cannot honestly revoke a source today: deleting a capture leaves a context-graph copy, evidence revocation does not reach derived facts, capsules retain tombstones, and there is no global forget operation. A source-wide erasure receipt is a felt safety boundary, not another explanation screen.
args.model_tier: Deterministic provenance traversal and deletion first; background model only to identify ambiguous derived records for owner review. Never use the expensive realtime tier for the deletion itself.
args.latency_budget: Return a complete inventory quickly (under 2 seconds for local indexes); execute deletion asynchronously with durable progress and a final receipt. Any unresolved copy must be reported, not marked deleted.
args.cost_estimate: Low model cost; the dominant cost is bounded local/relay storage traversal and, where applicable, regenerated artifact invalidation.
args.security_concerns: Require explicit confirmation because erasure is destructive. Never put the erased content in the spoken confirmation. Use source IDs and hashes, not snippets, in receipts; revoke future prompt eligibility before deletion begins; fail closed if a surface cannot be reached, and prevent stale queued audio or browser commands from replaying erased material.
missing: a provenance foreign key from memory facts and context-graph entities to evidence capsules/source IDs
a cross-store forget coordinator covering facts, graph, captures, capsules, browser provenance, jobs, audio artifacts, relay memory, and pendant inbox/outbox
relay-side tombstone/revocation propagation with durable retry and expiry
a queryable erasure receipt listing deleted, revoked, unreachable, and not-found records
executor and prompt guards that reject revoked source IDs even when a raw copy is already in a pending job

args.change: Add a mandatory claim-verification pass for every owner-facing spoken result that contains a concrete assertion: extract each claim, attach its source and freshness, classify it as observed/inferred/unverified, and block or qualify any claim lacking a current receipt. Use a cheap deterministic checker first and a background model only for ambiguous synthesis; realtime generation may not bypass the verifier.
args.why_useful_to_owner: The owner gets fewer confident falsehoods—especially about calendar, permissions, device state, and whether an action happened—and can hear a short honest qualification instead of a polished fabrication. This is different from an action receipt: it verifies the words about the world before they leave the speaker.
args.effort: Medium: define a claim envelope, instrument Mac/relay/browser result producers, add a verifier middleware before TTS, and create regression cases for empty-calendar permission failures and stale job results.
args.risk: Over-qualification could make speech tedious or suppress useful answers. Recover by limiting it to externally checkable claims, speaking only a compact uncertainty label, and retaining the full evidence view on the dashboard. If the verifier is unavailable, fail closed for high-impact claims and allow clearly labeled low-stakes summaries.
args.cost_impact: Small background-model cost only for ambiguous claim matching; deterministic extraction and receipt lookup dominate. No new hardware cost.
args.latency_impact: Typically 50–300 ms for deterministic checks; up to a few seconds for ambiguous multi-source synthesis, with a short 'checking' state rather than silent delay.
args.security_impact: Improves safety by preventing stale or unsupported private content from being spoken; claim envelopes must carry sensitivity and source IDs, and the verifier must never echo withheld snippets into logs.
depends_on: Wire GET /jobs/:jobId/receipts, GET /journal/:jobId, machine-context, browser status, and delivery ACKs into a common claim envelope
Fix the known unauthorised-calendar empty-result ambiguity before treating calendar absence as evidence
Ensure pendantSpeech and audioBrief pass through the verifier/redaction boundary rather than speaking raw result.message

result.note: Noted. Keep going, including layers you have not touched yet.

args.user_asks: “Make sure I actually receive my morning brief. If the pendant did not download or play it, recover it on the Mac or queue it for my next interaction, and tell me only once what was missed.”
args.why_useful: Today generation/acceptance is mistaken for delivery. This would make scheduled briefings dependable across relay, Mac, and pendant rather than silently lost after a dropped link or playback failure.
args.model_tier: Background model for delivery classification and concise fallback; realtime only when the owner asks what was missed.
args.latency_budget: No added spoken latency when delivery succeeds. Recovery should begin within one scheduler tick; fallback status under 2 seconds when asked.
args.cost_estimate: Low: one event reconciliation and usually no model call; dominant cost is optional fallback synthesis only when the original artifact was not played.
args.security_concerns: Use opaque artifact IDs and authenticated device-session ACKs, never raw audio in the delivery ledger. Do not replay private content aloud automatically; attention_arbitrate and the owner's policy choose pendant versus Mac display. Confirmation is required before any external resend or side effect.
missing: A durable delivery-aware scheduler that joins relay jobs to artifact IDs and ACKs
A Mac fallback renderer that marks an item delivered only after display or playback confirmation
Relay job leases/requeue so a failed producer cannot remain processing forever

args.user_asks: “Forget everything this website or source taught you—quotes, derived facts, graph links, and fleet copies—and show me what was removed and what could not be reached.”
args.why_useful: The current system can revoke an evidence capsule while derived facts and context-graph copies survive indefinitely. A real source-level forget operation would let the owner revoke a source rather than merely hide one capture.
args.model_tier: Background deterministic traversal; no expensive model required except an optional owner-readable summary.
args.latency_budget: Preview under 2 seconds for local stores; apply asynchronously with a visible receipt and completion state.
args.cost_estimate: Low API cost; storage traversal and durable tombstones dominate. No third-party call unless the owner explicitly asks for remote deletion.
args.security_concerns: Fail closed when provenance links are absent: report unreachable copies instead of claiming deletion. Require explicit confirmation for apply, preserve minimal tombstones/audit IDs, redact secret snippets from the spoken result, and propagate retractions to relay/fleet only through authenticated scopes.
missing: A capsuleId/source link on memory facts and context-graph entities
A durable cross-store deletion/retraction transaction with an unreachable-copy report
A production writer for fleet-memory retractions and the fleet-memory schema migration

args.user_asks: “When my Mac or connection dies during a task, recover it safely: tell me exactly what completed, re-check anything that changed, and continue only reversible steps without duplicating an action.”
args.why_useful: An in-flight relay job currently has no lease and can remain processing forever after a crash. The owner gets neither reliable continuation nor a trustworthy boundary between completed and merely planned work.
args.model_tier: Deterministic recovery and policy evaluation first; background model only to summarize the recovery receipt.
args.latency_budget: Detect orphaned work within one lease sweep; recovery decision under 1 second, with owner-facing explanation available immediately.
args.cost_estimate: Very low: state reads and idempotency checks dominate; model is optional.
args.security_concerns: Never replay an irreversible or externally visible action automatically. Revalidate source state, require physical consent for staged actions, honor the universal stop latch, and expose every skipped step with provenance. Browser commands must retain their existing lease/idempotency protections.
missing: lease_until and requeue sweep for relay_jobs
A durable relay-job↔Mac-job mapping rather than telemetry-only localJobId
A recovery record that joins receipts, action-ledger idempotency keys, and revalidation results

args.user_asks: “Is my pendant healthy right now? Run a safe end-to-end check of radio/link, audio quality, queue backlog, and last playback, then tell me the one thing I should fix—or say it is healthy.”
args.why_useful: The owner currently has isolated diagnostics and job receipts, not a truthful end-to-end health verdict. This would catch the practical failures they feel—missing audio, stale queues, checksum errors, or a dead relay path—without making them interpret UART metrics.
args.model_tier: Deterministic probes and thresholds first; a cheap background model may turn evidence into one short spoken sentence. Realtime is unnecessary.
args.latency_budget: Local checks in under 5 seconds; remote checks may take 15 seconds and return a staged result if the pendant is offline.
args.cost_estimate: Low API cost; device probe and metric aggregation dominate. No model call for normal/healthy results.
args.security_concerns: Read-only by default. Do not expose auth material or raw microphone/audio; return counters, opaque IDs, and redacted reasons. Any firmware update, queue purge, or repair requires explicit confirmation and physical stop-latch state must win.
missing: A typed aggregate health endpoint joining authenticated device telemetry, delivery ACKs, and Mac/relay reachability
A safe active audio loopback/test artifact with an owner-confirmed playback boundary
Threshold/version metadata so a health verdict is explainable and comparable over time

transcript.text:
Proposed three capabilities:

1. **Self-healing briefing delivery** — use authenticated pendant download/playback ACKs to detect missed briefings, retry or fall back to the Mac, and avoid repeating items already heard.
2. **Source-level forgetting** — rejected as a duplicate by the recorder, confirming this is already represented in the backlog. The underlying gap remains: revoking evidence does not remove derived facts or graph copies.
3. **Crash-safe task recovery** — recover interrupted Mac/relay tasks using leases, receipts, idempotency keys, revalidation, and autonomy policy, without repeating completed actions.
4. **End-to-end pendant health check** — a read-only owner-facing verdict joining UART/audio diagnostics, delivery ACKs, relay reachability, pipeline state, and Mac connectivity.

What I still need is not another tool request. To make policy-sensitive behavior truthful, the system still needs the owner to decide:

- whether notification content may ever be spoken aloud;
- which destinations are trusted for sensitive data;
- whether the Mac’s `America/New_York` zone should be treated as the owner’s actual timezone, rather than merely the machine’s routine timezone.

The owner’s interruption and disclosure preferences remain intentionally unset; conservative defaults must stay explicit and overridable rather than being treated as facts.

args.user_asks: “When someone else is close enough to hear me, keep private details private: automatically switch to a neutral spoken response or route the detail to my screen, then restore normal speech when I’m alone.”
args.why_useful: A pendant that speaks calendar, mail, browser, or memory content cannot know whether a bystander is present today. Timing suppression is not confidentiality. This gives the owner a practical physical-world privacy boundary instead of requiring them to remember to say ‘don’t say that’ every time.
args.model_tier: Fast local classifier for acoustic/proximity state; deterministic policy evaluation for content routing. Use the expensive realtime model only to answer the owner, never to infer privacy from raw audio unnecessarily.
args.latency_budget: Privacy decision before any sensitive utterance starts, under 100 ms locally. State changes may be debounced for 2–3 seconds to avoid flapping.
args.cost_estimate: Moderate hardware cost and low per-use API cost. The dominant cost is a second microphone or short-range proximity sensor and its always-on power budget; raw room audio should not leave the pendant.
args.security_concerns: Fail closed: unknown presence means no sensitive speech. Never upload room audio or retain bystander features. The relay signs only a coarse state (`private`/`public`/`unknown`), and the owner can override it with a physical control. Sensitive content remains on the Mac/display unless policy explicitly permits speech.
missing: A bystander/proximity sensor or microphone arrangement with local directional/voice-activity classification
A firmware privacy-state machine that can gate playback before PCM reaches the bridge
A signed, expiring presence state consumed by pendant speech, relay attention arbitration, Mac display routing, and browser-derived sensitivity policy
An owner-configurable rule table for which classes may be spoken in public

args.user_asks: “Forget everything you learned from this site, person, or project—and show me what was removed.”
args.why_useful: Today revoking an evidence capsule leaves derived facts and context-graph copies readable forever. A source-scoped erasure command would make privacy promises real: identify every capsule, fact, graph entity, briefing draft, and fleet-memory event descended from the source; tombstone or delete each; then return a receipt listing survivors and any unlinked copies that require review.
args.model_tier: background for provenance traversal and reconciliation; realtime only for the short confirmation and result
args.latency_budget: Under 5 seconds for the inventory; deletion may continue in the background, with a durable completion receipt
args.cost_estimate: Roughly $0.01–$0.05 per invocation; dominated by one background provenance/reconciliation pass, not TTS
args.security_concerns: Default to dry-run and require explicit confirmation for deletion. Never speak source text or secrets. A failed cascade must report partial completion rather than claim erasure. The owner must be able to revoke by origin, capsule, fact, or project key.
missing: fact records need capsule/source linkage
context-graph and fleet-memory writers need tombstone propagation
a durable cascade worker and completion receipt
an owner-confirmed erase endpoint spanning Mac and relay stores

args.user_asks: “What did I miss while the pendant or Mac was offline? Tell me what was generated, what actually reached the device, and what still needs my attention.”
args.why_useful: The system can generate briefings and jobs while delivery is uncertain, but today catch-up has no real pendant-item input and receipts stop before authenticated download/playback. This would reconcile relay jobs, audio artifacts, pendant delivery ACKs, browser spool, and local receipts into one honest offline-gap report—separating never generated, generated but undelivered, downloaded but unheard, and completed.
args.model_tier: background deterministic reconciliation; realtime only to answer the spoken question and optionally play one selected item
args.latency_budget: 2–4 seconds when receipts are present; stale or missing surfaces should return an explicit partial report

args.latency_impact: Adds no startup latency; recovery occurs on the next sweep, typically within one scheduler interval.

args.user_asks: “Make sure my morning brief actually reaches me. If I didn’t hear it, give me the missed version—not a duplicate—and tell me exactly what was delivered.”
args.why_useful: Today a routine can be marked completed when the relay/Mac generated audio, even if the pendant never downloaded or played it; duplicate 07:00 routines can also produce competing briefs. Delivery ACKs let the system distinguish generated, downloaded, started, finished, interrupted, checksum-failed, and no-audio, then recover with one concise replay. This is the single most useful daily capability: a briefing is not complete until the owner actually received it.
args.model_tier: Cheap background model deduplicates and compresses brief items; deterministic policy handles ACK state and retry; realtime model is used only when the owner asks for a spoken catch-up or clarification.
args.latency_budget: No added latency to generation. ACK reconciliation runs within 30 seconds of an event; a missed-brief alert is queued on reconnect and should be audible on the next deliberate play press.
args.cost_estimate: Near-zero incremental model cost for ACK/state transitions; roughly one short background summarization call only when a replay must be compressed. Storage is small event metadata per artifact.
args.security_concerns: Store opaque artifact IDs, hashes, timestamps, and playback positions—not raw audio in the relay event. Do not replay private content automatically while the owner may be in public; route through the owner’s configured speak policy and attention arbiter. A checksum error or ambiguous ACK must produce a reviewable 'not confirmed' state, never claim success.
missing: Wire record_pendant_delivery_event into the briefing/routine completion path and make event IDs idempotent end to end.
A durable mapping from routine/briefing item to artifact ID and a dedupe key across the duplicate 07:00 routines.
A delivery-aware replay scheduler that feeds attention_arbitrate and expires stale items.
A fix for relay job leases so a failed reconciliation cannot strand the source job.

args.user_asks: “The Mac died or the browser disconnected halfway through that task. Recover it safely, show me what is still pending, and never repeat an external action just because the connection dropped.”
args.why_useful: An in-flight job currently has no lease and can remain processing for up to 24 hours; relay and Mac IDs are not joinable, and a reconnect has no trustworthy checkpoint. The owner needs a recovery experience, not a dead job record: identify the exact step, revalidate current browser/Mac state, cancel stale work, and present only reversible or physically confirmed next steps.
args.model_tier: Deterministic lease/revalidation/policy machinery first; a cheap model summarizes the recovery packet. Realtime is used only if the owner asks what happened.
args.latency_budget: Detect an orphan within 1 minute; produce a recovery packet within 3 seconds after a surface reconnects. No automatic mutation during recovery.
args.cost_estimate: Negligible model cost for ordinary recovery; one short summary call for complex multi-step jobs. Main cost is durable metadata: one checkpoint and join record per active job.
args.security_concerns: Fail closed when the checkpoint is missing, stale, or sensitive. Revalidate before any retry; never replay a mutation from a pre-crash plan. Require the existing physical transaction approval latch for irreversible actions. Explanations must link evidence, plan, and effect, with secrets excluded.

Persist relay-job-id ↔ Mac-job-id ↔ browser-command-id and the current step/checkpoint.
Have the Mac write a durable checkpoint before and after every action, including whether an external side effect was committed.
A recovery packet route/UI that invokes revalidate_pending_plan, cross_surface_preflight, autonomy_policy_evaluate, and explain_action_provenance without executing.

args.user_asks: “Before I commit to this, show me the consequences if I say yes, no, or later—across my real calendar, inbox, browser commitments, and current work—without changing anything.”
args.why_useful: The owner can preview individual Mac actions, but cannot rehearse a consequential choice across all surfaces as competing futures. A counterfactual rehearsal would expose collisions, hidden follow-up work, deadlines, and irreversible effects before the owner commits, turning the pendant from an executor into a decision instrument.
args.model_tier: A cheap planning model builds candidate futures from read-only evidence; deterministic evaluators calculate conflicts, policy violations, and reversibility. Realtime is used only to explain the chosen branch conversationally.
args.latency_budget: Under 8 seconds for a normal branch comparison; no writes during rehearsal. The owner can request a deeper branch only after seeing the compact result.
args.cost_estimate: One small planning call per rehearsal, with bounded evidence excerpts; most conflict and policy checks are deterministic. No external API spend unless the branch explicitly includes research.
args.security_concerns: Rehearsal must be read-only and clearly labeled hypothetical. Never send, buy, delete, or alter calendar state while simulating. Sensitive snippets remain local or redacted; every predicted consequence carries evidence and a confidence level. A later real action must revalidate because the world may have changed.

Read adapters for all participating surfaces, including a truthful calendar/reminder permission result rather than empty success.
A consequence engine that maps one proposed commitment to downstream browser, mail, calendar, and local-job effects.

args.user_asks: “When I ask what I know about a person, project, or place, give me the living view: what is established, what is merely inferred, what has gone stale, and what evidence would change my mind.”
args.why_useful: Current memory can answer from accumulated facts, but it cannot present a calibrated, time-aware belief with supporting and contradicting evidence as one owner-facing object. This would prevent old assumptions from masquerading as current truth and make the AI useful for real decisions without pretending certainty.
args.model_tier: Deterministic projection computes freshness, source status, sensitivity, and contradictions; a cheap model compresses the belief map into a short spoken answer. Realtime is reserved for follow-up reasoning.
args.latency_budget: Under 5 seconds for a normal topic; evidence expansion is on demand. Spoken output defaults to one sentence with an option to hear the evidence chain.
args.cost_estimate: Usually no model call for projection; one short synthesis call when multiple contradictory sources need language. Storage is bounded by summaries and source references, not raw quotations.
args.security_concerns: Do not expose private evidence by default in audio. Distinguish observed, owner-asserted, and model-inferred claims. A source revocation must immediately remove its claims from the projection, and stale claims must never authorize an external action without fresh confirmation.

args.model_tier: Background model for collection and ranking; realtime model only for the owner's follow-up question or a one-sentence spoken rendering.
args.latency_budget: Prepare in under 10 seconds when sources are online; speak in under 3 seconds once the owner asks. If a source is offline, return a partial result with provenance rather than waiting indefinitely.
args.cost_estimate: Roughly one background model call per digest (about $0.01–$0.05 depending on source volume); realtime cost only for follow-up. Dominant cost is summarizing changed source material, not arbitration.
args.security_concerns: Never speak raw mail/browser text unless the delivery policy permits it; route all outgoing text through the existing redaction boundary. Calendar/reminder emptiness must be marked unreadable unless the corroborating permission-aware readers agree. External actions remain drafts or require physical approval. The owner must be able to inspect evidence and revoke a source.

A durable cross-surface correlation between relay jobs and Mac/browser jobs; today localJobId is telemetry only.

A user-configurable policy object for what may be spoken, rather than relying on placeholder interruption thresholds.

args.security_concerns: The scenario text and affected-person names may be sensitive. Recorded three new capabilities:

1. **Counterfactual commitment simulator** — preview the personal consequences of saying yes before changing anything.
2. **Seamless modality handoff** — move a conversation between pendant, Mac, and browser without losing context or evidence.

Each requires durable cross-surface correlation, provenance-aware context transfer, and explicit privacy/confirmation policies that do not exist today.

args.latency_impact: Normal jobs gain one conditional claim update; reconnect recovery becomes bounded by the sweep interval instead of a 24-hour TTL.
args.security_impact: Improves auditability. Lease tokens must be unguessable and never authorize a different job; receipts remain the source of truth for already-applied effects.

transcript.text:
Recorded three capabilities:

1. **Coverage-aware answers** — “nothing is waiting” would include what was checked, what was unreadable, stale, offline, or not requested.
2. **High-value clarification queue** — group only ambiguity likely to prevent repeated mistakes, ask at a suitable time, and propagate the answer across surfaces.
3. **Cross-surface correction loop** — when the owner says “that’s wrong,” identify the claim and evidence, retract dependent copies, prevent future actions from using it, and request only the necessary replacement fact.

Each requires new durable cross-surface records and provenance/retraction wiring that does not exist today.

args.body: I’m pursuing: (1) a pre-consequence decision rehearsal that gathers evidence and tests owner policy before external effects; (2) a ‘why am I doing this now?’ intent check-in that turns detected context drift into one spoken clarification and a reversible plan; (3) a cross-surface absence detector for things the owner expected but no surface delivered, with honest escalation.
